Root cause of five production defects: js/monsters.js never exported AD_STON, AD_DRLI, AD_DRDX, AD_DRCO, AD_WERE, AT_EXPL, AD_DISN, or AD_DCAY, so the new mondata.c ports compared a numeric adtyp against undefined and those branches could never fire; mstrength() was wrong for 13 species and max_passive_dmg()'s AD_DCAY instakill arm was dead. gender() returned the port's JavaScript boolean where C returns an int used to index pmnames[]. raceptr() passed the whole game state to Upolyd(), which reads the hero's mtimedone, so a polymorphed hero received the racial species. locomotion() duplicated the locoverbs words inline and collapsed C's flys and flyl rows; it now shares locoverb() with stagger(), which exposed an incomplete species fixture missing msize in scripts/startup-a11y.test.mjs. Tests now pin mstrength against the difficulty stored in every monsters.h entry, which would have caught all eight missing constants at once, and guard that every M.* name js/mondata.js reads is a number. Post-fix validation passed all 1625 tests, npm run check:monsters, and the development suite at 98270 RNG values, 241 screens, and 256 cursors with zero sessions differing. No holdout access.

rejections.summary: The comment above the moves >= 1e9 stop was said to claim a dismissal the slice never performs.
rejections.counterEvidence: js/allmain.js executes dismissPendingTtyMessage() before elapsedTurnBoundary() whenever that line is reached with planning false, so the comment describes its own site accurately and makes no reachability claim. The live do/while can call finishElapsedTurn more than once per advanceElapsedTurn, so the site is a live guard rather than dead by construction, and the range's game-end test pins the burdened dry run where planning is true and the dismissal is deliberately skipped. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: projected_capacity() was said to duplicate inv_weight()/calc_capacity() arithmetic that can silently drift, justified by a cache hazard no reader can experience.
rejections.counterEvidence: Both paths reduce to capacity_from_excess(inventory_weight(state) - weight_cap(state), weight_cap(state)) and share all three helpers, so no divergence is possible without editing one both call. The gw.wc write the comment avoids is observable: the retry snapshot covers gw and cmd.test.mjs asserts game.gw.wc equality across retries, so calling near_capacity() in the admission pass would fail those tests. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: blocksMove() reads loc.doormask while level generation writes loc.flags, so its closed-door arm is dead on every generated door.
rejections.counterEvidence: The reading is correct but neither blocksMove() nor doorMask() is changed by this range, and the dead arm is protective: requireSimpleHeroDestination() refuses closed, locked, and trapped masks through doorMask() itself. Both proposed repairs create new defects. Renaming the generated field is wrong for the C union, where include/rm.h overloads the same flags bitfield as doormask, altarmask, wall_info, ladder, drawbridgemask, and looted. Routing a closed door into domove()'s blocked branch produces a silent zero-time stop where C prints 'That door is closed.', because the ported test_move() returns true for a non-STONE, non-wall square. Reopen only with a ported closed-door owner to attach it to.

The generated CMAP_EXPLANATIONS entry for S_web held "',  S_web, " because the extractor scanned the whole entry for its last quoted string and that entry's character literal is a double quote.
objnam.c just_an() was ported twice in js/objnam.js.
vtense()'s es and s branches appended lowercase literals where C writes them through Strcasecpy(), dropping case propagation.
dfeature_at() read the door mask as doormask||flags, reversing the precedence every other reader in the port uses.
js/hack.js passed a literal 0 for look_here()'s obj_cnt where pickup.c check_here() passes the counted objects, which pile_limit is compared against.
display_pickinv() formatted names one at a time, and formatting marks a type discovered, so a pack whose later item could not be named left the earlier ones discovered and still refused the command.
88e2193 added test_move()'s diagonal-out-of-an-intact-doorway refusal to the destination seam only, so a hero on an open doorway swapped diagonally with the pet and elapsed a turn C refuses.

UnsupportedMonsterCreationError is converted only on the cloned planning round, so for an unencumbered hero the live maybe_generate_rnd_mon() refusal escapes runSegment() rather than ending the segment at a boundary. Verified pre-existing: the identical probe at the parent produces identical output. The fix must be a preflight, because a live conversion is not atomic.

rejections.summary: The displ argument added to tin_variety() has no test distinguishing displ=true from displ=false.

rejections.summary: The new test_move() ust rule (refuse a diagonal step out of a doorway that still has its door) was added only to requireSimpleHeroDestination(); requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap() still admits the same move, so a diagonal pet swap out of an open doorway succeeds where C refuses.

Counter-evidence: `git show 4fc57d80:js/hack.js` shows requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap() with an identical source-square check and no diagonal rule, and `doorway = location?.typ === DOOR && !(doorMask(location) & (D_CLOSED | D_LOCKED | D_TRAPPED))` already admitting D_ISOPEN as a destination. The pet-swap probe run against the parent tree returned the same swaps as at 03c2add for seeds 777, 5150, 840004, 31009 and 1234 (e.g. `31009 RETURNED hero [ 63

rejections.summary: The tests for stopStepIndex and ceilingFor restate the one-line implementations (identity and subtraction), and the seed8000-tourist-starter census cited as their independent anchor is false at this range's HEAD, so the stop-attribution convention has no working oracle.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The finding's central factual claim is false at the reviewed commit, and the assertions it calls tautological do in fact pin the convention. Counter-evidence: I ran `node scripts/scan-stops.mjs --json` in a tree exported at 03c2add (the range's HEAD). The seed8000-tourist-starter row is `{'screensEmitted': 11, 'recordedSteps': 23, 'key': 'i', 'command': 'inventory', ...}` — exactly the numbers the comments state ('11 is seed8000-tourist-starter's emitted count, where step 11 is the "i" the repeated-command boundary refuses' and '23 recorded steps, 11 emitted screens'), and ceilingFor({23, 11}) = 12 as asserted. The 13-emitted/'+'/showspells figures come from the current work

head: 60bf2c3cf1fc8d7313970a91417547af466206c3
evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the no-time-command goal: dodiscovered(), dospellmenu(), doattributes() and enlightenment(), plus weapon_descr()'s move into js/weapon.js. Four finders ran (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency were not enabled, because the range adds no hot-path work and no new shared mutable state. 17 raw findings, 16 after deduplication, 14 confirmed and all 14 applied across 7d11c53 and 2adc5af; 2 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. The four production defects were Fixed_abil read as intrinsic-or-extrinsic, a stop on every wielded towel rather than a wet one, a deafness guard that missed u.uroleplay.deaf, and can_advance() refusing on speedy ahead of the three tests C answers FALSE from. Validation at 2adc5af: 1,765 tests passing, four generated-data checks, check:namespace-members, development score unchanged at 98,759 PRNG values and 286 screens and cursors with no session regressed, and the no-time matrix matching 71,967 calls with 158 screens and cursors across 29 segments.

productionDefects.summary: one_characteristic() tested Fixed_abil through hasProperty(), which ORs the intrinsic and the extrinsic. youprop.h:385 defines the macro as the extrinsic alone, with no HFixed_abil term, so an intrinsic in that slot stopped the command where C prints the six characteristics.

weapon_insight() refused every wielded towel, but obj.h defines is_wet_towel(o) as otyp == TOWEL && spe > 0 and weapon.c lists TOWEL among weapon_descr()'s P_NONE overrides, so a dry towel prints "You are wielding a towel."

The deafness guard read u.uprops[DEAF] only, but youprop.h:245 defines Deaf as (HDeaf || EDeaf || u.uroleplay.deaf). OPTIONS=deaf sets the third term alone, so the port printed a window where C prints " You are deaf."

can_advance() refused on speedy before evaluating the three tests C answers FALSE from, so a restricted or maxed skill ended the segment instead of answering FALSE. C's shortcut is wizard && speedy and sits after those tests.

rejections.summary: status_enlightenment() accepts mode and never reads it, said to hide that C's `boolean magic = (mode & MAGICENLIGHTENMENT)` gate on the Fumbling, Sleepy and Hunger arms was replaced by unconditional stops.
rejections.counterEvidence: insight.c:728 declares basics_enlightenment(int mode UNUSED, int final), so upstream itself carries an unread mode on a section function and mirroring the C signature is the faithful choice; the port also threads mode to one_characteristic(), which reads it. The over-broad stops fail closed for states no supported path can produce, so no screen, message or random-number call differs from the C. The proposed lint check would equally flag a faithful port of insight.c:728. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input that makes an unread mode change output.

rejections.summary: None of js/insight.js's 16 stops is exercised by any test, and the fail-closed property is said not to hold because 12 of the 16 run after basics_enlightenment() has called find_ac().
rejections.counterEvidence: find_ac()'s write is conditional on armorClass !== u.uac, matching do_wear.c:2508-2510 at the same point in the same sequence, and js/u_init_inventory_attrs.js is untouched by the reviewed range. Measured on a live game at a ready D:1 prompt, u.uac and disp.botl read the same before and after an extra find_ac() call, so no stop leaves state the prompt did not already have; C calls find_ac() before the same points regardless. The residual true claim, that no test threw a stop, was addressed separately: the applied fixes add tests that throw the towel, stuck_ring() and deafness stops. Do not reopen without a state where find_ac() writes before a stop and the write is observable.

head: 2adc5af64b2a6dffc08e56c1ae71d0b453f92d73
evidence: Light delta review clearing the audit-fix debt from the no-time-command correctness pass, as .agents/review.md allows before a review deadline; the deadline is the holdout evaluation at that goal's close. Three finders ran (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability is what the light mode drops. 9 raw findings, 8 after deduplication, 7 confirmed and all 7 applied at acf05a3, 1 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. No production defect: five findings were against comments and tests the audit fixes themselves added, including a hasProperty() header that stated the direction of divergence backwards for four youprop.h macros and a can_advance() ordering test that passed with the bug reinstated. The rejected finding, a real Deaf mismatch in js/dogmove.js, is outside the range and unreachable, and is recorded in ROADMAP.md for the leashed-pet work. Validation at acf05a3: 1,767 tests passing, four generated-data checks, check:namespace-members, development score unchanged at 98,759 PRNG values with 286 screens and cursors, and the no-time matrix matching 71,967 calls with 158 screens across 29 segments.

rejections.summary: js/dogmove.js heroDeaf() reads u.uprops[DEAF] alone and adds a `blocked` term youprop.h:125 has no counterpart for, so OPTIONS=deaf was said to still diverge in dogmove.c's leashed-pet trap arm.
rejections.counterEvidence: The mismatch is real but the path is unreachable and the file is outside the reviewed range. js/unported_monster_actions.js refuses a leashed pet before dog_move() runs, and dog_move() has that one caller, so no live path reaches the arm. git diff --stat 60bf2c3..2adc5af does not list js/dogmove.js, and heroDeaf() is unchanged by both commits; widening the Deaf fix into it would breach the confinement rule this delta review exists to enforce. Recorded in ROADMAP.md as future work to fix with the leashed-pet slice. Do not reopen as a finding against this range; reopen against the leashed-pet work.

head: 60bf3d04c84bce48ff7aadf7989556874ee0f3e5
evidence: Full pass over the whole running and rushing goal: the room run, corridor running, and ctrl-direction rush, plus the runmode option and the animation-frame comparison stream. Four finders ran (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency were not enabled, because the range adds no hot-path work beyond the source-required per-turn traversal and no new shared mutable state. 16 raw findings, 16 after deduplication, 13 confirmed: 7 applied at 374fb85 and 6 deferred, 3 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. Both production defects were applied. The first is the one that mattered: endRunning() dropped the disp.time_botl set and terrainstatus recompute that hack.c:4132-4145 performs, while the port had already ported the two places that suppress those updates during a run, so the catch-up had no owner. The six deferred findings are all missing test pins rather than suspected wrong behavior, each naming a mutation the suite survives; they are recorded in ROADMAP.md with the instruction to clear them before the next holdout, and two of them need a fresh C recording with mention_walls set. Validation at 374fb85: 1,800 tests passing, four generated-data checks, check:namespace-members, development score unchanged at 99,496 PRNG values and 321 screens with all 33 sessions identical, and all three run matrices matching 90,877, 87,714 and 57,676 PRNG calls with 115, 126 and 61 screens and 325, 268 and 163 animation frames.

productionDefects.summary: endRunning() implemented two of end_running()'s four responsibilities, dropping the disp.time_botl set and the terrainstatus recompute that hack.c:4132-4145 performs inside its `if (svc.context.run)` guard. moveloop_core() and classify_terrain() suppress both updates for the whole of a run so this function can make them up; the port had the suppressing halves without the catch-up. nomul() masked it by setting disp.botl itself, but the direct callers in js/uhitm.js and js/eat.js reach endRunning() without nomul.

curs_on_u() took no state and flushed the module-global game, so runmode_delay_output(state) wrote disp.time_botl into one object while flush_screen()/bot() read and cleared it from another. Production always passes game, so the mismatch was reachable only from a test, and the existing test hit it silently. curs_on_u() now refuses a non-global state and the test drives the real object.

rejections.summary: interrupt_multi() was said to emit its boundary before nomul(0), reversing allmain.c's statement order, with the comment justifying the reversal on the wrong ground.
rejections.counterEvidence: Refuted against the source order in allmain.c; the reviewers' own verification could not sustain the claimed reversal as a behavioral difference. Do not reopen without a recorded case where the emitted boundary and the nomul(0) produce a different observable order.

rejections.summary: endRunning() was said to zero a positive multi, which end_running(TRUE) never does, making it an invented clamp now live on do_attack()'s 'is in the way' path.
rejections.counterEvidence: The central factual claim is false. hack.c:4153-4156 is `/* cancel multi */ if (gm.multi > 0) gm.multi = 0;`, the closing statements of end_running(), so the port's clamp is a faithful translation. The line is also pre-existing: `git show 2adc5af:js/hack.js` already contains it, and the diff shows it only as context. The proposed fix would introduce the divergence it claims to remove. Do not reopen without a C reading that contradicts hack.c:4153-4156.

rejections.summary: totalFrames() in scripts/diff-fresh.mjs duck-types two element shapes, the C side's {frames, location} objects and the JS side's bare arrays, behind `(step.frames ?? step).length`.
rejections.counterEvidence: Judged not to survive verification as a defect in this range. Do not reopen without a recorded case where the two shapes yield a different frame total than a shape-explicit reading would.

head: f826ba5392d313da8951095111b8201f5be497fe
evidence: Full pass over the extended-command prompt, which fired the commands gate at 1,289 of 1,000 unreviewed lines. Four finders ran; performance and concurrency were not enabled. 19 raw findings, 16 after deduplication, all 16 confirmed and none rejected. Four are applied at 2640c9f: three production defects and the generated-table test that pins the restored column. Twelve are deferred, and three of those are one defect seen from three angles — the port's flush_screen() is a whole-screen rebuild where display.c's re-emits only dirty cells, so the faithful vpline() flush_screen(1) call this range added erases an open tty menu at the two pre-existing menu-search call sites. .agents/review.md puts that outside audit-fix scope, because it changes rendering behavior and needs the gnew dirty discipline and gb.bot_disabled, which the port lacks; it is recorded in ROADMAP.md with the instruction to implement it and then run a new full pass over the expanded range rather than a delta. This pass does not cover that implementation. The applied fixes: tty_get_ext_cmd() had dropped C's iflags.extmenu guard entirely and the option was parsed and discarded, so a path meant to fail closed gave the typed prompt; a 0xFF byte was stored as text where C's signed char cast makes it EOF and cancels the line; and the generated table had dropped extcmdlist[]'s f_text column, which rhack() reads to name a counted command's occupation. Validation at 2640c9f: 1,808 tests passing, five generated-data checks including check:extcmds, check:namespace-members, development unchanged at 398 screens and 99,496 PRNG values, and the matrix matching 71,359 calls with 370 screens plus 12,261 calls with 33 screens in debug mode.

productionDefects.summary: tty_get_ext_cmd() dropped C's first statement, `if (iflags.extmenu) return extcmd_via_menu();`, replacing it with a comment. Nothing read the option at all: parseNethackrc accepted `extmenu` and discarded it, so a deliberately unported path did not fail closed and silently gave the typed prompt instead.

A 0xFF input byte was stored as ordinary text. cmd.c:452 ends pgetchar() with `return (char) ch;` and char is signed, so 255 arrives as -1 and getline.c:85 treats it as EOF, cancelling the line and setting iflags.term_gone. The restart arm is gated on Escape alone, so EOF cancels even over existing text.

The generated extcmdlist[] table dropped the sixth column, f_text, which rhack() reads at cmd.c:3728 to name the occupation a counted command starts. 'search' and 'wait' are the two rows carrying one, and neither the file nor the generator said a column was missing.

hooked_tty_getlin()'s new flush_screen(1) erases an open tty menu, because the port's flush_screen() is a whole-screen rebuild through _buildScreenOutput() while display.c's re-emits only dirty glyph-buffer cells and select_menu() sets gb.bot_disabled. The call itself is faithful to pline.c vpline(); the function it calls is not.
The two pre-existing ttyGetlinSearch menu call sites now run the new unconditional flush_screen(1) and are untested against the menu erasure it causes.

hooked_tty_getlin() ports pline.c vpline()'s `if (u.ux) flush_screen(...)` without the `state === game` guard that the other port of the same C line carries, so a non-global state would flush the wrong game.

head: 4e9a59f8b7098a4f9e80e7d05c7df2bc21363071
evidence: Light delta review of the audit-fix and debt-clearing tail behind the extended-command pass. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability skipped, which the clarity audit covers. 8 raw findings, 6 after deduplication, 5 confirmed. All five applied in 61f41f9: extmenu added to HANDLED_BOOLEAN_OPTIONS so every spelling options.c:5224 accepts reaches iflags; getline.c:120 corrected to getline.c:85 and cmd.c:102 to cmd.c:3728; six tests pinning the EOF gate and the extmenu guard, each verified by applying a mutation and watching it fail. Suite 1,823 passing, up from 1,817. Development unchanged at 398 screens and 99,496 random-number values across 33 sessions; the extended-command matrix unchanged at 31 segments and 71,392 calls plus 4 debug segments and 12,261 calls.

productionDefects.summary: applyBooleanOption() gained an extmenu arm but HANDLED_BOOLEAN_OPTIONS did not gain the name, so OPTIONS=extmenu:true fell through to the compound-option path: iflags.extmenu stayed undefined and the raw string was parked in flags. options.c:5224 maps true, yes, on and 1 to not-negated for any boolean, so C ran extcmd_via_menu() where the port opened the typed prompt. The fail-open the arm was added to close stayed open for one of the three spellings.

rejections.summary: The correctness finder filed the missing tests for the EOF gate and the extmenu guard a third time as one correctness defect anchored at js/getline.js:176.
rejections.counterEvidence: The anchor line is correct and the finder's own probes say so: '.#wa\xFF' ends with term_gone 1, '.#wa\x00' restarts to '#', and the text concedes 'the gap is validation, not behavior'. js/getline.js:176 reads `if (c !== EOF_BYTE && text)`, which matches getline.c:88's `if (c == '\033' && obufp[0] != '\0')` because only Escape and EOF reach the arm. Its two mutations are identical to ones already carried by the confirmed test findings at js/getline.js:169 and js/getline.js:278. Do not reopen without a divergence at this line that the confirmed test findings do not already cover.

head: 61f41f9b8255ad5359d491196bde97d69ea7d3eb
evidence: Light delta review of the audit-fix tail 61f41f9 together with 671c4fb, the recorder change that sits between it and the previous frontier. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability skipped. 9 raw findings, 7 after deduplication. The workflow confirmed six; the orchestrator rejected one of those on counter-evidence the adjudicator lacked, namely that the range spans two commits and the recorder feature it treats as bundled is 671c4fb's own fully described commit. Five applied in 2ac43bc: extmenu's Off default stored to match optlist.h:303, a third wrong C citation corrected in two files, the tracker test decoupled from live ROADMAP.md prose, and the recorder's own gate given a test through an injectable tracker read. Every fix verified by mutation. Suite 1,824 passing. Development unchanged at 398 screens and 99,496 random-number values across 33 sessions; all four matrices unchanged.

productionDefects.summary: js/options.js left iflags.extmenu out of the default state while every other Off-defaulting iflags boolean is stored as an explicit false: eight_bit_tty (optlist.h:300), hilite_pet (365), hilite_pile (368), hitpointbar (379) and altmeta (159). optlist.h:303 binds extmenu to &iflags.extmenu with a default of Off, so C's startup value is FALSE rather than absent. The difference is invisible to the truth test in tty_get_ext_cmd() but visible in the second-turn state snapshot, where it is the single differing path across all seventeen cases.

rejections.summary: The correctness finder reported that 61f41f9 bundles an unreviewed recorder feature (deferral validation in scripts/quality-status.mjs plus policy edits) that its commit message never mentions, violating the rule that an audit-fix commit is limited to corrections for confirmed findings.
rejections.counterEvidence: The premise mistakes the range for the commit. `git log --oneline 4e9a59f..61f41f9` lists two commits, and `git show --stat 61f41f9` touches only QUALITY.json, js/getline.js, js/options.js, scripts/generate-extcmds.mjs and the two test files. The recorder feature belongs to 671c4fb, a separate commit whose message describes it in full. The range spanned both because the orchestrator chose it that way, so there is nothing to split. The residual concern, that 671c4fb was never independently reviewed, is answered by this pass covering it: two of its confirmed findings came from that commit and both were applied. Do not reopen without showing that a single commit bundles work outside its stated findings.
rejections.reopenIf: a single commit is shown to bundle work outside its stated findings

rejections.summary: The variable-trace finder reported that the deferral requirement is enforced only at record time, so the 21 already-stored deferred findings across five passes keep no durable record permanently.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator refuted both causality and resolution. The gap predates the range: `git show 4e9a59f:scripts/quality-status.mjs` shows validateAuditMetrics() taking only requireRejections, so no pass carried a deferrals array and no mechanism to require one existed; the change adds a record for future passes and leaves the historical state as it found it. The proposed backfill is also impossible for the majority of the data it targets, because the commit message records that nine of the twelve findings deferred by the extended-command pass existed solely in session-scoped output under /tmp, which is gone. Do not reopen without a recoverable source for the historical deferrals.

head: 2ac43bceb22c833fb670117105f40f85d334cd13
evidence: Light delta review of the audit-fix commit 2ac43bc. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability skipped. 7 raw findings, 5 after deduplication. No production defect: every finding concerns the previous commit's own collateral. The workflow confirmed four and rejected one; the orchestrator promoted that rejection to confirmed and applied it, because the indentation probe it named genuinely certified a CommonMark divergence the test never exercised. All five applied in a010008, which touches test files only. The substantive finding is that storing extmenu's Off default drained the negated-spelling assertions: a mutation stopping the negation arm from writing iflags left all 1,824 tests passing, and failed before the default was added. Each fix verified by mutation. Suite 1,824 passing; development unchanged at 398 screens and 99,496 random-number values across 33 sessions; the extended-command matrix unchanged.

head: d1a71f7ea035fe6f21567fe7760416ce9b0b5674
evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the explicit search command and the debt accumulated in eight areas. Four mandatory finders (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency not triggered and not enabled. 13 raw findings, 13 after deduplication, 9 confirmed, 7 applied at c706db8, 2 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 4 rejected with counter-evidence, none unverified, no warnings. Two applied production defects were reachable and wrong: M_AP_TYPE() dropped monst.h:73's mask, and the statue-trap and hallucinatory-trap refusals threw a bare Error that escaped runSegment() instead of converting to the retryable command boundary. Neither moved a development session, which is why the fresh matrix and the new end-to-end boundary case are the gate rather than the score. Development score identical before and after the fixes at 433 of 7,765 screens and 99,552 PRNG calls; scripts/run-explicit-search.mjs matches 13 segments, 35,560 PRNG calls, 80 screens and 80 cursors; 1,857 tests, four generated-data checks and check:namespace-members pass at c706db8. Every new test was observed failing against the line it covers, each mutation named in that commit message. The range base is the oldest frontier among the claimed areas, so it re-reads commits already covered for the later ones; it also absorbs 88e2193, the previous pass's audit-fix commit, which had been correctness debt since.

productionDefects.summary: M_AP_TYPE() dropped monst.h:73's & M_AP_TYPMASK, so a monster carrying M_AP_F_DKNOWN with no appearance type read as truthy and the explicit search refused a square where C takes mfind0()'s else arm and calls newsym(). The search slice was the helper's first and only consumer.

The explicit search's statue-trap and hallucination exclusions refused with a bare Error instead of UnsupportedSearchError, so failClosedCommand() did not convert them and the refusal escaped runSegment() as a hard failure rather than the retryable command boundary every other exclusion in the slice uses. Reproduced end to end against the live s key.

The same defect traced from preflightTrap(): requireOperation() and requireInjected() raise a bare Error for the statue-trap and hallucination arms, which none of the nine Unsupported* classes failClosedCommand() recognises matches, so the checklist's claim that these exclusions fail closed did not hold at the command boundary. Recorded separately because the variable-trace finder reached it from the throw site rather than from the command path.

js/cmd.js held a second definition of the four hack.h ECMD_* codes while js/detect.js built dosearch()'s return from the js/const.js copy, so the producer and the consumer of that value read different tables.

rhack()'s new search arm applied two of the three result tests cmd.c:3810-3818 applies, omitting the ECMD_CANCEL|ECMD_FAIL test, while its comment claimed parity with the '#' arm. The two forms disagree for (ECMD_TIME|ECMD_CANCEL), the combined result cmd.c:3805-3809 documents by name.

hack.c nomul() has two JavaScript owners: the faithful js/hack.js nomul(), added at 0d4a4ac inside this range, and js/detect.js's older inline defaultNomulZero(), which omits end_running()'s disp.time_botl write and its iflags.terrain_typ/classify_terrain() catch-up. dosearch0() calls the second on its secret-door and secret-corridor finds.

deferrals.summary: hack.c nomul() has two JavaScript owners: the faithful js/hack.js nomul(), added at 0d4a4ac inside this range, and js/detect.js's older inline defaultNomulZero(), which omits end_running()'s disp.time_botl write and its iflags.terrain_typ/classify_terrain() catch-up. dosearch0() calls the second on its secret-door and secret-corridor finds.
deferrals.trackedIn: `nomul()` has two owners and they disagree

deferrals.summary: snapshotMfndposMutation()'s per-slot poss/info snapshot and restore are provable no-ops, because resetMfndposData() reassigns both arrays before the core writes anything, and the comment above them justifies the work with a caller state the same commit made impossible. The rollback test cannot distinguish their removal.
deferrals.trackedIn: the mfndpos rollback restores what nothing changed

rejections.summary: Two comments introduced with runSearchCommand() were said to miscount the command wrappers in opposite directions.
rejections.counterEvidence: Only one half is true. The wrapper definitions sit at js/cmd.js:598, 620, 647, 667, 690 and 695, so 'the five wrappers above' was indeed off by one and has been corrected to four. But the section header's 'the first five wrappers' reads against the handler list its own preceding sentence enumerates -- ddoinv(), dovspell(), dodiscovered(), doattributes(), dolook() and dosearch() -- and is right as written. The finding was stated as two miscounts of which 'neither is right', and that compound claim is false. Do not reopen the header without quoting the sentence two lines above it.

rejections.summary: preflightSearchMonster()'s doc comment was said to claim that a refusal from it always precedes the loop's first rnl(), while one of its two call sites is mfind0(), which runs inside the loop.
rejections.counterEvidence: The comment names the dependency the finding says is missing: js/detect.js:530-537 reads 'mfind0() calls this at the square it is looking at and preflightExplicitSearch() calls it at all eight, so a refusal here always happens before the loop's first rnl().' The 'so' clause is derived from the all-eight call site, and the conclusion is true because preflightExplicitSearch() runs to completion before dosearch0() reaches its loop. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input that refuses inside the loop and not in the preflight.

rejections.summary: A duplicate of the bare-Error refusal defect, adding that the refusal is mislabelled to the player-facing log as 'automatic search requires ...' and that a doc comment twenty lines above asserts the opposite.
rejections.counterEvidence: The underlying class mismatch is real and is recorded as an applied production defect above; this entry's two distinguishing claims are not. requireOperation() puts that text in an Error that reaches no window: js/cmd.js discards it into an UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError message when it converts, and js/jsmain.js rethrows it otherwise. Nothing routes it through ttyPline(), ttyNorep(), the status line or the top line. Do not reopen the player-facing half without naming the window call that prints it.

rejections.summary: glyph_is_invisible()'s invisible_monster marker was said to be not merely dormant but unimplementable, because remembered_glyph_from_presentation() is the port's sole builder of remembered glyphs and structurally cannot carry it.
rejections.counterEvidence: display.c:378-385 map_invisible() writes levl[x][y].glyph = GLYPH_INVISIBLE directly, routing through no presentation conversion, so a faithful port writes the marker straight onto location.remembered_glyph. That the field is writable is demonstrated in the tree: scripts/detect.test.mjs sets remembered_glyph = { invisible_monster: true } and glyph_is_invisible() answers true, which the same test asserts. head: 5879bed71b42deb7fe8346e75e589c42922d956b
evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the first slice of the closed-door goal. Four mandatory finders (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency not triggered and not enabled. 16 raw findings, 15 after deduplication, 13 confirmed, all 13 applied at cfbc205, none deferred, 2 rejected with counter-evidence, none unverified, no warnings. Three live production defects: flags.autoopen was never registered as a boolean option so autoopen:false stored a truthy string and defeated the new refusal gate; requireAutoopenClosedDoor() read a state.context.run the admission seam had not yet assigned, so a rush into a closed door committed its movement intent before being refused; and the portcullis guard re-implemented dbridge.c is_drawbridge_wall() without its DB_DIR test, refusing a door whose neighbouring drawbridge faces away. Five test findings were assertions that could not fail, including a refusal-term matrix covering one of six terms and a replay oracle that checked only a screen count. Every new test was observed failing against a named mutation, listed in the fix commit. Development score identical before and after the fixes at 436 of 7,765 screens, 437 cursors and 99,541 PRNG calls; scripts/run-closed-door-autoopen.mjs matches 10 segments, 27,136 PRNG calls, 33 screens and 33 cursors, and the rush matrix 32 segments and 100,341 calls. The range base is the oldest frontier among the claimed areas, so it re-reads the two search audit-fix commits already covered for commands, runtime and world-effects.

productionDefects.summary: flags.autoopen was never registered in HANDLED_BOOLEAN_OPTIONS, so the `autoopen:value` form fell through to the compound-option preservation path and stored the string "false"/"no"/"off" in flags. requireAutoopenClosedDoor() tests `!state.flags.autoopen` and a non-empty string is truthy, so the port pulled at a door options.c:5229-5233 requires C to refuse.

requireAutoopenClosedDoor() read state.context.run, which js/cmd.js assigns only after calling the admission preflight, so the run test was dead at the seam. A rush or run into a closed door was admitted there and refused only inside domove(), after the movement intent had committed.

The same stale-state defect traced from the call site: preflightDomoveDestination() already threads `run` for runStopsBeforeMonster() but dropped it when calling the closed-door guard. Recorded separately because the variable-trace finder reached it from the caller rather than from the guard.

The portcullis guard re-implemented dbridge.c is_drawbridge_wall() inline and omitted its DB_DIR test, refusing a superset: a DOOR whose orthogonally adjacent drawbridge faces away is not a portcullis and C opens it normally. A faithful port of the C function already existed unexported in js/startup_a11y.js.

The comment justifying the deletion of blocksMove()'s door term claimed js/mklev.js never writes loc.doormask for a generated door. dosdoor() does not, but create_door() and the special-level door path do, so the stated premise is false for doors ordinary levels produce; the deletion remains correct for the second reason the comment gave.

The same comment said the closed-door route is now owned "in both callers" when blocksMove() has exactly one caller left, so a reader auditing the deletion could not tell whether the second was removed deliberately or overlooked.

rejections.summary: domove() was said to call test_move() before every monster, attack and terrain branch whereas domove_core() calls it last, with the new comment anchoring the call to the wrong C line.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator found the ordering claim unsupported against hack.c's actual control flow for this path. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input whose observable output differs because of the claimed ordering, and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: The comment on the paired door.flags / door.doormask write was said to claim that every reader in the port accepts either spelling, when readers use the `flags || doormask` idiom.
rejections.counterEvidence: The `flags || doormask` idiom does accept either spelling for every value the port writes, so the comment is accurate as written for the doors this code produces. Do not reopen without a reader that consults only one field and an input that reaches it.

head: cdb83a481180205a8f011ee67b066116a93aaad6
evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the second slice of the closed-door goal, the lock.c doopen_indir() message switch. Four mandatory finders (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency not triggered and not enabled. 17 raw findings, 14 after deduplication, 10 confirmed, all 10 applied at b8323b1, none deferred, 4 rejected with counter-evidence, none unverified, no warnings. One live production defect: the seam refused D_LOCKED | D_TRAPPED, a mask lock.c:855 sends through the same message switch as a plain locked door and back out before the trap tail, so the port was refusing a case it fully supports. The second production finding is a premise three comments shared and the C refutes, that closed_door() admits D_LOCKED and D_CLOSED alone; it is a bit test, and the mask guard those comments make look redundant is in fact the only thing keeping a trapped door away from the pull. Six test findings were assertions that could not fail, including two of hack.c:1097's four autoopen terms with no case at all, the drawbridge predicate's vertical arms left unguarded when the range replaced a four-way adjacency check with it, and a replay oracle reading retained message history rather than the rendered line. Every new or changed test was observed failing against a named mutation, each listed in the fix commit. Development score identical before and after the fixes at 442 of 7,765 screens, 443 cursors and 99,625 PRNG calls; scripts/run-closed-door-autoopen.mjs matches 19 segments, 50,018 PRNG calls, 61 screens and 61 cursors. The range also absorbs cfbc205, the previous slice's audit-fix commit, which had been correctness debt since it landed.

productionDefects.summary: The seam refused D_LOCKED | D_TRAPPED as a door whose trap would fire and whose shop would be billed, but lock.c:855 tests only D_CLOSED, so 0x18 enters the same message switch as a plain locked door, prints the same line and returns at :895. The b_trapped() and add_damage() tail at :907-911 is inside the "known to be CLOSED" arm below that return, so the port was refusing a case it fully supports. D_CLOSED | D_TRAPPED stays refused because its roll does reach the tail.

Three comments stated that monmove.c closed_door() admits D_LOCKED and D_CLOSED only. It is a bit test, doormask & (D_LOCKED | D_CLOSED), so D_TRAPPED combinations satisfy it too. The consequence is not merely wording: the mask guard two lines below reads as a restatement of closed_door() when it is the only thing keeping a trapped door away from the pull, and a maintainer deleting it as redundant would let one through to lock.c:904's roll.

rejections.summary: verysmall() and u.usteed were said to be refused ahead of the locked-door arm, where lock.c checks verysmall only after the message switch returns and reads u.usteed inside the kick arm the port already refuses.
rejections.counterEvidence: Neither term can hold in any state the port produces: js/u_init.js initializes usteed to null and no assignment to it exists, and js/mondata.js verysmall() needs msize < MZ_SMALL, which no playable race satisfies while polymorph is unported. The guard lines are also unchanged context in the range's diff. The finding concedes it is latent rather than live. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input that makes either term true.

rejections.summary: The comment above the doopen_indir() call was said to misdescribe how test_move()'s injection contract narrows at the callee.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator found the described narrowing accurate for the env keys doopen_indir() accepts. Do not reopen without naming a key the caller forwards that the callee neither accepts nor rejects as described.

rejections.summary: Renaming a faithful port of dbridge.c is_drawbridge_wall() to its C name and exporting it from the accessibility-notice module into game logic was said to be the wrong home.
rejections.counterEvidence: The wrong home is real and is stated in a comment at the function, which records that it belongs in a js/dbridge.js port of that file; moving it is a relocation outside audit-fix scope rather than a defect in this range. Do not reopen as a correctness finding; raise it as a simplification trigger instead.

rejections.summary: The dormant-arm test was said to assert result === ECMD_OK for all five masks where C returns ECMD_TIME for one of them.

The three applied are all against the orchestrator's own discovery-ledger fix from 8bd4d6a. head: 005ea20e047e76958b57d78c39ed3136f3ebe1d1
evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the slice that gave monmove.c postmov() a home and admitted the inert doorway. Four mandatory finders; performance and concurrency not triggered. 16 raw findings, 13 after deduplication, 11 confirmed, 2 applied at 76659e9, 9 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 2 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. Both applied findings are the failure mode the pass was directed at: a call C makes that the port skips, which produces no refusal and no stop. The evacuation of postSimpleMove() out of the boundary file dropped its trap guard on the monster's own square, leaving a monster that reports MMOVE_MOVED without changing square, on a trap, unguarded — the refusal is restored at mintrap()'s own position at monmove.c:1509, reading the live square rather than a destination. And a third silent PRNG gap was found by hunting siblings of the two the slice itself had found: monmove.c:1692-1699 draws rn2(5) for a hides_under() species or an eel, and the pre-scan guard keyed on is_hider(), M1_HIDE, which is a different flag from hides_under(), M1_CONCEAL, so a garter snake, centipede or scorpion reached the arm and the draw was skipped. Of the nine deferred, five are comments stating a false rule about C's door block — its first arm tests D_TRAPPED alone for a magic-key holder and writes the doormask, which is why the port's whole-mask equality is right rather than despite — and four are assertions that do not discriminate. Development score identical before and after the fixes at 446 of 7,765 screens, 446 cursors and 99,840 PRNG calls; scripts/run-monster-doorway.mjs matches 6 segments, 17,436 PRNG calls, 146 screens and 146 cursors.

productionDefects.summary: The boundary evacuation dropped a refusal without replacing it. postSimpleMove() called assertSimpleDestination() for every MMOVE_MOVED, so its trap check covered the monster's own square whether or not the square had changed; postmov() relied on the pre-move gate, which only inspects a square a monster is about to enter, leaving a monster that reports MMOVE_MOVED without changing square, on a trap, with no guard at all.

A third silent PRNG gap: monmove.c:1692-1699 draws rn2(5) for a hides_under() species or an eel with mundetected clear, and helpless() cannot hold because dochug() returns before m_move() for a sleeping or immobile monster. The pre-scan guard keys on is_hider() (M1_HIDE), a different flag from hides_under() (M1_CONCEAL), so a garter snake, centipede or scorpion reached the arm and the draw was skipped with no refusal and no stop.

Five finders including performance, enabled because the cloned scan now owns a terrain grid and vision buffers and the preflight re-derives the transparency index every elapsed turn; the performance finder confirmed nothing. 14 raw findings, 11 after deduplication, 10 confirmed, 2 applied at d7dd150, 8 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 1 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. The material defect was at the seam the pass was pointed at: the transparency-index restore was not side-effect-free, because recalc_block_point() runs rebuildVisionPoint(), which sets vision_full_recalc whenever the change touches the hero's current vision — the normal case for a door in a lit room — so the dry run left a flag the live scan then consumed as a vision_recalc(0) C never performs. The second applied finding is the orchestrator's own from the previous cycle: the trap guard reinstated at monmove.c:1509's position had no test, so deleting it left the whole suite green and the repaired defect could return silently. Of the eight deferred, four are comments that outlived the code they describe — including two that still describe the design the implementer abandoned when a focused test disproved it — and three are gaps in the isolation's own coverage. evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the monster-door goal's last slice, the hero's two diagonal doorway refusals. Four mandatory finders; performance and concurrency not triggered. 17 raw findings, 12 after deduplication, 10 confirmed, 2 applied at 3471a99, 8 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 2 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. head: 3471a99a07b6fb35dbb8a2d63801ee4c787a380a
evidence: Light delta review of the movement-seam ordering fix, run because the monster-door goal's holdout evaluation is a review deadline and audit-fix debt cannot stand across one. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability is the perspective a light pass drops. 8 raw findings, 6 after deduplication, 6 confirmed and all 6 applied at ff865ec, none deferred, none rejected, none unverified, no warnings. This is the fourth consecutive goal in which a delta review found collateral from the previous fix, and this time it found the fix wrong in two ways. Half of it was dead: the refusal guard added for the safemon path was the last statement of its block with nothing after the chain, so deleting it changed no test, while its comment asserted an invariant that did not hold. And moving the pet-swap seam ahead of the refusal made the port throw a segment-ending boundary for a trap or object on the pet's square, on a step C declines without consulting them. The adjudicator settled the question the finder left open by going to the C: uhitm.c:474 evaluates foo = (Punished || !rn2(7) || ...) inside do_attack()'s is_safemon branch, so C spends a draw even for the pet before returning FALSE and letting test_move() refuse — which means neither the original nor the first-fix ordering matched C, and admitting the step silently diverges by exactly one rn2(7). Any monster on a refused diagonal now fails closed, safemon included, ahead of the swap-consequence gates. The pet test asserted the silent refusal and now asserts the boundary plus an unchanged draw count, since failing closed means before the draw rather than instead of it. Development score identical before and after at 459 of 7,765 screens, 459 cursors and 99,980 PRNG calls; the diagonal doorway matrix matches 14 segments, 35,931 calls and 38 screens.

productionDefects.summary: Moving requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap() ahead of the diagonal refusal made the seam throw a boundary for a trap, floor object, region or engraving on the pet's square, on a step C refuses inside test_move() without ever consulting them — reintroducing on the monster arm the hazard already recorded for the empty-square arm.

The refusal guard added for the safemon path was the last statement of the destination-monster block with nothing after the else-if chain, so it had no effect and deleting it changed no test, while its comment asserted that the diagonal refusal claims the step exactly as on an empty square. The adjudicator settled the underlying question: uhitm.c:474 evaluates foo = (Punished || !rn2(7) || ...) inside do_attack()'s is_safemon branch, so C spends a draw even for a pet before returning FALSE and letting test_move() refuse, and admitting the step silently diverges by exactly that rn2(7).

head: ff865ec919042f747f12d44962b8c7b2f782bc2a
evidence: Second light delta review in the chain repairing the movement seam, run because the monster-door goal's holdout is a review deadline. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace). 10 raw findings, 8 after deduplication, 6 confirmed and all 6 applied at 278bf6c, none deferred, 2 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. Both production findings are against the orchestrator's own previous commit, and the first is a claim that should have been checked before it was written: the comment justifying the fail-closed throw asserted the port has no do_attack() and cannot spend uhitm.c:474's rn2(7) until combat lands, when do_attack() is ported at js/uhitm.js:51 with that draw at :70 and domove() calls it live at :1098 — an ordinary pet swap draws it today. That is the third comment in this chain to assert an invariant the tree does not have. The throw remains load-bearing for a different reason, now stated: domove() runs test_move() at :1065 before the do_attack() call, the reverse of hack.c:2794 and :2841, so admitting the step refuses it inside test_move() and never reaches the draw, and the removal condition is a domove() reorder rather than a trigger that has already fired. The second finding is that the ordering half was pinned by nothing — swapping the throw back after requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap() left the suite green, because the pet fixture's square holds nothing and every swap gate returns. A trap on the destination distinguishes them and now reports 'pet swap trap interaction' under the base order, a boundary naming a situation C never reaches. Development score identical before and after at 459 of 7,765 screens, 459 cursors and 99,980 PRNG calls.

productionDefects.summary: The justification for the new fail-closed throw was factually wrong: it claimed the port has no do_attack() and cannot spend uhitm.c:474's rn2(7) until combat lands. do_attack() is ported at js/uhitm.js:51 with the draw at :70, and domove() calls it live at :1098, so an ordinary pet swap draws it today. The throw is still load-bearing, but because domove() runs test_move() at :1065 before that call — the reverse of hack.c:2794 and :2841 — so admitting the step refuses it inside test_move() and never reaches the draw. A maintainer greping for do_attack would have read the stated removal condition as already met and deleted the guard.

The half of the change placing the refusal ahead of requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap() was pinned by no test: swapping the two statements back left the whole suite green, because the pet fixture's square holds no trap, object, region or engraving and every swap gate returns.

evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the first slice of the trap goal: mintrap(), trapeffect_selector() and the monster arm of trapeffect_sqky_board(), into a new js/trap_effects.js. All three production defects are the same class the pass was directed at: a refusal or check that does not precede what it guards. trapeffect_sqky_board() and seetrap() resolved their own injected owners, so those throws landed after mintrap() had written mtrapseen on the victim and every onlooker, spent rnl(5), and emitted the squeak; m_move()'s random fallback was narrower than its call graph and the resulting bare TypeError is not a class the elapsed turn converts, so it would discard a segment rather than stop it; and wake_nearto() made wake_msg() live without the coordinate prefix C's pline_mon() adds, with new_were()'s plain pline() checked against source and deliberately left alone. evidence: Light audit-diff-correctness pass over bf96cda..21cea25, three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability was dropped, which is what light mode drops. 10 raw, 9 deduped, 9 confirmed, 9 applied, 0 deferred, 0 rejected, 0 unverified, no warnings. Applied at 628d9fe. The range was widened from the intended b7cc9a3..b51b1d2 because record-review correctly refused to advance the frontier over 8de4b76, the audit-fix commit for the previous pass, whose twenty-five production lines across js/mon.js, js/monmove.js and js/trap_effects.js no pass had read; audit-worktree.mjs cannot scope that tail alone, which is filed in .agents/proposals.md. Five of the nine findings land on 21cea25, the previous pass's own applied fixes, which answers whether a fix needs auditing. The worst was a test added at 21cea25 that pinned wrong behavior: it made a monster minvis to separate C's in_sight and cansee() gates, which also makes canspotmon() false, so C's Monnam() answers It through x_monnam()'s do_it branch at do_name.c:863 while the port answers the species name. The fixture now grants detection, keeping canspotmon() true, and both gates are asserted directly; the missing do_it branch is a silent divergence with no refusal behind it and is recorded under ## Unresolved, unreachable today because nothing on level one sets minvis and assertSimpleActionState() refuses is_hider. Two production defects fixed: mintrap()'s random proof covered only its own two draws while the dart arm needs three more, so the late check ran after mtrapseen was written and raised an unconverted bare TypeError; and the freeze detector's typed-array snapshot missed vision.c's spare COULD_SEE and rmin/rmax buffers, which are unreachable from the state and are precisely what vision_recalc() writes. Six test gaps closed, including both halves of mintrap()'s eager proof, which nothing pinned in either direction, and wake_msg()'s coordinate prefix, which unwrapping left every test and every score unchanged. Validation at the applied head: 2,035 tests pass; development holds at 467 of 7,765 screens, 467 cursors and 100,825 of 610,816 random-number values; the dart matrix passes 9 segments, 47,465 calls and 949 screens; the squeaky-board matrix passes 10 segments, 47,504 calls and 2,084 screens; generated-data and namespace checks pass.

productionDefects.summary: mintrap() proved only rn2 and rnl before its first write, while the dart arm it dispatches to needs rn1, rnd and rne; that late check ran after mon_learns_traps() had written mtrapseen and after the rn2(4) and rnl(5) gates could draw, and raised a bare TypeError that ELAPSED_TURN_PLANNING_REFUSALS does not convert.

The freeze detector's typed-array snapshot reached only the COULD_SEE buffer game.viz_array points at; the spare row set and both rmin/rmax pairs are module-level, unreachable from the state, and are exactly what vision_recalc() writes.

mutation.finderConclusion: Carried from the b7cc9a3..b51b1d2 run, whose target lines this range does not change: 17 mutants of kind relational, logical and boolean under a whole-suite verdict, 4 survivors, each with a reason no test can remove. Three are equivalent mutants (greatest_erosion()'s tie, find_mac()'s cap at exactly plus or minus AC_MAX, and thitm()'s !obj branch, which trapeffect_dart_trap() never takes) and one is nocorpse, read only by the refused strike arm. This pass's own subject, 8de4b76's twenty-five production lines, is a set of refusals and a message wrapping rather than operators, and the tests finder reached the same conclusion the mutation run would: the wake_msg() wrapping was killed by nothing, which is why it now has an accessiblemsg case.

Three production defects were applied. goto_level()'s Punished guards read state.u.uball where the port owns state.uball, so do.c:1616's refusal failed open, and the test pinning it wrote the same wrong field. flush_screen()'s delay lived in a module variable that an aborted level change latched for the rest of the process, so every later segment would have recorded its cursor at the origin; it now lives on the game state that resetGame() replaces per segment. evidence: Light delta review over the audit-fix commit, run because .agents/review.md treats the authorized holdout evaluation that follows as a review deadline that audit-fix debt may not cross. head: 04c26211d2f0d10bc2277fff1a2fb3aaf9bddc21
evidence: Counts: 11 raw, 10 deduplicated, 6 confirmed, 6 applied, 0 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 2 survivors of 2 mutants. Full correctness pass over the whole of the experience-level-gain goal: wiz_level_change(), pluslvl(), attrib.c's innate tables with adjabil() and postadjabil(), xlev_to_rank(), add_weapon_skill(), record_achievement(), and the Tourist arrival grant. Five finders including concurrency, enabled because threading a message owner through You_feel() made adjabil() async and rippled to 26 call sites across seven files, among them the new-game initializer every recorded session runs. All six confirmed findings were applied at feac9a2 with the development score unchanged at 648 of 7,765 screens and 107,437 of 610,816 random-number values. The one production defect was scanLevelArgument() returning the full-precision decimal where wizcmds.c:448 declares int newlevel and reads it with sscanf('%d%c'): C converts through strtol() to a long, saturating, then keeps the low 32 bits, so it reads 4294967296 as 0 and any 20-digit answer as -1, while the port raised the hero toward MAXULEV instead. The concurrency finder returned nothing, which is the pass's substantive negative result about the async seam. Recording this pass also surfaced a defect in the recorder: --areas was documented but never parsed, and the summary printed an unbound identifier, so the write succeeded, dropped the field every other pass carries, and then exited non-zero.

optionalFinders.concurrency: enabled: the range converts adjabil() to async, which rippled to 26 call sites across seven files including u_init_misc() and newgame_pre_mklev(), the new-game initializer every recorded session runs
optionalFinders.performance: not enabled: the range adds no unbounded or amplified work, no worse complexity, no hot-path traversal and no startup cost beyond the source behavior it ports

productionDefects.summary: scanLevelArgument() returned the full-precision decimal where wizcmds.c:448 declares int newlevel and reads it with sscanf("%d%c"). glibc converts in two stages, strtol() to a long saturating at LONG_MAX or LONG_MIN and then a store keeping the low 32 bits, so C reads "4294967296" as 0 and any 20-digit answer as -1 while the port read each as itself and raised the hero toward MAXULEV.

mutation.finderConclusion: Both survivors are the saturation guards the audit fix added to scanLevelArgument(): js/wizcmds.js:32 `>` -> `>=` and :33 `<` -> `<=`, each verified against the whole suite of 143 test files and a 2,286-test baseline. Both are equivalent by construction, so no test can kill either: the only input that distinguishes the operators is wide === LONG_MAX (or LONG_MIN), where the guarded body assigns the value the variable already holds. js/display.js contributed no mutable site, its change being a string literal, and the reviewed range's own three survivors were recorded as equivalent by the slices that landed them.

readiness.boundary: Starting event: the newline submitting `levelchange` at the `#` prompt, and the `>` accepted on a down staircase. Ending events: the `Welcome to experience level N.` top line with the status line the flush repaints beside it and the next command prompt; and the D:2 arrival screen with `Xp:1/2`. The real game executes both paths: `js/cmd.js` doextcmd() dispatches `#levelchange` into `js/wizcmds.js wiz_level_change()`, and `js/do.js goto_level()`'s isNew arm runs the Tourist grant. Five recorded development sessions replay the first path and gained 128 screens across the range.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable before the ending events was traced against nethack-c/upstream/src/: exper.c pluslvl(), more_experienced() and newexplevel(); attrib.c's fifteen innate tables, role_abil(), adjabil() and postadjabil(), setuhpmax(); wizcmds.c wiz_level_change(); botl.c xlev_to_rank() and exp_percent_changing(); weapon.c add_weapon_skill(); insight.c record_achievement() and achieve_rank(); do.c goto_level():1961-1964. The trace covered state and random-number order, including that pluslvl() prints before newhp() and newpw() draw and that postadjabil() runs after its entry's message. Explicit stops, partial implementations and missing subsystems were identified and are listed in the completeness attestation.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Every excluded branch stops before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output, through a named refusal: adjabil()'s loss arm and lose_weapon_skill(); wiz_level_change()'s lowering arm behind losexp(); pluslvl(TRUE) behind newexplevel(); the Upolyd arms of pluslvl() and setuhpmax(); give_may_advance_msg(); and exp_percent_changing() with a status-highlight rule on Xp. Four excluded branches are unreachable rather than refused, each recorded with the reason: pluslvl()'s Upolyd arm and setuhpmax()'s else branch, since js/u_init.js is the port's only writer of u.umonnum; pluslvl()'s 'Welcome back' arm, since u.ulevelmax is bumped in the same block; adjabil()'s already-held suppression test, filed as a deferral against #wizintrinsic; and count_achievements() with rank_to_xlev(), whose only reader is a file the port does not write.

rejections.summary: js/allmain.js:132 -- The comments that justify the new `async` signatures state that these initializers cannot suspend, which is false for JavaScript `await`, and the false claim invites dropping an `await` that silently leaves the hero half-initialized.
rejections.counterEvidence: The comments do not claim what the finding says they claim. js/u_init.js:340-342 reads 'Asynchronous only because attrib.c adjabil() is: its gain arm can print You_feel(), which blocks on --More--. No level-1 innate entry prints, so this call awaits nothing that can suspend.' The word 'suspend' is anaphoric to 'blocks on --More--' in the preceding sentence, and under that definition the sentence is true. js/allmain.js:131-132 uses the same term in the same sense. 'suspend' is used nowhere in js/ in the microtask sense (grep -rn suspend js/ returns only these two lines, js/hack.js:1887 about notices, js/allmain.js:859 about occupations, and the extcmdlist row for ^Z), so no in-repo convention makes the strict reading natural. Counter-evidence: js/u_init.js:340-342 defines its own term one clause earlier: 'its gain arm can print You_feel(), which blocks on --More--. No level-1 innate entry prints, so this call awaits nothing that can suspend.'

rejections.summary: js/attrib.js:244 -- UnsupportedAbilityChangeError's own doc says every throw site changes an intrinsic while the hero is playing, but two of its three sites do not, and cmd.js repeats the incomplete claim by attributing all of them to adjabil()'s lowering arms.
rejections.counterEvidence: The impact rests on setuhpmax() raising this class on the raising path, and it cannot. js/exper.js:192 calls setuhpmax(u.uhpmax + hpinc, true, state), and js/attrib.js:434 guards the throw with `if (!Upolyd(u) || even_when_polyd)`; with even_when_polyd true the else arm is unreachable for that call regardless of Upolyd, and the decided non-issues already record Upolyd as false for every hero the port can build. The class is therefore reachable only from adjabil()'s two arms, exactly what js/cmd.js:918-922 describes, so no wrong edit follows from the wording. Counter-evidence: js/exper.js:192 passes even_when_polyd = true, so js/attrib.js:434's `!Upolyd(u) || even_when_polyd` is always true on the pluslvl() path and the throw at js/attrib.js:394-397 cannot execute; the claim that 'setuhpmax() throws it from the raising path' is false.

rejections.summary: js/attrib.js:320 -- adjabil() validates its message-owner contract in the middle of the traversal, after it has already written intrinsics, so a caller that omits `env.message` gets a half-applied hero plus a raw TypeError that no refusal list catches; the invariant that licenses u_init.js's owner-less call is enforced only by a test.
rejections.counterEvidence: No caller can reach the throw. The two in-tree callers are js/exper.js:217 adjabil(u.ulevel - 1, u.ulevel, state, { message }), which always supplies an owner, and js/u_init.js:377 adjabil(0, 1, state), whose span crosses only ulevel-1 entries, every one of which has an empty gainstr (js/attrib.js:127-218). The invariant is stated at js/attrib.js:123-125, 270-274 and 346-349, the last naming the test that asserts it. A non-atomic assertion on an unreachable path is a harmless deviation. Counter-evidence: js/exper.js:217 passes { message } and js/u_init.js:377 crosses only entries with gainstr '' (js/attrib.js:127-218), so js/attrib.js:320's throw is unreachable from either caller.

rejections.summary: scripts/level-change.test.mjs:378 -- Three assertions use a bare `TypeError` matcher to stand for two different refusals that adjabil() can raise -- see_monsters()'s non-global-state guard and adjabil()'s own missing-message-owner check -- so the oracle does not say which contract each test is pinning.
rejections.counterEvidence: The three assertions are not ambiguous once their setups are traced. The see-invisible test passes `message: () => assert.fail(...)`, so typeof env.message !== 'function' is false and js/attrib.js:320's TypeError cannot fire; had the message printed, the rejection would be an AssertionError, which the TypeError matcher rejects. The postadjabil test likewise passes a collector function. In the third, adjabil(9, 10, rogue) crosses rog_abil's SEARCHING entry, which js/attrib.js:262 does not dispatch on, and the owner check throws before postadjabil() is reached, so see_monsters()'s TypeError is unreachable there. No swap of one refusal for the other is possible. Counter-evidence: scripts/level-change.test.mjs supplies a message function in both see_monsters cases, making js/attrib.js:320's TypeError unreachable, and the third case crosses SEARCHING, which js/attrib.js:262 does not dispatch on, making see_monsters()'s TypeError unreachable.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:3328 -- _stat_update_time()'s `rendered ? … : statusLayouts()` fallback performs a complete status recompute — exactly the whole-bot() behavior timebot()'s comment nine lines above says C never takes — under a header that says the function "refreshes blstats[BL_TIME] alone".
rejections.counterEvidence: The description of what the fallback does is accurate, but the hazard it rests on is not. The finding says the unreachability argument "rests on ordering that nothing enforces"; the ordering is in fact enforced twice over. Counter-evidence: js/allmain.js:141-142 (newgame_pre_mklev) sets g.disp.botlx = true before mklev, and js/moveloop_preamble.js:69 sets state.disp.botlx = true unconditionally, outside the `if (!resuming)` block, so it fires on resumed segments too. js/display.js:3201 gives the `botl || botlx` arm priority over the time_botl arm, and bot() assigns game._renderedStatusLayouts at js/display.js:3275 before clearing botl/botlx at 3276-3278. Every writer of disp.time_botl -- js/allmain.js:527, js/hack.js:372 and js/hack.js:1628 -- runs inside the moveloop, after both botlx writers. So reaching the timebot arm requires botl and botlx to be false, which requires a prior bot(), which sets _renderedStatusLayouts. The fallback cannot execute. The finding's secondary charge, that the arm "neither clears disp.botl/disp.botlx", describes correct porting rather than a defect: botl.c timebot() (293) clears only disp.time_botl.

rejections.summary: js/hack.js:678 -- The comment introducing the blind-terrain guard enumerates dungeon.c surface()'s per-terrain answers and omits THRONE and SINK, which C answers with the already-ported word "floor" through IS_ROOM(), not with a word of their own.
rejections.counterEvidence: The comment does not omit THRONE and SINK; it states their answer. Counter-evidence: js/hack.js:679-681 reads "answers per terrain: \"altar\", \"headstone\", \"fountain\", \"stairs\", \"doorway\", \"floor\" in a room and \"ground\" otherwise". The clause "'floor' in a room" is precisely dungeon.c:1783's `IS_ROOM(levtyp) && !Is_earthlevel(&u.uz)` arm, and rm.h:126 `#define IS_ROOM(typ) ((typ) >= ROOM)` with THRONE=29 / SINK=30 (rm.h:85-86) is exactly how those two types reach it, so the comment already gives them their C word rather than implying a missing one. The list is plainly a summary of the arms this guard can reach and not a per-type catalogue: it also names none of surface()'s "maw", "husk", "air bubble", "cloud", "air", "water", "bottom", "ice", "lava", "bridge" or "wall" arms, and it cites dungeon.c (1750-1787) for the full function.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:2514 -- `_optionalStatusFieldList()` joins two pre-existing helpers whose names already overlap: `_optionalStatusFields()` returns a joined string, `_optionalStatusEntries()` returns `{field, text}` records,
rejections.counterEvidence: The naming overlap is real, but the harm mechanism the finding rests on is impossible. Counter-evidence: The finding claims substituting `_optionalStatusFields()` into a `fields.push(...)` site "produces one unowned blob ... which no type check and no throw catches". It throws. `_optionalStatusFields()` returns a plain string; whether pushed whole or spread into characters, the resulting element has `field.text === undefined`, and js/display.js:2612 (`row.write(nominal, field.text, field.owner)`) reaches `_newStatusRow()`'s `write` at 2405, which evaluates `text.length` on undefined and raises a TypeError before any cell is written. The same is true of the `_writeStatusFields()` path at 2546-2547. There is no silent wrong-shape outcome to guard against.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:2744 -- The sibling builders `_statusLine2Fields()` and `_statusLine3DetailsFields()` return different shapes — a bare array versus `{ fields, hungerX }` — and the missing `hungerX` silently changes `_conditi
rejections.counterEvidence: The stated impact depends on the omission being undetected; it is detected loudly, by three existing tests including two on the whole-pass path. Counter-evidence: I applied the finding's own mutation in an isolated copy of the tree — dropping `hungerX` from `_statusLine3DetailsLayout()`'s call to `_renderStatusFields()` (js/display.js:2782), which is equivalent to dropping it from `_statusLine3DetailsFields()`'s return — and ran the full suite. Three tests fail beyond the four environment-only baseline failures: 'initial three-line status preserves tty overlap until the forced refresh', 'status uses source attribute order and exceptional strength text' (whose assertion at scripts/display-symbols.test.mjs:5175 pins `row(23).indexOf('Deaf') === row(22).length + 1`), and 'a turn-counter refresh leaves the conditions where a whole pass does'. Two of those three are whole-pass tests, contradicting the finding's claim that only the refresh path is covered and that the conditions move "with the suite still green".

rejections.summary: js/display.js:2799 -- The layout `_statusLine3DetailsLayout()` returns on the `initialTtyRefresh` pass pairs an overlap `text` with a `fields` list that re-renders to a different (steady) row, yet `_stat_update_time()`'s c
rejections.counterEvidence: No supported input can feed the overlap layout to `_refreshTimeField()`, so the stated impact — a whole-row repaint where C repaints only BL_TIME — is unreachable, and the finding itself concedes the trigger is 'anyone who later makes that row survive into a turn-counter tick'. Counter-evidence: js/moveloop_preamble.js:69 sets `state.disp.botlx = true` unconditionally (outside the `if (!resuming)` block, so resumed segments too) and only then sets `state.program_state.in_moveloop = 1` at line 84. js/display.js:3285-3296 and js/allmain.js:847-852 both give the `botl || botlx` arm priority over the `time_botl` arm, and js/display.js:3290-3294 computes `initialTtyRefresh` from `!game.program_state.in_moveloop`, so the first in-moveloop flush runs a steady `bot()` that overwrites `game._renderedStatusLayouts` at js/display.js:3360. Every `disp.time_botl` writer (js/allmain.js:527 and the two in js/hack.js) runs inside the moveloop, after that preamble. The overlap layout is therefore always replaced before any `timebot()`.

rejections.summary: scripts/quality-status.test.mjs:1003 -- The new `--areas` command-level test stops at `rejectUnknownOptions()` and never reaches the code that consumes the option, so the 'correct but unreachable branch' defect its comment names is only hal
rejections.counterEvidence: The test covers the defect its comment actually names, and the assertion is not vacuous for it. Counter-evidence: The comment at scripts/quality-status.test.mjs:981-990 names the defect as the recorder rejecting `--areas`: 'passAreas() shipped correct and unreachable ... the recorder rejected the option before the branch could run, because the name was missing from the allowed set', and the added lines say 'The defect this replaced was preparePass() rejecting --areas from an inline set'. scripts/quality-status.mjs:1118 calls `rejectUnknownOptions(options, passOptionNames(kind))` as the first statement of `preparePass()`, before any other validation, so if `areas` were missing from that set the run would return 'unknown option: --areas' and the first assertion would fail. Running the test's own argv confirms the three outcomes discriminate: `['--areas','commands']` returns '--audit-metrics or --audit-metrics-file is required', `['--nosuchoption','x']` returns 'unknown option: --nosuchoption'. The 'correct but unreachable branch' the finding attributes to the comment is the rejection, not a silently ignored option.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:3443 -- `_refuseUnfittableStatusRow(cached, refreshed)` takes two whole field arrays, but its parameter names are the same two identifiers its only caller uses, twenty lines below, for two
rejections.counterEvidence: The stated impact is not material: it is a parameter-naming and comment-placement concern, and the concrete failure mode claimed is refuted by the code as written. Counter-evidence: The finding claims a reviewer 'will bind the names to the single BL_TIME field and conclude the guard measures one field's text ... i.e. that the guard is dead'. _rowWidth is defined immediately above the guard at js/display.js:3439-3441 as `function _rowWidth(fields) { return fields.reduce((total, { text }) => total + text.length, 0); }`, so both call sites inside the guard body (`_rowWidth(refreshed)`, `_rowWidth(cached)`) show on the same screen that the arguments are field lists, not single fields. No scrolling to the call site is needed, and the guard cannot be read as dead. Behavior is unchanged either way.

rejections.summary: js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1191 -- `d.consumed` carries two unrelated contracts -- C's `bp - origbp` bookkeeping and the port-only "the player typed a qualifier" boundary signal -- and neither comment mentions the o
rejections.counterEvidence: The omission is correct rather than accidental, the guard order makes it harmless, and both claimed failure scenarios are refuted by adjacent code. Counter-evidence: cnt cannot belong to a list of 'fields that must still equal their readobjnam_init() value': js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1270-1271 (C objnam.c:4928-4929) runs `if (!d.cnt) d.cnt = 1;` unconditionally before requireUnqualifiedWish() is called at 1275, so the init value 0 is always overwritten and any such test would refuse every wish. The first claimed misreading ('counted wishes are already supported') requires ignoring the d.consumed test that is the first line of the same function the field list belongs to. The second sub-claim is wrong on its own terms: a leading count IS one of readobjnam_preparse()'s arms (objnam.c:3984-3990, the `digit(*d->bp)` branch), so the message 'the "2" qualifier' sends the reader to preparse, the correct block, not to the wrong one.

Ending events: the painted wish prompt with its keystroke echoes, and prinv()'s inventory-letter line for the created object. The running game executes both; two development sessions replay them, moving 676 to 726 of 7,765 screens.

The trace covered state and random-number order and enumerated six draw sites inside the parse chain. It also corrected the range own account twice: SCR_MAIL sits inside #ifdef MAIL_STRUCTURES, which this pass reported as defined by no config or patch -- wrong, as the next pass found: include/global.h:430 defines it unconditionally -- and four comments stated something the source does not.
readiness.completeness: Two known divergences remain inside the boundary and are filed rather than left silent: a wished-for holy water loses its blessing, because the port reaches POT_WATER by a route that does not set d.blessed or d.iscursed; and wishymatch() folds case where C strsubst() does not.
