evidence: Counts: 17 raw, 15 deduplicated, 11 confirmed, 11 applied, 0 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 1 survivors of 14 mutants. The goal-closing correctness pass over wizard-mode-wish, run before the authorized holdout evaluation that .agents/review.md makes a review deadline. Four finders; concurrency and performance were not triggered. Eleven of fifteen findings confirmed and all eleven applied at 41cd43b, so the pass closes over its own fixes and leaves no correctness debt. Three were production divergences, two of them introduced by the range itself when 517f5fb stopped refusing a nonzero d.spesgn and a count: a requested enchantment reached the four types objnam.c breaks on, which is screen-visible on a towel, and the count guard read d.cnt before postparse1 settles it, so a plural wish ran the unverified stack line. The third withdrew a deferral this range had recorded: SCR_MAIL's arm is compiled in, because include/global.h:430 defines MAIL_STRUCTURES unconditionally, and the port's own objects table carries the row that proves it. The development score is identical at 782 of 7,765 screens before and after, since no development session wishes for a towel, an iron chain, a scroll of mail or a plural; the fresh wish matrix and the unit tests are the whole evidence for these fixes, which the pass prompt stated. One rejection is recorded as a partial: the count trace was correct and is fixed, and only its claim of an unported path was refuted.

optionalFinders.concurrency: not enabled: the range changes no shared mutable state beyond the single object under construction, and adds no asynchronous, reentrant, cancellation, retry or overlapping-lifecycle path
optionalFinders.performance: not enabled: the range adds three straight-line blocks inside a function that runs once per wish, with no unbounded work, worse complexity, hot-path traversal, material allocation or startup cost

productionDefects.summary: readobjnam()'s spe switch sent TOWEL, SKELETON_KEY, HEAVY_IRON_BALL and IRON_CHAIN to its default arm, which assigns d.spe, where objnam.c:5133-5146 gives TOWEL an arm assigning only d.wetness and the other three a bare break. Harmless while a nonzero d.spesgn was refused; 517f5fb stopped refusing it, so `+2 towel` produced spe 2 and js/objnam.js:304-305 renders that as "moist towel" where C prints "towel". Fix: Ported C's TOWEL arm and the bare-break group; rewrote the default arm's comment, which had claimed the default handles those four correctly.

The count guard ran before readobjnam_postparse1(), which is where d.cnt is settled: objnam.c:4408 doubles it for "pair of " and 4423-4433's makesingular() block raises it from 1 to 2. So "daggers" reached hold_another_object() with quan 2 and ran the stack line the port declares unverified, and the range widened the hole, since "the daggers" was refused at a00741d0 and admitted at 223e9079. Fix: Moved the refusal into requireSingleWishedObject(), after typfnd:, testing both operands objnam.c:5071-5083 reads. The count alone is the wrong test, because the tail leaves quan at 1 for a type that does not merge, so "pair of speed boots" must still be admitted. Reading oc_merge costs one draw, C's own lookup at C's position, with none after it.

The SCR_MAIL arm was absent, so a wished-for scroll of mail took the default arm and was created with the enchantment the wish asked for rather than objnam.c:5168-5174's spe 1. The deferral recorded in this range justified the absence on a false premise, that no config or patch defines MAIL_STRUCTURES. Fix: Ported the arm. include/global.h:430 defines MAIL_STRUCTURES unconditionally and global.h reaches the build through hack.h; include/objects.h gates the SCR_MAIL row on the same macro and js/objects.js carries it at SCR_MAIL = 364, which is the port's own proof the comparison build compiles both. The deferral is closed and its two narrative copies corrected in place.

The module header added in this range stated that js/objnam_readobjnam.js "calls back here for the naming helpers above". Neither file imports the other. Fix: Replaced the clause with the real dependency: that file reaches the objects[] tables through js/objects.js OBJ_NAME() and OBJ_DESCR(), and object construction through js/obj.js. Verified by grep in both directions.

mutation.finderConclusion: The one survivor, `&&` to `||` in the case SCALE_MAIL arm's own PM_GRAY_DRAGON..PM_YELLOW_DRAGON test, stands. The refusal in front of the parse chain admits no monster outside that range, so both operands hold for every wish that reaches the arm, and --whole-suite over all 146 test files did not kill it either. The line is kept because C has it and it begins doing work the moment that refusal widens. The finder's separate conclusion was that the surviving risk lay not in mutable operators but in lines no test reached at all: the `if (d.spesgn === 0)` branch, the uncursed arm's `blessed = false`, and 24 of the 27 UNSUPPORTED_WISH_FIELDS entries. All three now have oracles.

rejections.summary: js/obj.js:818 -- curseFreeObject() is labelled the port of mkobj.c curse() while the file already holds a function named curse() ported from the same C function, and the two disagree on a bag of holding.
rejections.counterEvidence: The premise is false: `grep -n "mkobj.c curse" js/obj.js` returns exactly one hit, line 818, on curseFreeObject(). The file-local `function curse(obj)` at line 810 carries no C-ref comment at all, before or after the range, and the two are not interchangeable ports of one routine. Do not reopen without showing two functions that both claim the same C ref.

rejections.summary: js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1184 -- UNSUPPORTED_WISH_FIELDS reads as the complete set of fields the typfnd: tail cannot accept, but four entries are also assigned inside postparse1, after the guard has run.
rejections.counterEvidence: The comment's first clause scopes the object precisely, to the fields readobjnam_preparse() and readobjnam_parse_charges() can set that still feed unported fine-tuning code. All four fields named are in fact set by readobjnam_preparse(), which is why they are listed. Do not reopen without a field in the object that preparse and parse_charges cannot set.

rejections.summary: js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1205 -- requireSimpleWishQualifiers() reads d.cnt before postparse1 doubles it, so the documented count boundary does not hold for the plural and "pair of" forms.
rejections.counterEvidence: Rejected on causality alone, and only for its stated impact: the claim that the port fails open on an unported path does not survive, because js/invent.js:2004-2061 ports hold_another_object()'s stack path rather than stopping on it. The underlying trace is correct and was confirmed as a separate finding at the same site, which this range fixes; this entry records that the failure mode is an unverified path, not an unported one.

rejections.summary: js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1393 -- the default arm of the ismnum(d.mntmp) switch is annotated only with the refused corpse, tin, egg, figurine and statue types, hiding that it is the normal path for an admitted dragon-named wish whose object is not scale mail.
rejections.counterEvidence: The reachability observation is correct and was reproduced -- readobjnam('gray dragon ring mail') returns RING_MAIL through that arm -- but the comment states nothing the source contradicts and never claims the arm is unreachable. It is prose completeness, which this pass is directed to leave to a clarity audit. Reopen in a clarity pass, not a correctness one.

readiness.boundary: Starts at the Enter that submits a wish line at the prompt wiz_wish() or #wizwish opened, and ends at prinv()'s inventory-letter line for the created object. The running game executes it: seed0360-wizard-world-tour steps 74, 98 and 129 type 'blessed +3 gray dragon scale mail', 'blessed +3 speed boots' and 'blessed amulet of life saving' after Ctrl-W, and the development score moved by exactly the 56 screens and 19 random-number calls those three wishes cover.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch reachable before the ending event was traced against nethack-c/upstream/src/objnam.c: the d.spesgn clamp at 5093-5120, the whole spe switch at 5121-5187, the ismnum(d.mntmp) block at 5191-5253, and the four BUC arms at 5255-5268, plus mkobj.c curse() at 1783 and blessorcurse(). The trace covered state and random-number order, and it corrected the range's own account three times: the spe switch was missing C's TOWEL and bare-break arms, the count guard read d.cnt before postparse1 settled it, and SCR_MAIL's arm was omitted on the false premise that MAIL_STRUCTURES is undefined. Stubs and partial implementations are identified: Luck has no owner, so the BUC arms are ported through their wizard operand alone; the non-wizard clamps at 5099-5117 and the long-worm-tail and werecreature rewrites at 5195-5203 are unported behind refusals.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Each reachable excluded branch stops before changing state, producing output, or spending a draw C does not spend at the same position: requireSimpleWishQualifiers() refuses the 27 unported fine-tuning fields before the parse chain draws at all, the monster-name and ' named ' refusals stand ahead of postparse3()'s lookup, and requireSingleWishedObject() and requireSimpleWishedObject() stop after that lookup -- the one draw C makes there -- and before mksobj(). The wish matrix at scripts/run-wizard-wish.mjs passes strictly over 21 recorded segments, and the development score is identical to the reviewed head, since no development session wishes for a towel, an iron chain, a scroll of mail or a plural.

A shared owner would add coupling or a cycle. Reopen when a neutral existing owner gains the exact stable contract.

rejections.summary: Surviving dogmove ordinary-pet admission operators represent untested admitted behavior.
rejections.counterEvidence: The fixed starting species cannot also be minions, priests, or vampshifters in a valid game, and the outer action boundary rejects the incompatible lifecycle shapes. Reopen with a production-reachable admitted starting-pet state carrying one of those identities.

rejections.summary: The pet_ranged_attk random-dependency guard needs gameplay coverage for one missing operation.
rejections.counterEvidence: Live gameplay always supplies the complete core random adapter; one missing rn2 or rnd is malformed test-harness injection and cannot arise from a seed, option, or input sequence. Reopen if a production caller can provide a partial adapter.

rejections.summary: Surviving mhitm starting-pet aggressor admission operators are distinguishable in the selected boundary.
rejections.counterEvidence: pet_ranged_attk() first admits the fixed tame starting species with edog state and is the only selected caller. Reopen if mattackm() gains another in-boundary caller or the caller guard changes.

rejections.summary: Surviving mhitm defender-speciality admission operators can be reached after target selection.
rejections.counterEvidence: find_targ() skips invisible and undetected targets for these pets, while score_targ() refuses minions, priests, shopkeepers, guards, leaders, and guardians before mattackm(). Reopen if target selection admits any such family.

rejections.summary: Surviving mhitm attack-array guard operators distinguish a valid starting-pet attack array.
rejections.counterEvidence: The generated immutable kitten, little-dog, and pony templates have exactly six AD_PHYS slots whose types are the expected bite or kick followed by AT_NONE. Reopen if generated templates or admitted species change.

rejections.summary: mattackm() needs an in-boundary one-null-argument case.
rejections.counterEvidence: The selected pet_ranged_attk() caller invokes mattackm() only after it has both a live aggressor and selected defender. A one-null call is a direct harness misuse. Reopen with a production caller that can pass one missing combatant.

concurrency.conclusion: Sequential planning and live replay isolate gb.bhitpos, gn, gs, gv, monster wake state, and mlstmv; the corrected retry fixture proves writes occur before a later refusal and no live state leaks.

performance.conclusion: The fixed eight rays and bounded line scans are source-required; the audit simplification removed temporary boolean arrays rather than adding work.

evidence: Counts: 20 raw, 18 deduplicated, 9 confirmed, 8 applied, 1 deferred, 9 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 3 survivors of 53 mutants. Full correctness pass over the apply-tool-command goal: apply.c apply_ok(), doapply()'s entry and its STETHOSCOPE and LOCK_PICK arms, insight.c ustatusline(), lock.c pick_lock() and cmd.c get_adjacent_loc(). Two findings were defects rather than test gaps, and both matter beyond this range. piousness() read C's pointer-NULL suffix test as a truthiness test, a mistranslation no differential could reach because no ported caller passes an empty suffix. run-test-suite.mjs reported success for a signal-killed test child, so every OOM-killed npm test has been reporting green; killing a real run's child gives exit 0 before the fix and 137 after. The five test findings closed the arms no key sequence reaches -- the steed, engulfed and cursed refusals, the cloud-of-vapor clause, set_bknown()'s change guard and heroDeaf()'s other two terms -- and killed two of the window's three mutation survivors. The ninth finding's convergence half is deferred as will-weld-ported-twice because it needs a file outside this range. Score unchanged at 1,027 of 7,765 screens and 116,207 of 610,816 PRNG values, as expected for latent and test-only fixes; suite 2,817 tests green.

productionDefects.summary: js/insight.js:251 piousness() translated C’s `if (suffix && ...)` pointer-NULL test as a JavaScript truthiness test, so an empty-string suffix — non-NULL and therefore true in C — took the opposite branch and lost the separating space C emits. Fixed to `suffix != null`. No ported caller passes an empty suffix, so nothing observable moved.

scripts/run-test-suite.mjs:16 assigned `process.exitCode = result.status` unconditionally, and spawnSync leaves `status` null for a signal-terminated child, which Node reads as 0. Every OOM-killed or externally killed `npm test` reported success. Verified end to end by killing a real run’s test child: the parent exited 0 before the fix and 137 after.

mutation.finderConclusion: The window run over the frozen range killed 50 of 53 first-wave mutants, and all three survivors sat in js/apply.js. They were routed to the test-quality finder, which traced each against source and confirmed two as genuinely unpinned behavior rather than unreachable lines: js/apply.js:184:26 (`u.usteed && u.dz > 0`) and the heroDeaf() disjunction. Both are killed by the cases this pass added — a re-run scoped to js/apply.js falls from 3 survivors to 1. The remaining survivor, js/apply.js:71:24 `!hallucination || !resistance` -> `&&`, is classified rather than fixed: it is a fail-fast guard against uninitialized u.uprops, and u_init together with every test fixture creates the HALLUC and HALLUC_RES entries as a pair, so no constructible state makes the two spellings disagree. The audit prompt described that survivor as sitting on the resistance disjunction at line 74; that was the orchestrator’s error, and line 74 is killed.

readiness.boundary: The hero types `a` and answers the object prompt. Two arms run to an observable end: the stethoscope prints insight.c ustatusline()’s one-line report, and the lock pick answers the doormask switch. Both execute in the running game — seed0016 steps 3-5 and seed0077 steps 19-20 — and seed0077 now matches all 33 of its screens.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch reachable before those two endings was traced against nethack-c/upstream: apply.c apply_ok() (4149-4210), doapply() (4213-4430), use_stethoscope() (313-424), insight.c ustatusline() (3401-3489) and piousness() (3234-3271), lock.c pick_lock() (356-656), cmd.c get_adjacent_loc() (3929-3953), engrave.c freehand(), and wield.c welded()/will_weld()/erodeable_wep(). The trace covered PRNG order specifically: use_stethoscope()’s cursed arm refuses ahead of C’s rn2(2), and pick_lock()’s usedtime resume refuses by name because only the unported picklock() occupation writes it. Stubs and explicit stops were enumerated: retouch_object() stops on obj.oartifact alone, on a derivation this pass re-checked, and every other switch arm and pick_lock() branch stops at a named error.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Each excluded branch refuses before changing state, consuming randomness, or producing output, and this pass added the cases pinning the three arms that previously had none. Two fresh differentials against the patched C reference matched call for call and screen for screen: 20 segments and 47,343 PRNG calls, and 10 segments and 24,545 PRNG calls.

rejections.summary: js/apply.js:158 (readability) — `use_stethoscope()` silently drops C's entry-time `interference` initializer, and the file's two header comments — which otherwise enumerate every covered guard and every stopping arm — never record that the omitted expression draws an `rn2()` *before* the three guards.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The header comment makes no completeness claim that this refutes. It says "Four arms between the direction prompt and confdir() stop rather than run" — a true statement about the four arms — and never claims to enumerate every unported expression in use_stethoscope(). More decisively, the expression it is faulted for omitting can never execute: C's initializer short-circuits on u.uswallow. Counter-evidence: apply.c:324-325 reads `boolean interference = (u.uswallow && is_whirly(u.ustuck->data) && !rn2(...))` — `&&` short-circuits, so no draw occurs unless u.uswallow is set. `grep -rn "uswallow" js/` shows exactly two writers in the whole port: js/u_init.js:161 `uswallow: false` and js/mon.js:260 `state.u.uswallow = 0;`. Nothing sets it truthy, so C and the port agree on all four exits in every state the running game can build. The finding also miscites the C location as a Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The claimed divergence requires u.uswallow to be truthy, and no code path in the port can make it so. With u.uswallow falsy, C's `&&` short-circuits before rn2(), so C draws nothing on all four exits and the port matches C call for call. The claim that the three guards "fail open" is therefore about a state the port cannot construct. Counter-evidence: apply.c:324-325 `(u.uswallow && is_whirly(u.ustuck->data) && !rn2(...))` — short-circuit `&&`. `grep -rn "uswallow" js/` returns writers only at js/u_init.js:161 (`uswallow: false`) and js/mon.js:260 (`state.u.uswallow = 0;`); every other hit is a read. The engulf machinery is unported wholesale — js/monmove.js:1820 records "release_hero(), u.ustuck — no hero-grabbing monster is reachable". The finding's secondary claim that the line-186 refusal is "late" relative to the stethoscope_seq write is also wrong: C performs the s Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

No site reads either value before writing it, so the finding's own premise ("unobservable today only Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/insight.js:843 (readability) — The comment above `UNPORTED_USTATUS_CONDITIONS` claims "The rows follow C's order inside ustatusline(), because C builds `info` by appending in that order", but three of C's `info` writers are checked after the whole array, so the file's actual stop order is not C's append order.

The comment at js/insight.js:849-850 states "So each stop can only fire early, never late", which is exactly the disposition of the WOUNDED_LEGS row that drops C's `!u.usteed` conjunct at insight.c:3438 — the stop is deliberately wider, and the commen Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/insight.js:862 (variable-trace) — UNPORTED_USTATUS_CONDITIONS lists FAST and INVIS before the u.utrap, u.uundetected and disguised checks, but C appends those fragments in the opposite order — contradicting the table's own comment that the rows follow C's order.

Every row and every following check throws the same UnsupportedEnlightenmentError and ends the segment, so the order changes only the diagnostic string. The remaining harm — a future porter converting stops into appends in the listed order — is speculative and contradicted by the port's governing rule to implement from the C function. Counter-evidence: js/insight.js:872-891: all five checks below the rows raise UnsupportedEnlightenmentError. The finding states it itself: "No output or PRNG effect today, because every row and every following check raises the same UnsupportedEnlightenmentError and ends the segment." AGENTS.md: "Implement from the C function, never from observed output."  ||  resolution refute: The validation is tautological. Asserting that a hero with u.utrap and FAST raises 'the trappe Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/insight.js:881 (correctness) — `ustatusline()` compares the raw `youmonst.m_ap_type` field against `M_AP_NOTHING`, but C's `U_AP_TYPE` is `gy.youmonst.m_ap_type & M_AP_TYPMASK` (`monst.h:71`); the unmasked read answers truthy whenever the `M_AP_F_DKNOWN` bit (0x8) is set on an otherwise-`M_AP_NOTHING` hero.

Counter-evidence: `grep -rn 'youmonst\.m_ap_type' nethack-c/upstream/src/` returns only whole-value assignments — hack.c:2960, potion.c:214, mhitu.c:676, timeout.c:397, polyself.c:226/782/1794/1867, teleport.c:495, monmove.c:611, eat.c:173/1219 — every one storing M_AP_NOTHING, M_AP_OBJECT or M_AP_MONSTER, never OR-ing a flag. The single C writer of the flag, pager.c:372 inside object_from_map(), operates on the `mtmp` it takes from the map ('there might be a mimic here posing as an object', pager.c:305), and the hero is never in the monster chain, so it can never be &gy.youmonst. On the port side `grep -rn 'm_ap_type' js/` shows js/insight.js:881 is the only mention of youmonst.m_ap_type at all — no writer exists. Masked and unmasked reads there Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/insight.js:881 (variable-trace) — ustatusline() reads `youmonst.m_ap_type` raw instead of through the canonical `M_AP_TYPE()` helper, so the M_AP_F_DKNOWN flag bit alone would make it report the hero as disguised.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: Same trace as finding 9: the masked and unmasked reads cannot disagree, and the supporting claim about the const.js helper's provenance is wrong. Counter-evidence: C sets M_AP_F_DKNOWN only at pager.c:372, on a map mimic obtained inside object_from_map() (pager.c:284-305); all twelve writers of gy.youmonst.m_ap_type assign whole appearance values, so U_AP_TYPE's mask is defensive for the hero and never load-bearing. js/ has no writer of youmonst.m_ap_type at all. rejections.summary: scripts/apply-stethoscope.test.mjs:310 (tests) — The `refreshes()` helper reports "no refresh happened" for any error other than `UnsupportedObjectOperationError`, so its two negative assertions pass whether the refresh was skipped or attempted and failed for an unrelated reason.

head: 049a95ae2bd0bb62fdbecd78c705d971059e6ff3
evidence: Counts: 17 raw, 15 deduplicated, 14 confirmed, 14 applied, 0 deferred, 1 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 434 survivors of 507 mutants. Full correctness pass over the monsters deferral sweep and the first options slice. Four production defects, all applied. The sharpest was count_bind_keys(), which counted every BIND statement where C's cmdbind_add() overwrites in place: two binds of one key printed '(2 currently set)' against C's 1, reproduced and then pinned by a fresh three-segment differential whose bind-keys row now agrees with C. The other three shared one habit rather than being three slips: each justified a hard-coded answer by reasoning from the port's own parser gap as though it were evidence about C, so the fixes replace guesses with refusals and teach parseNethackrc() to record the statements it drops. One finding's preferred fix was declined as out of scope and applied as a refusal instead: routing applyBooleanOption()'s fallback through booleanOptionStorage() would activate about 47 options the parser currently drops, each with a live consumer, which is a state-owner change belonging to implementation. Applying the findings also corrected two of them: C's parsebindings() recurses into the comma suffix before handling the head, so the reviewer's second bind case was wrong, and optlist.h's negateok column makes sortloot's negation a stop rather than an ignored argument. Development score identical before and after at 1,043 of 7,765 screens and 116,207 of 610,816 PRNG values; suite 2,856 green. The mutation figure needs its recorded caveat: 425 of 434 survivors are in the generated table, which the runner does not exclude.

productionDefects.summary: js/cmd.js count_bind_keys() counted every `bind` operation, where C’s cmdbind_add() overwrites in place and keeps one entry per key, so two BIND statements for one key printed "(2 currently set)" against C’s "(1 currently set)". Both loops now read the createCommandBindingModel() bindings, which replay with C’s semantics, and the model gained C’s userbind flag. This also fixed the command(param) spelling, which was counted as zero.

js/options.js booleanOptionValue() read a boolean through allopt[].addr while applyBooleanOption()’s fallback wrote flags[<lowercased name>], so any boolean whose C storage name differs was read from the wrong place. Fixed by refusing when the two disagree, covering 32 divergent spellings. The finding’s preferred fix, routing the write through booleanOptionStorage(), was declined: it would activate about 47 options the parser currently drops, each with a live consumer, which is a state-owner change needing new end-to-end cases and therefore implementation rather than an audit fix.

js/options.js count_menucolors(), msgtype_count() and count_autocompletions() returned hard-coded answers justified by the port’s own parser gap rather than by C. parseNethackrc() now records a dropped MENUCOLOR, MSGTYPE or AUTOCOMPLETE statement with C’s own prefix lengths, and each count stops on its own statement instead of guessing.

js/options.js dosetEntryFormat() hard-coded doset()’s padded layout on a false premise, that menu_tab_sep is wizard-mode-only. set_wizonly governs where doset() lists an option, not whether a config file may set it, so the tab-separated form is reachable. Now refused by name, with the comment corrected.

mutation.finderConclusion: The headline survivor count is an artifact and must not be read as a coverage figure. 425 of the 434 survivors are in js/optlist_data.js, the generated options table: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs selects sites from changed lines and does not exclude declared generated outputs, so it mutated 217 table entries whose correctness comes from check:options diffing them against the C source rather than from any test. That also explains the boolean kind’s 16-of-442 figure. The real survivor list was nine, all outside the table, and it was routed to the tests finder, which traced each. The audit fixes killed eight; one remains, js/command_bindings.js setBinding()’s restBinding default, classified rather than fixed because no call omitting the argument can bind Space: extcmdlist has no row with key 0x20, the alias table has none, and resetCommandBindings() touches only direction keys and their variants. The tooling gap is worth recording separately, because every future goal that generates a table will bury its real survivors the same way.

readiness.boundary: Two boundaries. For the monsters sweep, each resolved entry’s refusal, observable as a named stop rather than a silent skip or a bare TypeError. For the options slice, the hero types m then O and seven menu pages reach the screen; seed0007-rogue-snake-swamp advances from 20 to 36 of 302 screens, which the running game executes.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch reachable before those endings was traced against nethack-c/upstream: options.c doset(), doset_simple(), doset_add_menu(), longest_option_name(), term_for_boolean(), parsebindings() and the optfn_*(get_val) arms; optlist.h allopt[] with its negateok and valok columns; cfgfiles.c’s dispatch table and match_optname(); cmd.c cmdbind_add(), cmdbind_remove(), reset_commands() and count_bind_keys(); mon.c minliquid_core(); wield.c will_weld() and mwelded(); worn.c which_armor(). The trace covered PRNG order: the menu draws no random number, and the development total is unchanged across the range. Stubs and explicit stops were enumerated: the pick loop, reset_needed_visuals(), doset_simple_menu() and get_option_value() all stop by name.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside either boundary. Each excluded branch refuses before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output, and the fixes added refusals where the port had been guessing from its own gaps. Every new refusal was checked against all 34 development sessions, 45 nethackrc values, and none carries a statement or spelling any of them covers, which is why the development score is identical before and after. A fresh differential for the fixes recorded three segments against the patched C reference: 7,023 PRNG calls, 30 screens and 30 cursors, all matching, with the bind-keys row reading (4 currently set) in C and in the fixed port where the pre-fix port printed 5.

evidence: Counts: 19 raw, 16 deduplicated, 14 confirmed, 14 applied, 0 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 851 survivors of 977 mutants. Full correctness pass over the options goal's pick application, closed over its own fixes. Five production defects, all applied. The sharpest is a relapse: reglyph_darkroom() threw a bare Error outside failClosedCommandRefusals(), so an ordinary OPTIONS=!color plus one menu pick aborted the whole segment and discarded every screen already matched - the same failure class the monsters sweep had just removed from dosounds and artifactTouchable, reappearing in new code and reproduced end to end by the reviewer. The others: costly_spot()'s return discarded, collapsing C's if/else and dropping a branch; oc_to_str() called on a raw pickup_types string without the guard the menu applies to the same field; the ', with exceptions' clause decided from a list the port never populates; and setBooleanOptionValue() leaving a stale parse shadow that tripped the guard the previous pass added. Two findings mattered more than their labels: the tests for the relaxed vision_recalc() guard and the new vpline() hook asserted almost nothing, and those are the only two changes in the range that no recorded session pins. The fixes corrected the reviewers twice - finding [11] proposed deleting a call that is not inert once [10] is fixed, and [10]'s own proposed validation was run and found not to discriminate, so it was pinned by a unit test instead of a recipe that would have proved nothing. Development score identical per session across all 33, at 1,056 of 7,765 screens and 116,602 of 610,816 PRNG values; suite 2,903 green. The mutation headline is noise for the third pass running: 826 of 851 survivors sit in a declared generated table the runner does not exclude.

productionDefects.summary: js/display.js reglyph_darkroom() threw a bare Error, which failClosedCommandRefusals() does not list, so an ordinary `OPTIONS=!color` or `!dark_room` plus one menu pick aborted the whole segment and discarded every screen already matched, instead of stopping on the last match. Reproduced end to end by the reviewer. This is the same failure class the monsters sweep removed from dosounds and artifactTouchable, reappearing in new code. Fixed with a named UnsupportedGlyphRepairError declared beside the existing UnsupportedStatusRefreshError in the same file and listed in js/cmd.js, so failClosedCommand() rewraps it into the command boundary runSegment() already admits. The guard stayed inside reglyph_darkroom() rather than being hoisted, so C’s other two call sites keep it.

js/insight.js discarded costly_spot()’s return value, collapsing C’s if/else at insight.c:808-819 into straight-line code and silently dropping the "temporarily disabled while inside the shop" branch of the autopickup enlightenment line.

js/insight.js called oc_to_str() on flags.pickup_types without the raw-string guard the options menu applies to the same field, so a nethackrc setting pickup_types turned ^X into unreadable output. Now refused by name.

js/insight.js decided C’s ", with exceptions" clause from state.ga.apelist, which the port never populates, so the clause could never appear. Fixed by refusing on the unported AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION statement rather than by porting the parser: autopickup_exception joins UNPORTED_CONFIG_STATEMENTS and count_apes() refuses on the same input, so no deferred work was needed.

js/options.js setBooleanOptionValue() wrote only allopt[].addr, leaving parseNethackrc()’s raw copy under flags.<name> stale, which tripped the consistency guard the previous pass added on the next menu build. Fixed by deleting the parse shadow when the two storage names differ. The affected set was enumerated programmatically at 43 boolean options and each grepped for a real reader; two hits, neither on the interactive path.

mutation.finderConclusion: The headline survivor count is an artifact for the third pass running and must not be read as coverage: 826 of the 851 survivors are in js/optlist_data.js, a declared generated output whose correctness comes from check:options diffing it against the C source rather than from any test, because scripts/mutate-sites.mjs selects sites from changed lines and does not exclude such outputs. Prior runs on this goal saw the same distortion at 425:9 and 827:25. The real list was 25, and 21 of those clustered in js/options.js 3298-3365, choose_classes_menu()’s bounds arithmetic; the tests finder was asked to decide whether that density meant an unpinned region or equivalent mutants. The audit fixes then ran their own mutation over the changed lines and reported 0 survivors of 14, having killed four that could have been excused as unreachable — including both menuinvertmode arms in js/windows.js — with direct unit tests rather than arguments.

readiness.boundary: The hero types m then O, commits nine picks from the seven-page menu, and the eight booleans plus the pickup_types class menu apply. seed0007-rogue-snake-swamp advances from 36 to 49 of 302 screens, which the running game executes.

head: eed732b3175f7b50bbe7c92dc92c4a0a881fa462
evidence: Counts: 18 raw, 14 deduplicated, 12 confirmed, 12 applied, 0 deferred, 1 rejected, 1 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 20 mutants. Full correctness pass over the twoweapon-command goal, closed over its own fixes. Its sharpest finding was against the goal record rather than the code: the boundary and detail cited dotwoweapon() as 845-905 and can_twoweapon() as 761-833, where the spans are 843-864 and 760-804. Line 905 is the head of untwoweapon(), so the bad span attributed untwoweapon() and drop_uswapwep() to this goal - the two functions its own open deferral records as unported, which a later selector would have read as done. The other production defects: the ADMITTED_COMMANDS comment named M-2 as the command's own key when its key is X and M-2 the alias; obj.h carried() became a sixth duplicate port and was converged; and two live fail-closed boundaries were unpinned, the newly reachable Dual-weps status field and both update_inventory() calls, the first now pinned by a fresh C recording rather than an assertion. Applying the findings corrected three of them, one materially: the reviewer justified an unreachable arm by saying no role starts with a launcher in a wield slot, but the human Ranger takes a dagger primary and a bow secondary; the arm is unreachable because wield.c:765 refuses that role monster one arm earlier, verified by replaying all thirteen roles. Score bit-identical per session at 1,081 of 7,765 screens and 116,787 of 610,816 PRNG values, which is the required outcome for a range no development session can reach; the evidence is the differential, now fourteen fresh C segments at 42,032 PRNG calls and 243 screens. Mutation was clean for the first time in this sequence - 20 of 20 killed, no generated-table noise - so the tests finder judged whether tests pin behavior instead of triaging survivors, which produced five of the twelve findings.

productionDefects.summary: The goal record’s own C citations were wrong, and the error was material. `boundary` and `detail` gave `dotwoweapon() (845-905)` and `can_twoweapon() (761-833)`; the spans are 843-864 and 760-804. Line 905 is the head of `untwoweapon()`, so the bad span attributed `untwoweapon()` and `drop_uswapwep()` to this goal — the two functions the open deferral `twoweapon-unreachable-refusal-arms` records as NOT ported. A later selector reading the boundary would have concluded they were done. Corrected in ce65d2f by direct edit, since goal-log.mjs offers no amend for an open goal’s boundary.

The ADMITTED_COMMANDS comment said `#twoweapon`’s "own key is M-2". Its own key is `X` (cmd.c:1913, extcmdlist row 0x58); M-2 is the alias commands_init() adds at cmd.c:2776, and the port binds both. A reader auditing the boundary would have concluded `X` was already handled.

`obj.h carried()` became a second live named port: `js/obj.js:675` exported, added by this range, beside the module-private `js/eat.js:598` with an identical body. The sixth duplicate port found in this repository in two days. Converged on js/obj.js, which obj.h names; js/eat.js repointed and the private copy deleted, with the development score verified bit-identical per session.

Two live fail-closed boundaries were unpinned: `set_twoweap(true, …)` makes js/display.js’s "Dual-weps" status field reachable for the first time, and both `update_inventory({ state })` calls in dotwoweapon() could be deleted with the whole suite still green, though under `OPTIONS=perm_invent` each is the port’s only stop. The status field was pinned by a new C recording rather than a unit assertion.

mutation.finderConclusion: The first clean mutation signal of this goal sequence: 20 of 20 killed, no survivors, no timeouts, and no declared generated output in range, so none of the distortion that made the three previous passes report 425, 827 and 826 meaningless survivors applies here. With no survivor list to triage, the tests finder was asked instead to sample-verify the claim that eighteen mutation-invisible lines had each been broken with their covering test observed to fail. That reframing produced five of the twelve findings, all of them gaps a survivor list could not have shown: an untested refusal-class registration, a matrix test re-asserting a constant copied from a few lines away, an unpinned `state.flags.female` guard, and a setuwep test covering three of its expression’s terms. The audit fixes added no mutable site of their own, so their evidence runs the other way: each new assertion was shown killing a specific mutant on already-committed lines.

readiness.boundary: The hero issues `#twoweapon`. On the success path the command prints "You begin two-weapon combat.", sets `u.twoweap`, refreshes inventory and spends or does not spend the move on one `rnd(20) > ACURR(A_DEX)`; on a refusal it prints one of seven messages and spends nothing. `seed0107-samurai-twoweapon-enhance` executes the success path in the running game, advancing from 15 to 40 of 98 screens.

The trace covered PRNG order: the command draws exactly one random number on the success path and none on any refusal, which the differential confirms.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Three arms stay unported with derivations recorded in code and tracked as `twoweapon-unreachable-refusal-arms`, and applying the findings corrected one of those derivations: the reviewer said no role starts with a launcher in a wield slot, but the human Ranger takes a dagger primary and a bow secondary (u_init.c:124-128). The arm is still unreachable, for the different reason that wield.c:765 refuses the Ranger and Caveman role monsters one arm earlier — verified by replaying all thirteen roles. The differential grew from twelve to fourteen fresh C segments: 42,032 PRNG calls, 243 screens, all matching.

head: 5168910fede17e2588c598d9673dd003f24c4665
evidence: Counts: 21 raw, 20 deduplicated, 15 confirmed, 15 applied, 0 deferred, 5 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 11 mutants. Full correctness pass over three goals' work: chat-command, commands-deferral-sweep-2, and hero-combat slices 1 and 2. Four mandatory finders, 21 raw findings, 20 after deduplication, 15 confirmed by independent adversarial adjudication, 5 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. All 15 applied across five Audit-fix-for commits. Five were production defects, the sharpest being a refusal placed after a random-number draw and a state change in js/hack.js overexertion(), and an over-broad two-weapon refusal in js/uhitm.js do_attack() that was discarding three calls a turn from seed0107. Two findings were the eighth and ninth duplicate ports found in five days. Six were test defects, including a term whose deletion left all 3,000 tests green. Development score 1,102 of 7,765 screens and 116,830 of 610,816 calls, the only movement being seed0107 gaining the three calls the two-weapon refusal discarded.

productionDefects.summary: js/hack.js overexertion() refused both arms of hack.c overexert_hp() (3035-3047), where only the `uhp <= 1` arm prints, exercises Constitution and calls fall_asleep(). The `uhp > 1` arm is two portable statements. Worse, the refusal sat after gethungry() had spent rn2(20) and mutated u.uhunger, so a branch C walks past ended the segment after a draw and a state change. The common arm is now ported and only `uhp <= 1` refuses. Unreachable today through any admitted command, so it closed on authorized substituted evidence, tracked as overexertion-arm-has-no-fresh-differential.

js/uhitm.js do_attack() refused on u.twoweap alone, where uhitm.c:528 reaches unported code only when can_twoweapon() is additionally false. A two-weaponing hero walking into a hostile monster ended the segment three draws and one screen before C does. This is the only finding in the pass that moved the development score: seed0107-samurai-twoweapon-enhance gained the rn2(19), rnd(20) and rn2(3) the over-broad refusal discarded, 2842 to 2845 of 2902 calls, with every other session byte-identical.

js/uhitm.js attack_checks() read C’s Hallucination as intrinsic-or-extrinsic, dropping the !Halluc_resistance factor youprop.h:120 requires. That is a third distinct reading of one macro, in a file whose own is_safemon() 57 lines above reads it correctly. With hallucination intrinsic set and resistance active, C puts up the paranoid "Really attack?" prompt and the port did not. Reported independently by the correctness, readability and tests finders as findings 8, 9 and 12; one defect, fixed once.

display.h vobj_at() and engrave.c u_wipe_engr() each gained a second JavaScript home in this range: the new js/display.js vobj_at() against the pre-existing visibleObjectAt() at js/monmove.js, and the new js/engrave.js u_wipe_engr() against the statements inlined in js/allmain.js maybeWipeHeroEngraving(). The eighth and ninth duplicate ports found in five days. Both converged onto the file named for the C file, with the development score verified identical session by session across the convergence.

js/uhitm.js attack_checks() called engulfing_u(mtmp) against the module-global `game` while threading `state` through every other read in the same function, so a reader reasonably treating the function as state-pure would be wrong about its first guard.

mutation.finderConclusion: No survivors across the five audit-fix commits, but the number understates the work: two mutants survived the whole suite rather than one wave and needed new assertions written for them. js/monmove.js onscary()’s Elbereth disjunct had no test at all for its displaced-image and guarded-pile arms, and js/const.js engulfing_u()’s && survived flipping to || because nothing distinguished being held from being swallowed. The five test findings this pass confirmed are the same shape: finding 13 showed that deleting `!is_undead(mtmp.data)` from js/uhitm.js left all 3,000 tests green, and finding 15 that the known_hitum() test passed dieroll into the uattk slot, so it could not detect the parameter-order defect it existed to pin. Mutation score alone would have reported this range as healthy.

readiness.boundary: The range eed732b3..5168910 holds three goals: chat-command (sounds.c dotalk() and dochat() to the wall reply), commands-deferral-sweep-2 (hack.c end_running() and nomul() merged from two disagreeing ports into one, plus a fail-closed backstop at the two live domove() call sites), and hero-combat slices 1 and 2 (domove() reordered so the attack precedes test_move() as hack.c:2798 precedes 2843, then the hostile melee attempt ported down to the miss). The development score at the frozen head was 1,102 of 7,765 screens and 116,827 of 610,816 calls with 3 of 33 sessions matching; after the fixes it is 116,830, the whole movement in seed0107.
readiness.sourceReview: Four mandatory finders ran at full mode: correctness, readability-risk, test-quality and variable-flow. Neither optional finder was enabled, and both omissions were reasoned rather than skipped: the range adds no unbounded or amplified work, and source-required melee iteration does not trigger the performance finder on its own; the port is single-threaded replay, and although the reorder moved two awaits and the backstop added error handling around one, neither introduces overlapping work, cancellation or retries. Each finding was adversarially verified against the C source by an independent adjudicator applying evidence, causality and resolution checks; 15 of 20 deduplicated findings survived, 5 were rejected with counter-evidence, none went unverified and no warnings were raised. The random-number order of the melee path was re-derived from uhitm.c, eat.c and attrib.c rather than taken from the diff’s own comments, because the order originally supplied to the implementing agent was wrong.
readiness.completeness: All 15 confirmed findings are applied across five commits carrying Audit-fix-for: 5168910. Every new test was observed failing first by breaking the line it covers and restoring it, thirteen breakages in all, each named in its commit. Two items were reported rather than silently handled and are recorded in the ledger: overexertion-arm-has-no-fresh-differential, where no admitted command can raise the hero past Stressed encumbrance so the fresh differential AGENTS.md requires cannot be recorded yet and substituted evidence was authorized; and pickup-burden-option-has-no-parser, a live bug outside this range found while attempting that recording, where js/options.js has no parseoptions() arm for pickup_burden so the option silently becomes stricter than its default rather than looser. One trigger was deliberately not run: /simplify-codebase applies to artifact.c artifact_light()’s five ports, which is tracked as artifact-light-ported-five-times and scheduled into the slice that consumes the function.

evidence: Counts: 17 raw, 17 deduplicated, 8 confirmed, 8 applied, 0 deferred, 9 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 60 survivors of 220 mutants. Full correctness pass over hero-combat slice 3, 1,439 changed production lines in one commit, plus the five audit-fix commits of the previous pass. Four mandatory finders; 17 raw, 17 deduplicated, 8 confirmed, 9 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. All 8 applied across two Audit-fix-for commits. No production behavior defect was confirmed, against five in the previous pass: the implementation held and the tests did not. Six of the eight were tests pinning nothing, each naming a term deletable with all 3,072 tests green, which matches the slice's own 68-of-144 mutation survivors. The one production fix restored hmon_hitmon()'s dropped doreturn guard, write-only until artifact_hit() lands two slices out and would have had its abort discarded. Applying the findings corrected three of them against the C source. Development score 1,102 of 7,765 screens and 116,833 of 610,816 calls, unchanged by the fixes.

productionDefects.summary: js/uhitm.js hmon_hitmon() copied all 27 struct _hitmon_data fields, including doreturn and retval, while dropping C's guards that read them, so both fields were write-only. Harmless at the time because no ported helper sets them, and a time bomb for the slices that follow: artifact_hit() sets doreturn on DEADMONSTER(mon) to abort before damage lands, and the abort would have been discarded, subtracting damage from a monster already dead and then running _pet, _splitmon, _msg_hit and wakeup() on a corpse. The finding asked for three guards; the source gave one. C's guards at uhitm.c:1090-1091 and 1418-1419 are the last statements of their own functions, so the guarded return reaches exactly what the fall-through reaches, and both are no-ops in C. The guard at 1806-1807 was restored alone, with the other two documented as absent by derivation. Mutation confirms it is live: flipping the doreturn initializer to true now fails tests, where at dc31f03 it did not.

mutation.finderConclusion: The audit-fix diff itself holds no mutable site: 32 lines in scope, 0 sites, 0 mutants, because it is 26 comment lines plus one restored guard statement. The figure that matters is the before-and-after over js/uhitm.js at the same kinds: 220 mutants, 62 survivors at dc31f03 and 60 after, so two previously-surviving mutants became killable. One is the doreturn initializer, killed by the restored production guard; the other is the first && of uhitm.c:1467's condition, killed by the new two-handed strength test, where JavaScript precedence turns a && b && c into a || (b && c) and the one-handed row lands two points where it expects one. The other five test findings kill nothing, and that is structural rather than a shortfall: they name term deletions, while the mutator's site set is operators and literals, so dropping a whole disjunct is outside what it can express. That is the same gap the previous pass demonstrated from the other direction, where a range scored 253 of 220 mutants killed while six real test defects sat in it. The 60 remaining first-wave survivors cluster in the _hitmon_data initializers, the first_weapon_hit() guard whose body is empty so nothing it decides is observable, and mhitm_knockback()'s return statements whose value hmon_hitmon discards; most look structurally unkillable, and recording that here should spare the next pass re-deriving it.

readiness.boundary: The range 5168910..dc31f03 holds one slice of the hero-combat goal, 4d2a9cb at 1,439 changed production lines, plus the five audit-fix commits of the previous pass. A hero move into a hostile now lands a blow that does not kill: uhitm.c hmon() (817-834) and hmon_hitmon() (1752-1935) with eleven helpers, known_hitum()'s hit arm, the weapon.c damage math, and artifact.c shade_glare() and artifact_light(). The development score is 1,102 of 7,765 screens and 116,833 of 610,816 calls with 3 of 33 sessions, unchanged by the fixes.
readiness.sourceReview: Four mandatory finders at full mode: correctness, readability-risk, test-quality and variable-flow. Neither optional finder ran; the range adds no unbounded work and the port is single-threaded replay. Every finding was adversarially verified against C by an independent adjudicator applying evidence, causality and resolution checks: 8 of 17 survived, 9 were rejected with counter-evidence, none went unverified and no warnings were raised. No production behavior defect was confirmed, against five in the previous pass over the two slices before this one. Applying the findings corrected three of them against the source: two of the three requested doreturn guards are no-ops in C; a gem cannot complete the swing, because objects.h:1516-1520 gives every gem oc_skill of -P_SLING so is_ammo() holds and the gem takes the ranged arm; and the ternary named by the barehands finding is redundant with special_dmgval()'s own which_armor() lookup, proven by deleting it and running the whole suite green.
readiness.completeness: All 8 confirmed findings are applied across two commits carrying Audit-fix-for: dc31f03. Every new assertion was observed failing first by deleting the term it covers and restoring it, with the deletions and their results recorded in a script rather than asserted in prose. Six of the eight were tests that pinned nothing, each naming a term deletable with all 3,072 tests green, which is what the slice's own 68-of-144 survivor count had been saying. Writing them surfaced a further defect the pass had not found: the old barehands test passed its bounds assertion because game.twohits was undefined, so special_dmgval() received an empty mask, rather than because the target ignored silver. Citation drift in js/uhitm.js is systematic at roughly +4 in the hmon_hitmon_do_hit region and +9 in dmg_recalc; the new comments use verified numbers and the pre-existing ones are left for a clarity pass, which is outside audit-fix scope.

productionDefects.summary: xkilled()'s pit arm refused on mon.c:3514's outer guard alone, where C acts only when a boulder is present: 3514-3522 sets nocorpse from sobj_at(BOULDER, x, y) and burycorpse from m_carrying(mtmp, BOULDER), and does nothing at all when neither holds. A refusal wider than the C condition it stands for, and the third of that shape found in this subsystem. It could not fire today, because PIT sits in UNPORTED_TRAP_EFFECTS, but it would have become a live wrong stop the moment mintrap()'s pit arm landed, aborting a segment on an ordinary early-level kill that C completes. A test at scripts/mon-kill.test.mjs pinned the wider behavior, so the defect was held in place by its own coverage. Applying it corrected both findings that reported it, which proposed contradictory fixes: neither arm needs an unported operation, so both flags are ported and xkilled() gains no refusal. The flags remain unreachable, but for a reason neither finding gave -- mondead() stops on both boulder states before xkilled() reads either, at fill_pit()'s settling refusal and flooreffects()'s boulder-landing refusal, and both stops sit above the rn2(6) treasure draw.

mutation.finderConclusion: Two boolean survivors, both the newly ported pit flags at js/mon.js:1932-1933, neither of which has a reachable reader while mondead() stops above them. The worker declined to manufacture a stale-coordinates fixture that would have killed one, on the ground that the running game cannot produce a monster killed off its own coordinates and the row would imply the arm is live -- the right call, and the same judgement the mutation instrument cannot make for itself. Adding the missing no-trap row killed the && to || mutant on t && is_pit(t.ttyp), which the previous test comment had claimed to cover and did not. This is the third pass in a row where the mutation figure and the test quality point in different directions; js/exper.js:178 remains a known false survivor tracked as mutate-sites-reports-a-false-survivor.

productionDefects.summary: The merge admission in preflight_dropx() tested lamplit, timed and globby on the object being dropped, while invent.c merged() reads those fields on the floor pile member it absorbs. mergable() forces lamplit to match and short-circuits on globby, so two of the three were accidentally symmetric; timed was not, because mergable() rejects a timer mismatch only for EGG and revivable CORPSE. The finder proved it by execution rather than argument: the object left inventory, place_object() ran, and only then did UnsupportedObjectOperationError fire. The orchestrator recommended the fix that supplies the missing operations from objectGenerationHooks(); that rested on a false premise, since it supplies stopObjectTimers but neither mergeLightSources nor absorbGlob, both of which are unported C in light.c and mkobj.c. The applied fix walks the floor pile and refuses any member mergable() would accept that carries one of the three fields, which also covers the wish path in js/zap.js because it shares the admission.

evidence: Counts: 21 raw, 16 deduplicated, 13 confirmed, 13 applied, 0 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 4 survivors of 36 mutants. Full correctness pass over the pickup-command goal: the , command for a square holding at most one takeable object. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered, since the range adds only source-required iteration and no shared-state or overlapping-lifecycle change. The finding that mattered is the burden gate: the , command routed through a limit computed with Math.max(near_capacity(), flags.pickup_burden), and an rc file leaves that option as raw text, so the limit was NaN and the refusal silently disappeared rather than widening. It was reachable only through an option no scored session sets, which is why two slices, a mutation run and 17 recorded C segments all passed over it, and why the variable-trace finder rather than the score found it. Tests led again: 5 of 13 confirmed were test gaps, the seventh consecutive pass where tests lead or tie. Three of those gaps sat in work this session produced, including nine recorded segments that npm test never replayed. The score is unchanged at 1254 screens and 117940 calls across the fixes, as a set that changes no scored behavior should be. The pass also opened one new ledger entry, addinv-burden-read-accepts-unparsed-option, for the same read one level down in js/invent.js, which is outside this range.

productionDefects.summary: preflightPickupObjects() in js/pickup.js computed its burden limit as Math.max(near_capacity(), flags.pickup_burden ?? MOD_ENCUMBER), the gate the `,` command newly routes through. parseNethackrc() has no arm for pickup_burden and keeps an unported option's raw text in flags[<option name>], which for this option is the field the parsed value would occupy, so OPTIONS=pickup_burden:overloaded leaves a string there. Math.max() then returns NaN and calc_capacity(...) > NaN is false for every value, so the refusal disappeared rather than widening: the port lifted the object where pickup.c:1759-1777 stops at a ynq() prompt. Fail-open, and invisible to the development score because no scored session sets the option. Fixed with a Number.isInteger() guard that refuses an unusable value before the limit is computed, keeping the boundary closed until js/options.js gains the parse arm. js/invent.js addinvCore1() holds the same read one level down, where the string makes a comparison false rather than deleting a refusal; that file is outside this range and is recorded as the deferral addinv-burden-read-accepts-unparsed-option.

Stone_resistance had two differently-written owners once this range added the second. js/pickup.js u_safe_from_fatal_corpse()'s st_resists arm reads the macro as (intrinsic || extrinsic), while js/invent.js activeStoneResistance(), read by will_feel_cockatrice(), added a `&& !blocked` term. youprop.h:65 defines Stone_resistance as (HStone_resistance || EStone_resistance) and carries no blocked term, unlike Blind() at :103 which does, so the invent.js copy was the wrong one. Renamed to Stone_resistance for the macro it ports and the term dropped. No behavior moved: nothing in js/ writes uprops[STONE_RES].blocked, and the development score is identical. The finder proposed one shared owner called from both files; the narrower fix was applied instead, because a per-file local property reader is the established idiom here -- a dozen files carry their own propertyActive() -- and the defect was the divergence, not the two call sites.

rejections.summary: A correctness finding that js/hack.js:2154's `if (ret >= 0)` is unpinned and its surviving mutant semantically inequivalent, filed as a correctness defect.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator refuted the category, not the observation: js/hack.js:2154 reproduces hack.c:3884 `if ((ret = pickup_checks()) >= 0) return ret ? ECMD_TIME : ECMD_OK;` exactly, and the shipped code answers C's result on both squares the finding named. The only substantiated problem is absent test coverage, which the confirmed test-category finding at the same site reports; filing it twice double-counts one gap. The coverage gap was fixed. Do not reopen as a correctness defect without a source divergence in the shipped line, as opposed to a missing test.

rejections.summary: A readability finding that preflightPickupObjects()'s header overclaims by saying it holds everything C decides inside pickup_object(), lift_object(), pick_obj() and addinv() that can refuse, while shop billing is refused elsewhere.
rejections.counterEvidence: pickup.c:1893-1941 pick_obj() contains no refusal at all: it computes robshop, calls addtobill() and remote_burglary(), and always returns addinv()'s result. There is therefore nothing C decides in pick_obj() that can refuse for the header to be missing. The port's shop stop is a port-side inability to bill, not a C decision, so the premise that one C refusal is handled in two places does not hold. Do not reopen without naming an early return or refusal inside pick_obj() in the C source.

rejections.counterEvidence: The sentence immediately before the limits list (js/pickup.js) already scopes the two arms by name -- autopick()'s, used by a level teleport arrival, and the `,` command's, for a square holding exactly one object it is allowed to take -- so the one-object restriction is attributed to `,` one line above. The list reads as the union of pickup()'s refusals, and other items in it are equally arm-specific in the opposite direction. Do not reopen without a reading that survives the preceding sentence.

evidence: Counts: 15 raw, 14 deduplicated, 11 confirmed, 10 applied, 1 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 3 survivors of 34 mutants. Full correctness pass over the two force-fight-command slices. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered, since the range adds no hot-path or resource cost and no overlapping-lifecycle work. The pass earned its place on risk rather than size: 483 changed lines, but they replaced a single-prefix arm with a general prefix loop, corrected three lines that had been latently wrong for as long as nothing set context.forcefight, and made a representation decision outside C. Two production defects were applied and one deferred, and the first applied one was introduced by the range itself: moving unmap_object() back to C's position put a refusal below it, so a stop fired after map memory and the display buffer had been rewritten. That is the same late-refusal failure mode an earlier pass in this repository found, arriving by a different route -- an ordering fix that was right for the arms C completes and wrong for the one the port refuses. The second, a bare Error in unmap_invisible(), would have escaped the segment rather than ending it, and its stated reason had been falsified by this very range porting unmap_object(). Tests led again: 5 of 11 confirmed were test gaps, the eighth consecutive pass where tests lead or tie, and four of the five were invisible to the mutation run because they sit on ordering or on lines with no mutable site. One further gap the pass created rather than found is recorded separately as parsed-retry-forcefight-restore-untested. The score is unchanged at 1294 screens and 118144 calls across the fixes.

productionDefects.summary: js/hack.js domove_fight_empty() refused terrain with no remembered appearance after unmap_object() and newsym() had already run. Slice 2 introduced this by moving unmap_object() back to C's position (hack.c:2280-2285) without noticing that C's seenv test at 2302 sits below it because C completes that arm rather than refusing it. The port refuses, so putting the refusal where C puts the test meant a stop that had rewritten map memory and the display buffer, ending the segment on a screen the port had already diverged from -- the late-refusal failure mode this repository has found before. Fixed by hoisting the seenv/IS_STWALL/SDOOR/SCORR test above unmap_object(), guarded by the already-computed `solid`, with a comment stating that this is the one place the port deliberately departs from C's order and only on the arm it refuses. Pinned by asserting that the square's remembered_glyph and the top line are both untouched after the refusal.

js/display.js unmap_invisible() refused with a bare Error whose stated reason was that unmap_object() is not ported. This range ported unmap_object(), so the reason had ceased to exist, and a bare Error is not one of the classes js/cmd.js failClosedCommandRefusals() converts, so it would have escaped the segment as a hard failure and discarded the matching prefix instead of ending on it. Fixed by raising UnsupportedMapMemoryError and naming the blocker that actually remains: map_invisible(), the only writer of the 'I' marker the arm clears, is unported, so the arm has never run. The TRUE arm was deliberately left unwritten rather than implemented, because AGENTS.md forbids preparing an unreachable branch. js/detect.js:624's comment carried the same falsified claim and was corrected. An existing test in scripts/detect.test.mjs pinned the old message and was updated.

js/cmd.js captureParsedCommand() recorded the reqmenu prefix's effect (iflags.menu_requested) but not the fight prefix's (context.forcefight), so a retryable boundary raised under a force-fight would replay the direction key as a plain walk -- a different command from the one the player typed -- and would leave the flag set into the following command. The capture site at js/cmd.js inside rhack()'s prefix loop runs after do_fight() has set the flag, so the path is reachable. Fixed by capturing and restoring it alongside menuRequested, with the doc comment rewritten to name both prefixes. The new property's boolean mutant survives the suite because no test drives a retry through that path; that is a coverage gap rather than an unkillable mutant, and it is recorded as the deferral parsed-retry-forcefight-restore-untested.

js/hack.js domove_fight_empty()'s dig-tool guard refuses every force-fight by a hero wielding a pick or an axe, which is dig.c:173 dig_typ()'s own first test and no more. C refuses only when dig_typ() answers something other than DIGTYP_UNDIGGABLE: dig.c:176-179 gives an axe DIGTYP_UNDIGGABLE at every wall, rock, pool and furniture square, where C swings and spends the turn, and dig.c:181-191 gives a pick DIGTYP_UNDIGGABLE on ROOM and CORR. scripts/force-fight.test.mjs's PICK_AXE/AXE row at a VWALL was pinning the port's refusal as though it were C's behavior. The guard is fail-closed, so the port is narrower than C rather than wrong. Narrowing it would make an axe-wielding hero's swing at a wall live, which is new supported behavior needing its own recorded C differential, so under .agents/review.md that returns to implementation rather than being an audit fix. Deferred as dig-tool-guard-refuses-where-dig_typ-answers-undiggable; the guard's comment and the test's comment now both state the real width.

rejections.summary: A correctness finding that executeMovement() still passes the command row's run value to preflightDomoveDestination(), the same wrong source corrected six lines below, so under a prefix that pre-commits DOMOVE_WALK the admission seam branches on a run value set_move_cmd() will never install.
rejections.counterEvidence: The deviation is provably unobservable rather than merely masked. A forcefight with a nonzero run value is reachable only through a prefix pair, because the runwest/runeast rows carry MOVEMENTCMD|CMD_M_PREFIX and no CMD_gGF_PREFIX (js/extcmdlist_data.js:199-206), so `FL` is refused at the prefix flag test and only `mFL`/`FmL` with wasMPrefix latched get through. In every such case iflags.menu_requested is true, which sends requireNoMonsterBump() down the same arm regardless of the run value. Do not reopen without an input that reaches preflightDomoveDestination() with a nonzero run value and menu_requested false.

rejections.summary: A readability finding that rhack()'s prologue comment claims C resets both prefix effects at every rhack() entry, while the fight prefix's effect, context.forcefight, is deliberately not reset there.
rejections.counterEvidence: The comment is accurate as written. The two statements it introduces are `state.iflags.menu_requested = false;` and `state.context.nopick = 0;` -- exactly the two values cmd.c:3634-3636 resets in rhack()'s prologue, and exactly the two effects the `m` prefix leaves behind. It says 'both prefix effects', not 'both prefixes'. Do not reopen without showing that C resets a third value there.

Do not reopen without a caller that reaches it with a record lacking the property.

C refuses only when dig_typ() answers something other than DIGTYP_UNDIGGABLE: dig.c:176-179 gives an axe DIGTYP_UNDIGGABLE at every wall, rock, pool and furniture square, where C swings and spends the turn, and dig.c:181-191 gives a pick DIGTYP_UNDIGGABLE on ROOM and CORR. scripts/force-fight.test.mjs's PICK_AXE/AXE row at a VWALL was pinning the port's refusal as though it were C's behavior. The guard is fail-closed, so the port is narrower than C rather than wrong. Narrowing it would make an axe-wielding hero's swing at a wall live, which is new supported behavior needing its own recorded C differential, so under .agents/review.md that returns to implementation rather than being an audit fix. Deferred as dig-tool-guard-refuses-where-dig_typ-answers-undiggable; the guard's comment and the test's comment now both state the real width.

mutation.deltaRun: 5 mutants, 1 survivor over the audit-fix diff; the survivor is the new forcefight property in captureParsedCommand(), deferred as parsed-retry-forcefight-restore-untested
mutation.finderConclusion: The tests finder traced all three window survivors and confirmed the slice worker's classification of each: js/cmd.js's `iflags.menu_requested = false` write, which rhack() clears at every entry (cmd.c:3609) above both readers, and the two '<'/'>' disjunctions at js/cmd.js:1520-1521, where no extcmdlist row makes one conjunct true and the other false. Ending events: the swing message domove_fight_empty() prints for the square attacked -- "You harmlessly attack the wall." for solid terrain, "You attack thin air." for anything accessible and not furniture -- with one turn spent; or, for a prefix followed by a command that does not accept it, cmd.c rhack()'s refusal line with no turn spent. The real game executes all of these: twelve recorded C segments replayed by the port over 31,346 PRNG calls and 56 screens, and seed0013-rogue-friday13-combat now matches completely at 59/59 steps and 4838/4838 calls.

Three earlier handoff claims were also checked and two were wrong -- that spot_shows_engravings() is ROOM-only, and that the off-edge arm needs directionname(xytodir()) -- and were corrected in commit 32938e6 before the pass ran.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Every reachable excluded branch stops before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output, which the pass checked explicitly and which is where it found the seenv defect. Excluded and verified fail-closed: the off-map-edge arm and move_out_of_bounds(); the boulder/statue arm, which needs ansimpleoname() and a glyph_is_statue() answer the port's presentation map memory cannot give; Underwater; Upolyd with AT_EXPL; the dig-tool guard, which is wider than C and deferred; domove_fight_ironbars(); domove_fight_web(); attack_checks()'s force-fight arm; and unmap_object()'s engraving arm, which this range made genuinely reachable in ordinary play, so a force-fight at a square carrying a random graffito now ends the segment there. That last case is recorded as the deferral force-fight-engraved-square with its inputs and expected failure.

head: 6b87d14d284275e4c39c9f02858dfbafc4c5754b
evidence: Counts: 13 raw, 13 deduplicated, 9 confirmed, 8 applied, 1 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 0 mutants. Full correctness pass over the commands deferral sweep: five ledger entries, four of which changed production code. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered, since the range adds no hot-path cost and no overlapping-lifecycle work. No production defect was found, which for a sweep is the expected result and is consistent with a range mutation run that produced no mutants at all. That empty run is the pass's most useful methodological result: the changed lines hold almost no relational, logical or boolean sites -- a bare return false, an assignment and a call, a straight-line body -- so the zero carries no evidence either way rather than evidence of coverage, and the three gaps it could not see were all found by reading. The one production change hardens an implicit contract whose two failure modes run in opposite directions: stop_occupation() took an optional env while env.message was mandatory on its common arm, where a missing operation is a bare TypeError that js/jsmain.js does not convert, so the segment is discarded rather than ended; on the sibling arm the same omission silently falls through to the live terminal writer during a planning clone. Five of the nine confirmed findings were comments the range itself falsified, which is now the third consecutive pass to find that pattern and the strongest recurring signal in this ledger. Tests led or tied for the ninth consecutive pass. One finding is deferred with its test shape and required mutation recorded.

productionDefects.summary: js/allmain.js stop_occupation() took `env = {}` while env.message is mandatory on its common arm, and the header described env only as something maybe_finished_meal() forwards to eatfood(), never as an operation this function calls itself. The two ways of getting it wrong fail in opposite directions, which is why the implicit contract was worth hardening rather than documenting: on the printing arm a missing message is a bare TypeError, and js/jsmain.js breaks the segment only for the named boundary classes, so the whole segment is discarded rather than ended on its last matching screen; on the finished-meal arm the same omission is not fatal at all, because js/eat.js eatOperations() defaults `message = ttyPline`, so a planning-mode caller that forgot it would write to the live terminal during a dry run. Reproduced by execution: calling stop_occupation with an installed occupation and `{ statusRefresh }` alone throws `TypeError: env.message is not a function`, and that shape is not hypothetical -- js/allmain.js invokes the occupation callback with exactly `{ statusRefresh }` twenty lines above the new call site. The range multiplied the caller count from one unexported helper to three exported call sites, and C has roughly fifteen further stop_occupation() sites unported, so new callers are expected. Fixed by resolving message through a requireOccupationOperation() helper matching the requireEatOperation/requireAttackOperation/requireDochugwOperation idiom the same file family already uses, and by rewriting the header to say message is required whenever an occupation is installed.

evidence: Counts: 18 raw, 12 deduplicated, 9 confirmed, 9 applied, 0 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 0 mutants. Full correctness pass over the monsters deferral sweep. Seven of the nine confirmed findings were wrong C line citations, and that is the result worth keeping. One sat on the single line of production code recording why starvePet refuses rather than being wired, and began seven lines inside a different function. That settles the argument for a checking script over careful hand-correction, since a citation written correctly can rot inside its own diff, and it is noted on the tracked entry, whose scope now extends past the four files it originally named. Two further comments misdescribed what this range did rather than where it came from: the note justifying the move enumerated the pre-move import while the same commit widened it, and the stopOccupation injection shadows a ported function three lines below a comment saying it is ported.
