evidence: Counts: 23 raw, 22 deduplicated, 19 confirmed, 10 applied, 9 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 10 survivors of 10 mutants. Full correctness pass over the wish-name-resolution goal, on the largest range this ledger has reviewed: 678 changed production lines in one commit across five files, three of which lay outside the slice's stated boundary and were reached by following a trace. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered. Nineteen confirmed findings, the largest set recorded here. One production defect, and it is this project's most durable pattern: set_artifact_intrinsic() refused after it had already written the hero's extrinsics, the third refusal-after-a-state-change found in five passes. The methodological result is the one worth carrying. The slice's ten mutation survivors were all argued equivalent and all the arguments held, but the pass showed the argument proves less than it looks: the mutator's relational map covers only the four ordering operators, so a strict-inequality line is not an enumerable site and the run is silent about it rather than covering it. A finder demonstrated that by taking such a line, bane_applies()'s SPFX_DALIGN hero arm, and proving with V8 coverage that it never executes. Nine test gaps were found that way, none visible to mutation, and they are deferred as one grouped ledger entry because nine fixtures across four test files exceeds what an audit-fix commit should carry. Two claims that no randomness lay on this path proved false during the work, both on the path the recorded case walks, and the comments asserting them are corrected rather than merely narrowed. The score is unchanged at 1363 screens and 118168 calls across the fixes.

productionDefects.summary: js/artifacts.js set_artifact_intrinsic() wrote the carried-resistance extrinsic into u.uprops through extrinsicMask() and only then read oart.cspfx to refuse the HALRES/ESP/WARN/XRAY group, so the stop fired after the hero extrinsics had already moved. C completes both effects, so C order is correct for C; the port stops on that group, and a refusal that has changed state ends the segment on a screen the port has diverged from rather than on its last matching one. This is the same defect class two earlier passes in this ledger found -- a refusal after rewriting map memory, and a refusal after the object had left inventory -- making it the third instance in five passes and the most durable pattern in this project. Fixed by hoisting the cspfx read and its refusal above the cary lookup and the extrinsicMask() call, leaving the rest of the order as C has it, with a comment stating that this is the one place the port departs from C order and why.

evidence: Counts: 9 raw, 8 deduplicated, 6 confirmed, 6 applied, 0 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 805 survivors of 879 mutants. Full correctness pass over the options-simple-menu goal. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered. Two production findings sharing one root cause, and together the most consequential this ledger holds: the range retired a display refusal on the claim that this port keeps no glyph-to-symbol-and-color table, and loc.remembered_glyph is exactly that table. The pass proved it by execution -- turning color on from the O menu leaves a remembered out-of-sight door at NO_COLOR where C repaints it CLR_BROWN -- so a clean fail-closed stop had become a silent wrong screen on a row the menu lists. hilite_pile is the worse half, because this port records no piletop mark at all and cannot re-highlight a remembered pile even in principle. Restoring the refusal costs the goal every development screen it had earned, since seed0006 picks hilite_pile at step 64, and that is the right trade: a stopped segment is worth more than one that runs on painting wrong cells. The underlying representation gap -- map memory storing a resolved presentation where C stores an unresolved glyph number -- is recorded as the new ledger entry remembered-glyph-caches-a-resolved-presentation, which is a display-subsystem goal rather than a finding of this range. The pass earned its place twice over on method. The goal's own trace had been wrong about the same function, so every claim from it was re-checked rather than carried, which is what surfaced the defect. And the mutation numbers said it first: 805 survivors sound alarming and 803 are boolean flips in a generated table pinned byte for byte by check:options, but of the two in hand-written code, one the slice never reported was the tell -- after the retirement opt_need_glyph_reset was written in four places and read nowhere. One finding was tried and reverted rather than applied, and the comment records why: the offered fix for give_opt_msg's three-valued read seeds a field in the parse result rather than the game state, so it never reaches the read and silences four toggle messages. The score ends where the goal began, at 1373 screens.

productionDefects.summary: The range retired js/options.js reset_needed_visuals()'s reset_glyphmap(gm_optionchange) refusal on the claim that this port keeps no glyph-to-symbol-and-color table, so a docrt() repaint would answer the whole question. The claim is false and the pass proved it by execution rather than argument. loc.remembered_glyph IS that table: remembered_glyph_from_presentation() stores an already-resolved {ch, color, decgfx, attr}, with the colour already pushed through mapColorEnabled(), and newsym()'s out-of-sight arm replays those fields without recomputing any of them. Measured: with OPTIONS=!color, walking until a door is remembered and out of sight and then picking the color row from the O menu, in-sight cells recolour correctly while the door stays NO_COLOR where C repaints it CLR_BROWN. hilite_pile is the worse half, and is a second confirmed finding with the same root: C carries piletop-ness as MG_OBJPILE in glyphmap[] and applies ATR_INVERSE at every print, while this port bakes the attribute in at draw time and records no piletop mark at all, so a remembered pile cannot be re-highlighted even in principle. That converted a clean fail-closed stop into a silent wrong screen on a row the O menu lists and the range's own recipe picks. Fixed by restoring the refusal, which costs seed0006 the five screens the pick loop earned because it picks hilite_pile at step 64; the development score returns from 1378 to 1373. The test asserting the repaint was inverted rather than deleted so the refusal has an oracle. The mutation survivor at js/options.js:4120 was the tell: after the retirement opt_need_glyph_reset was written in four places and read nowhere.

The same retirement loses hilite_pile, and this half cannot be recovered later even in principle. C carries piletop-ness as the MG_OBJPILE bit that reset_glyphmap() stores in glyphmap[], and wintty.c applies ATR_INVERSE from that bit at every print, so a repaint re-highlights remembered piles. This port bakes ATR_INVERSE into remembered_glyph.attr at draw time from the live iflags.hilite_pile (js/display.js:1136-1142) and records no piletop mark at all, so after the toggle a remembered pile is redrawn with the attribute it had before, and nothing in map memory says it was ever a pile. hilite_pile is a row on the recorded first page of the simple menu and the range own recipe picks it deliberately, so any game where the hero walked past a pile before opening O showed the pile un-highlighted where C shows it inverse. Closed by the same restored refusal.

evidence: Counts: 24 raw, 23 deduplicated, 19 confirmed, 19 applied, 0 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 9 survivors of 147 mutants. Full four-finder audit-diff-correctness pass over the pray-command goal, verified adversarially in three batches. 24 raw findings, 23 after deduplication, 19 confirmed, 4 rejected, none left unverified; all 19 applied in 34516de. The development score is identical either side of the fixes at 1388/7765 screens and 118743/610816 calls, measured by me at b0bb30e and again at 34516de. Two confirmed findings were behavioral and both were invariants that went stale rather than code that was wrong when written: pray.c critically_low_hp() had been ported a second time while the first copy kept serving botl.c and wintty.c with C's Upolyd arm missing, and dopray()'s nomul(-3) became the port's first negative-multi call site, falsifying the reason js/uhitm.js hitum() gave for dropping C's gm.multi < 0 term. The first was converged onto one owner; the second was re-derived from uhitm.c, which reads that term after passive() and so answers only for a paralysis inflicted inside the blow, leaving the port correct for a different reason than the one it stated.

productionDefects.summary: pray.c critically_low_hp() was ported twice and the two copies disagreed. The goal added a canonical js/pray.js critically_low_hp() while the pre-existing private js/display.js _criticallyLowHp() stayed in place, and that copy omitted C's Upolyd arm, so a polymorphed hero read u.uhp/u.uhpmax where C reads u.mh/u.mhmax. The display copy is not dormant: it serves botl.c:2555, which asks critically_low_hp(FALSE) for the BL_HP field, and win/tty/wintty.c:4539, which asks critically_low_hp(TRUE) for the hit-point bar, so the status line and the prayer could answer differently about the same hero. AGENTS.md's Keep each game value in one place governs. Fixed by deleting _criticallyLowHp() and pointing both C sites at js/pray.js critically_low_hp() with the argument each C site passes; verified that botl.c passes FALSE and wintty.c passes TRUE. The development score is unchanged because no recorded session polymorphs, which is exactly why the divergence survived until a second port of the same function exposed it. check:duplicate-symbols fell from 287 to 285.

The same defect reported independently by the variable-trace finder, which reached it from the other end: the range added a second port of one C function without deleting or repointing the first, so the port held two answers for one C value. Two finders converging on one duplicate from opposite directions is why it was treated as a defect rather than as tidying.

Porting do_wear.c stuck_ring() left js/insight.js:539-541 refusing insight.c one_characteristic()'s Fixed_abil arm with the reason stuck_ring() ... not ported, which the same range had made false. A refusal whose stated reason no longer holds is a fail-open in waiting: it stops a path that is now portable, and the next reader has no way to tell whether the stop is still needed. Fixed by porting the arm from C and removing the refusal.

The new restricted arm of tty_yn_function() added a module-private QUITCHARS as a second copy of decl.c quitchars[], while js/const.js:2014 already exported quitchars with the same value and the same C citation. Fixed by deleting the private copy and importing the existing one.

evidence: Counts: 23 raw, 21 deduplicated, 16 confirmed, 16 applied, 0 deferred, 5 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 3 survivors of 11 mutants. Full four-finder audit-diff-correctness pass over objects-deferral-sweep-2, verified adversarially. 23 raw findings, 21 after deduplication, 16 confirmed, 5 rejected, none left unverified; all 16 applied in f6a3350. The development score is identical either side of the fixes at 1389/7765 screens and 118859/610816 calls, measured by me at 1792cdc and again at f6a3350, and identical session for session. One confirmed finding was behavioral: makewish() handed an async hook to hold_another_object(), which invokes it through the synchronous merged() and drops the promise, so the merge message was neither ordered before obfree() nor awaited before the inventory line. No development session merges a wish into a carried stack, so the score could never have shown it. The rest were nine falsified or misstated comments and six test gaps where the code under test could be deleted with the whole suite green. The readiness mutation left three survivors in one function and the pass resolved them as an artifact of a narrower wave, then found the real issue beside them: a range simplification whose validity depends on an object-table adjacency that nothing pinned.

productionDefects.summary: js/zap.js makewish() supplied an async inventoryComparisonDiscovered hook to hold_another_object(), which invokes it through the synchronous merged() and discards the returned promise. The message invent.c merged() (933-942) prints when a wished object merges into a carried stack -- "You learn more about your items by comparing them." -- was therefore neither ordered before obfree() nor awaited before the inventory line. The hook had been added a few commits earlier because a scan found it missing, so the path is live rather than hypothetical. Fixed by awaiting addinvCore0Runtime() in hold_another_object(). It is invisible to the development score because no development session merges a wish into a carried stack, which is exactly why the pass was worth running: the defect sits on a live path the recorded set does not traverse. The apply session then built the end-to-end guard the pass had judged possibly expensive -- a Rogue wishing for an uncursed +0 dagger merges into the starting stack on all five seeds tried, and naming uncursed +0 removes the BUC and enchantment rolls that would otherwise make the merge seed-dependent. head: 52c65135eefcdc190e7f18d9abbfd2683963184c
evidence: Counts: 22 raw, 20 deduplicated, 16 confirmed, 16 applied, 0 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 40 mutants. Two production defects and one wrong refusal were introduced by this goal and fixed in its audit-fix commit 52c6513. The one that mattered is same_remembered_glyph(): the goal's own slice-selector had flagged the coarseness as a known residual and the code comment said so, but nobody had asked whether it was observable. It is, on the single path the goal made live, where it decides whether applying a lock pick costs a turn. Two finders reached it independently from different directions. The development score is identical before and after the audit fix at 1458/7765 screens, 120419/610816 calls, 1484/7765 cursors and 7 of 33 sessions, so none of the sixteen findings changed a recorded path; the goal's whole +27 screens came from the two implementation commits. Applying the sixteen took a further 2521 seconds beyond the pass's own 3221.

productionDefects.summary: same_remembered_glyph() answered "unchanged" for two remembered corpses C calls changed, because it compared a drawn presentation where C compares a glyph number. display.h corpse_to_glyph() encodes corpsenm, so a jackal corpse and a sewer-rat corpse carry different numbers while sharing symbol and colour; the finder executed both against the worktree and got byte-identical records. lock.c:584 is the sole consumer, and its result reaches doapply() at apply.c:4288 as the ECMD_TIME choice, so a wrong answer costs or saves a whole turn of monster movement and random-number draws. Fixed by stamping objectGlyphId in object_glyph_info(), carrying otyp, oclass, corpsenm and statue gender with a pile-top suffix, copying it as a non-enumerable sidecar in remembered_glyph_from_presentation(), and adding it to REMEMBERED_GLYPH_IDENTITY_FIELDS. The end-to-end C recording needs a pile top to change while the hero cannot see the square, which could not be arranged; that gap is recorded as pick-lock-lookalike-pile-top-has-no-fresh-case.

The same same_remembered_glyph() defect reached independently from the object side: two floor objects of different otyp that draw with one class symbol and colour compared equal, where C compares objnum_to_glyph(otyp) values that differ. The finder proved it by probe, mapping an otyp 2 object, blinding the hero, replacing it with otyp 21 of the same class and colour, and applying a lock pick: the remembered record was byte-identical and doapply() returned ECMD_OK where C returns ECMD_TIME. One adjudicator refuted this on causality as a duplicate of the corpse finding while the mandatory source-trace lens confirmed it, so it stands as its own record of a second reachable case. Fixed by the same objectGlyphId change, and pinned separately by an ARROW versus CROSSBOW_BOLT test.

reglyph_darkroom() refused more than its justification supported. Only two of C's four arms at display.c:1826-1848 need GLYPH_NOTHING; the two behind dark_room and colour need only the cmap index this same range added, so a remembered lit corridor kept S_litcorr where C rewrites it to S_corr, and an O-menu lit_corridor toggle repainted out-of-sight corridor cells in CLR_WHITE where C paints the terminal default. Fixed by running display.c:1831-1833 and 1842-1844 inside the non-refused branch, keeping the refusal for the two GLYPH_NOTHING arms, and adding C's third gate term Is_rogue_level(), which the port had ignored.

The pet cursed-step report hallucinated only the pile name. do_name.c noit_mon_nam() passes SUPPRESS_SADDLE|SUPPRESS_IT without SUPPRESS_HALLUCINATION, so x_monnam()'s do_hallu arm replaces the pet's name with rndmonnam() and draws twice from the display RNG; the port printed the true species name, drew nothing, and the committed test pinned that wrong string. QUALITY.json records nine prior production defects of exactly this shape, two of them introduced by the fix for a previous one, and every one was found by its symptom rather than by review; this is the first found by review, by the concurrency finder enabled for that reason. js/display.js newsym() has no port of display.c:1013-1024's mtrapped branch, which sets trap->tseen for a displayed monster held in a bear trap, a pit or a web before filing the remembered glyph. grep -c mtrapped js/display.js returns 0, and both newsym() sites test trap?.tseen with no mtrapped term. A catch the hero did not watch therefore leaves the trap unremembered where C remembers it: kill the monster before its next m_move() and C redraws the trap glyph while the port redraws floor, with the map memory wrong for the rest of the level. Every segment in scripts/run-monster-bear-trap.mjs catches its pony in sight, where trapeffect_bear_trap()'s own seetrap() has already set tseen, which is why the validation could not see it. js/allmain.js interrupt_multi() carried the claim that a run is the only way this port reaches a positive multi, so the arm that refuses allmain.c interrupt_multi():975-983's Norep(msg) half was a no-op. cmd.c rhack():3728-3729's set_occupation() call, landed by this goal, falsified it: a counted `s` or `.` leaves gm.multi above 0 with neither svc.context.run nor svc.context.travel set, which is exactly the state the guard admits, so a count spanning the turn the hero regains the last hit point or power point ends the segment where C prints one line and stops the count. The refusal itself is correct and fail-closed: it is taken ahead of nomul(0), which C runs first, so the interruption is wholly unapplied. Deferred rather than fixed because porting Norep(msg) makes js/regen.js regen_hp(), regen_pw() and js/allmain.js interrupt_multi() async and emits a message on a turn no input boundary bounds, which is new rendering behavior and needs a fresh recorded C case.

rejections.summary: state.go.occupation holds callbacks with two incompatible signatures, eatfood(state, env) and timed_occupation(state), and timed_occupation() drops the env js/allmain.js:1102 passes, so a timed occupation's handler can receive no injected operation.
rejections.counterEvidence: The facts hold and the impact does not. Enumerating extcmdlist[] prints exactly two rows carrying f_text, `115 search dosearch "searching"` and `46 wait donull "waiting"`, so timedOccupationFunction() can return only dosearch or donull. js/detect.js:844 dosearch(state, rawEnv = {}) hands dosearch0() a normalizeSearchEnv() that defaults every operation, and js/cmd.js:388 donull(state) takes no env at all; js/cmd.js:1528 already calls dosearch(state) with none from the typed path. Widening timed_occupation() to forward an env no reachable callee reads is the speculative plumbing AGENTS.md forbids, and it weakens the translation of C's argument-less `(*timed_occ_fn)()`. Do not reopen without a third f_text row in upstream extcmdlist[] whose handler reads an injected operation.

js/options.js parseNethackrc() silently skipped a line with no ':' or '=', where cfgfiles.c parse_config_line() answers with a configuration error that a UNIX build never suppresses. It is one of the two commonest rc typos, and its absence under-counts the error summary whenever it coexists with a reported error.

js/options.js parseNethackrc() silently skipped a line whose statement name matches no CONFIG_STATEMENTS row, where cfgfiles.c parse_config_line():1436-1437 reports Unknown config statement. Reporting it today would wrongly flag WIZKIT, HILITE_STATUS, BOULDER and the rest, because the port's table holds 13 of config_line_stmt[]'s 31 non-syscnf_only rows.

js/options.js dropped cfgfiles.c's three remaining configuration errors in the section and CHOOSE arms, so a sectioned rc under-reported and under-counted: a player who writes [mysection] headers without a CHOOSE line gets one C error per header and none from the port.

js/options.js's three Missing parameter errors interpolated the raw comma element with its negation prefixes, where C's string_for_opt() reports the negation-stripped statement the function already held under another name.

js/cfgfiles.js gave the one C value configfile two JavaScript homes: get_configfile() read state.configfile while js/tutorial_startup.js read state.configFileName, each with its own '.nethackrc' literal, so whoever supplies the real path would set one and silently leave the other on the default.

js/tty_startup.js raised iflags.cbreak below its display guard, so a state without an nhDisplay kept the getret-only key set for the rest of the game. With cbreak falsy, xwaitforspace() accepts only CR and LF, so such a caller drains the input queue and dies as 'Input queue empty', which runSegment() mistakes for a deliberate end of recording.

js/options.js returned early for mouse1 and mouse2 on a false reading of C. In options.c parsebindings():7635-7641 only the accepting arm returns, and txt2key("mouse1") answers M-o, so C reports Error binding mouse button 1 and still binds key 0xEF where the port reported nothing and bound nothing.

js/options.js decided whether a name is a menu command with a bare property read on a prototype-bearing object, so inherited names such as constructor were treated as menu commands and appended verbatim to iflags.mapped_menu_op instead of reaching bind_key(). C compares against default_menu_cmd_info[] with strcmp, which holds no such name. The same unguarded read appeared at three further rc-text sites in the status-highlight parser.

Its two production findings are both against a ledger record rather than code, and both matter more than that sounds. The deferral text-window-line-drops-its-g-putch-first-byte recorded that one of the port's two rendering loops correctly models C's first-byte arm; patch 006 hooks nomux_putch() three times on that path, both putchar hooks wrap the call in a curx-- compensation and the g_putch hook has none, and the loop pre-increments curx, so C records the stripped byte one column to the right and neither port matches. The pass also says something about the instrument: five of its eight findings are substitutions scripts/mutate-sites.mjs cannot express, since its site set is relational operators, logical connectives, boolean literals and integer bounds while the unpinned seams here were an identifier and four awaits. productionDefects.summary: The deferral text-window-line-drops-its-g-putch-first-byte recorded that js/tty_menu.js writeRecorderTtyWindowLine() correctly models C's g_putch first-byte arm. It does not, and neither port does. Patch 006 hooks nomux_putch() three times on process_text_window()'s path; both putchar hooks wrap the call in a curx-- compensation and the g_putch hook has none, while the loop pre-increments curx in its condition. So C records the stripped byte one column to the right of its own. A successor closing that entry by merging the two loops would have propagated a one-cell column error into every text and menu window instead of removing it, and screen comparison is per cell.

The same deferral omitted a second divergence in the same function: writeRecorderTtyWindowLine() writes a byte below 0x20 into a shadow cell that nomux_putch() discards, while writeStyledText() now drops it. The entry asks for the two loops to be merged, so without this the merge had no recorded statement of which behavior is right for control bytes.

First, the range did not introduce or widen the gap: at 856b9f69 the same redirect sat inside object_glyph_info() as `if (obj.otyp === BOULDER) symbol = misc_symbol(SYM_BOULDER, state);` and was equally untested — `git grep -n BOULDER 856b9f69 -- scripts/*.test.mjs` returns only bury, cmd, dismount-steed, dodown, dogmove-goal, dogmove and the display-symbols piletop fixture at :1108-1110, none of which asserts a symbol. I executed the port's own tables: `misc_symbol(SYM_BOULDER, state)` returns {"ch":"`"} and `object_class_symbol(state.objects[BOULDER].oc_class /* 14 */, state, BOULDER)` returns {"ch":"`"} — the same character, because include/defsym.h:481 gives ROCK_CLASS the default '`'. Deleting the redirect changes nothing a boulder draws unless a config S_boulder override (js/options.js:3885's ov_primary_syms read) or a non-default symbol set has moved one of the two, so "on every square holding a boulder, in sight and in memory alike" is false. The re-keying risk the finding attaches to the move is also absent: for a generic object the offset is an oclass in 1..16 while BOULDER is 475, so the two key spaces cannot collide.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:1781 The object layer's whole representation change turns on `Number.isInteger(glyph.glyph)`, where `glyph` is a **non-enumerable** property, and the file's own other presentation-copy boundary already drops it — with no guard, a copied presentation silently reverts an object square to a stored resolved presentation.
rejections.counterEvidence: No path exists that feeds a copied presentation back into remembered_glyph_from_presentation(), so the described failure cannot occur. Counter-evidence: `grep -rn "disp_glyph" js/` returns every use: show_glyph_cell() writes it (js/display.js:1722, 1726), js/display.js:4378 nulls it, and js/startup_a11y.js:315-438 and :805 read it for save/restore and comparison. It is never an argument to remembered_glyph_from_presentation(). I inspected all fourteen production call sites of that function (js/display.js:1976, 1981, 2009, 2048, 2175, 2193, 2248, 2253, 2444, 2514, 2554, 2735, 2747 and js/detect.js:273): each receives a presentation constructed moments earlier by terrainCmap(), trap_glyph_info(), engravingGlyph(), object_glyph_info() or mappedObjectGlyphInfo(), and the object-bearing ones (2048, 2444, 2514, and newsym()'s rememberedUnderlying at 2419-2430) come straight out of map_glyphinfo(), which stamps `glyph` at js/display.js:1393. The one transform on that path, withAccessibilityMetadata() (js/display.js:646-675), mutates the record in place via Object.defineProperties and returns the same object, so the non-enumerable sidecar survives it. The stored record's own `glyph` is an ordinary enumerable field of the object literal at :1782, so it also survives serialization.

rejections.summary: js/makemon.js:313 `grow_up()` computes a `PM_KILLER_BEE && !victim -> PM_QUEEN_BEE` branch two statements above the refusal that makes `!victim` unreachable, so the branch reads as live code that can never execute.
rejections.counterEvidence: The claimed evidence is false where it matters: the finding asserts the queen-bee arm has no test behind it and that `grep -n PM_QUEEN_BEE scripts/` returns nothing. Counter-evidence: `grep -rn PM_QUEEN_BEE scripts/` returns nine hits, including scripts/makemon.test.mjs:876-888, a dedicated test named 'grow_up keeps a killer bee that killed something a killer bee' whose comment cites makemon.c:2062-2067 and explains the !victim conjunct in as many words: 'the pair is absent from grownups[], so a kill leaves newtype at PM_KILLER_BEE and the queen's level never raises lev_limit'. It asserts state.mons[PM_QUEEN_BEE].mlevel === 9 to show the queen's level was not read. The header comment at js/makemon.js:286-291 already names the !victim arm as refusing, with C's line range 2099-2106.

rejections.summary: js/monmove.js:1854 `shootsAfterMoving` names a value that does not decide whether the monster shoots — it decides whether control falls through into PHASE FOUR — and computing it can spend a random-number draw and can throw a refusal, neither of which the name or the expression shape suggests.
rejections.counterEvidence: The concrete hazards the finding says are unmarked are documented and pinned. Counter-evidence: js/mhitu.js:970-974, the doc on ranged_attk_available() itself, states 'The draw is real and belongs to the caller's turn... That is why this is not a pure predicate and why monmove.c dochug() must reach it in C's order.' The order is pinned by two tests: scripts/monmove-dochug.test.mjs:256-300 ('dochug rolls a random breath where C rolls it, before the attack phase') and :360-395 ('dochug stops a mover that fell asleep before it tests its attacks'), the second written so that 'the injected rn2 fails the test if the order is wrong'. The name paraphrases the C comment transcribed directly above it at monmove.c:943-944, and the const has exactly one use, on the next line.

rejections.summary: js/options.js:4860 `go.opt_need_glyph_reset` is now written and cleared but read nowhere in `js/`, while the comment at the site of the deleted read says the rebuild and the repaint "are one act here" — implying the flag still gates something.
rejections.counterEvidence: The write-only flag is real, but the mechanism the finding says is unrecorded is both wrong and already written at the site. Counter-evidence: The finding claims 'the equivalence rests entirely on the unstated fact that every C setter also raises opt_need_redraw'. js/options.js:4856-4860 states the actual reason: 'display.c reset_glyphmap(gm_optionchange) rebuilds glyphmap[]... This port keeps no such table: js/display.js map_glyphinfo() resolves one glyph number on demand.' Because there is no cached table for the converted layer, C's rebuild has no counterpart to skip -- in the hypothetical state the finding constructs, C's reset_glyphmap() without a docrt() draws nothing and the port's next newsym() resolves afresh, so the two agree. The stale-memory risk for the unconverted terrain layer is held by the named refusals at js/options.js:4572 and 4610, not by the flag.

rejections.summary: js/options.js:4869 The comment that replaces the deleted `reset_glyphmap()` refusal enumerates the option arms that now reach the repaint as two ('hilite_pile' and 'showrace'), but the switch case it describes has five reachable members, and one of them — 'wizmgender' — is the subject of a deferral filed in this same slice saying the port's repaint is wrong for it.
rejections.counterEvidence: The finding's central count is wrong: three of the five arms it names cannot reach the repaint at all. Counter-evidence: js/options.js:4562-4565 defines unsupportedWindowOption() over TTY_WINCAP, which at js/options.js:3540-3542 holds only WC_COLOR, WC_HILITE_PET, WC_INVERSE and WC_EIGHT_BIT_IN. WC_OPTION_CAPABILITY maps ascii_map to WC_ASCII_MAP (3478), tiled_map to WC_TILED_MAP (3487) and perm_invent to WC_PERM_INVENT (3482), so all three are skipped by doset()'s boolean loop at js/options.js:4190 (`if (unsupportedWindowOption(option.name)) continue;`) and never appear as pickable rows; perm_invent additionally has its own refusal at 4477-4481. The switch holding the six-member arm is guarded by `if (state.go.opt_initial) return optn_ok;` (js/options.js:4525), so a config-file parse never reaches it. Three arms reach the repaint from the menu, not five, and the comment omits exactly one of them, wizmgender.

rejections.summary: scripts/options-toggle.test.mjs:365 The new refusal test asserts only that parseoptions() rejects, and does not pin the stopping point; execution shows both refusals fire after the option value has already been written.
rejections.counterEvidence: The observation is right and the conclusion is wrong: the write before the refusal is the write options.c itself performs at that point, so there is no divergence for the test to pin. Counter-evidence: js/options.js:4486 carries C's own marker, `setBooleanOptionValue(state, option, !negated); /* <==== SET IT HERE */`, and both refusals sit in the third switch below it, at 4573 ('use_inverse') and 4610 ('color'), which is where options.c:5379-5385 and 5407-5409 sit relative to the same assignment. A test asserting state.iflags.wc_color unchanged would assert behavior contrary to options.c. The repository has no rule requiring a refusal to precede every state change: `grep -rn 'state change' .agents/*.md AGENTS.md` returns nothing, and js/cmd.js:1332-1338 documents the opposite practice -- 'zap.c dozap() raises this from its three effect arms. Each one stops after the command has already spent a charge and painted its prompts'. js/cmd.js:1315 ends the segment on UnsupportedOptionMenuError, so nothing after the throw is scored.

mutation.finderConclusion: Two runs compose this record. The window run over 856b9f69..de2a8b5 killed 74 of 81 first-wave mutants; its seven survivors all sit in the range's monster half, six in js/makemon.js grow_up() and one in js/mhitm.js, and none in the display work the range is mostly about. The delta run over de2a8b5..bea560c, the audit fixes, produced one mutant at js/display.js:1289 -- the new argument guard's `glyph !== undefined && !Number.isInteger(glyph)` -- and killed it against eighteen first-wave test files. The tests finder reported no finding against any survivor; its five confirmed findings were coverage gaps neither run could see, because a line with no mutable site produces no mutant. Four of the five are display.h macro transcriptions whose bases are constants, and the fifth is a test row that isolated no term.

readiness.boundary: The user-visible starting event is a pick of a boolean row from doset_simple()'s menu whose optfn arm sets go.opt_need_glyph_reset; seed0006-wizard-water-demon reaches it at step 64 with the byte 'f', hilite_pile, on page 2. The ending event is the screen drawn after reset_needed_visuals() returns, that is after reset_glyphmap(gm_optionchange) and the docrt() at options.c:9002. The real game executes it: seed0006 completes that pick loop and gains five screens, and the fresh recipe 'remembered pile repainted by a glyph reset' (seed 6193044, 20281114093000) drives the same path over a pile the hero has walked out of sight of.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable before the ending event was traced against the C source in two passes, first by the orchestrator at e310ec0 before implementation and again by the worker while implementing, with the results recorded entry by entry in .agents/implementation-checklist.json. The trace covered include/display.h's enum glyph_offsets and object-glyph macros, all eight object arms of src/display.c reset_glyphmap() and its closing colour clamp, map_glyphinfo(), win/tty/wintty.c tty_print_glyph()'s ordered attribute chain, and options.c reset_needed_visuals(). It covered state and random-number order: no ported arm consumes randomness, and the two macros that do under Hallucination were left unconverted and are excluded because the number they produce lies in the monster ranges. Stubs, stops and partial implementations were identified: three refusals stand inside the boundary's neighbourhood, on the 'color', 'use_inverse' and 'wizmgender' arms, the third added by this pass; map_glyphinfo() raises a TypeError for a number outside the object ranges, which nothing can currently produce.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Every reachable excluded branch stops before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output: each of the three option refusals is raised in optfn_boolean()'s switch, which js/cmd.js ends the segment on, and reglyph_darkroom() keeps its own refusal for a dark_room change and for any rogue level. The two cannot-occur entries rest on conditions rather than on absence of evidence: a hallucinated object's glyph number lands in the monster ranges, and any rogue level stops earlier at reglyph_darkroom(), whose third gate term is Is_rogue_level(). The one limit worth stating is that the rogue exclusion was verified against that refusal rather than against the 33 development sessions.

head: 683ac584179d4eddf5fc7de17b93da2edccc4b25

checklist.reason: the checklist covers e414c117, an ancestor of the range head; the 1 path(s) changed between them own no QUALITY.json area

evidence: Counts: 20 raw, 18 deduplicated, 17 confirmed, 17 applied, 0 deferred, 1 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 2 survivors of 76 mutants. Seventeen of eighteen deduplicated findings confirmed, the highest rate any pass here has produced, and the reason is the shape of the change rather than the quality of the work: a range that redefines what a data structure means leaves every comment, test seed and oracle that described the old shape describing something that no longer exists. Five findings were production defects. Two could produce a wrong screen -- the GLYPH_NOTHING arm's missing accessibility kind, which made js/startup_a11y.js's 'nothing' disjunct unreachable, and the altar customization name the glyph registry does not hold. One was a wrong transcription with no reachable consumer, glyph_to_cmap()'s zap arm, where a test in the same range had pinned the port's omission as if it were C's contract. One was a name collision, js/region.js storing a cmap index in a field called glyph while C's struct region.glyph holds the number; renaming it caught two further readers only because the full suite ran. And one was two dead expressions newsym() still passed. Six test findings were coverage gaps no mutation run can see, because a line with no mutable site produces no mutant: a name table with no test at all, an oracle comparing production output with itself, a seed in a shape no production path can build, and two halves of struct rm's field aliases that the tables never wrote. One finding was rejected and its counter-evidence recorded: the claim that regenerating the second-complete-turn oracle left the stored glyph unguarded was refuted by executing the mutation it offered as proof, which the unit suite killed. One finding was left to Implementation rather than applied: unmap_object()'s engraving refusal cites a helper this range ported, so the stop is avoidable now, but retiring it lets a force-fight at an engraved square keep running and needs a recorded case; its comment was corrected to say so and the open deferral force-fight-engraved-square owns the port. Every fix was watched failing first, by six mutants reversed with git restore. The development score did not move: 10 of 33 sessions, 1,768 screens, 125,937 random-number values and 1,786 cursors before and after, and both fresh differentials match C unchanged. Optional finders: performance was not enabled, because the range replaces stored-field replay with the resolution C performs at print time, which .agents/review.md excludes from the trigger; concurrency was not enabled, because the range changes no asynchronous or reentrant flow. A clarity pass was not run: the six comment findings this pass confirmed were applied here.

productionDefects.summary: js/display.js map_glyphinfo()'s GLYPH_NOTHING arm attached no accessibility metadata, because the sidecars hung off the cmap classifier and that arm draws from no defsym index. js/startup_a11y.js tests oldKind === 'nothing', its transcription of display.c show_glyph()'s disjunct on the old glyph, so the reader fell back to 'other' and that disjunct could never fire for a square reglyph_darkroom() had blanked.

js/display.js ALTAR_CUSTOMIZATION_NAMES ended in 'G_other_altar', which the glyph registry does not hold. glyphs.c:1015-1027 prefixes the alignment to the base name for four altars and gives the sanctum one 'altar other' with skip_base set, so C's name is G_altar_other; sourceGlyphName() answers null for the old spelling, so a customization of that altar could never apply.

js/display.js glyph_to_cmap() answered MAXPCHARS for a zap glyph where glyphs.c:1003-1004 answers ((glyph - GLYPH_ZAP_OFF) % 4) + S_vbeam, and a test in the same range pinned the wrong answer as if it were C's contract. The arm is pure arithmetic and was transcribed; nothing in the port produces a zap glyph, so no drawn cell moves.

js/region.js stored a bare S_* cmap index in a field named glyph, where C's struct region.glyph holds the display.h glyph number, and this range added a cmap_to_glyph() call over it. Renamed to glyph_cmap so glyph keeps one meaning across js/; the full suite caught two readers the first rename missed, currentGas?.glyph and nextGas?.glyph in js/monmove.js.

js/display.js newsym() passed a second trap argument at two call sites that remembered_glyph_from_presentation() stopped taking in this range, and JavaScript discarded it silently, leaving two live expressions computing a trap for no consumer.

rejections.summary: scripts/fixtures/second-complete-turn.session.json:119 All 17 stateDigest values were rewritten from this commit's own output, and that digest is the only oracle in the repository that sees the stored glyph numbers, so any mis-numbering introduced by the same commit was absorbed rather than caught.
rejections.counterEvidence: The finding's discriminating experiment is wrong: the mutation it offers as proof that the digest is the sole detector is killed by the unit suite. Counter-evidence: I applied exactly the stated mutation in a scratch copy -- cmap_walls_to_glyph()'s default arm changed from GLYPH_CMAP_MAIN_OFF to GLYPH_CMAP_SOKO_OFF at js/display.js:1123 -- and ran `node --test scripts/display-symbols.test.mjs`: 152 tests, 150 pass, 2 fail. The failures are 'cmap_to_glyph walks display.h's six arms in order' and 'cmap_walls_to_glyph reads the branch the hero is standing in'. The latter, at scripts/display-symbols.test.mjs:8288-8305, pins all five bases explicitly, main dungeon included: the table's first row is `['main', {}, GLYPH_CMAP_MAIN_OFF]`. The claim that this mutation 'makes second-complete-turn.test.mjs fail ... and nothing else in the display suite' is therefore false, and with it the premise that stateDigest is the only detector for mis-numbering of this class.

mutation.finderConclusion: Two runs compose this record. The window run over the slice killed 72 of 74 first-wave mutants at kind=boolean,logical,relational; the delta run over the audit fixes killed both of its two. The window run's two survivors sit at js/display.js:1218 and :1560 and were argued undecidable by arithmetic. The tests finder was asked to check that arithmetic against the generated tables rather than take it on trust, and did not report against either: at GLYPH_ALTAR_OFF the cmap A arm computes S_brdnladder + 1 = 33 = S_altar, and at GLYPH_CMAP_A_OFF a > 0 test falls into the Sokoban wall arm at offset 11 giving S_vwall + 11 = S_ndoor, coloured CLR_GRAY by both arms. Its six confirmed findings were coverage gaps no mutation run could see: a name table with no test, an oracle that compared production output with itself, a seeded record in a shape no production path can build, and two alias halves the tables never wrote.

readiness.boundary: The starting event is a pick of the 'color' row from doset_simple()'s menu or of 'use_inverse' from the full 'mO' menu; the ending event is the screen drawn after reset_needed_visuals() returns, with every remembered out-of-sight terrain square repainted under the value now in force. The real game executes it: scripts/run-options-menu.mjs's three new recipes over seed 6193044 drive a pile out of sight and toggle each option, and two of the three fail against C when the re-derivation is broken.
readiness.sourceReview: Traced in two independent passes and recorded entry by entry in .agents/implementation-checklist.json, which reaches ready-for-audit with eighteen entries, all done. The orchestrator traced the candidate list at the slice base before implementation, reading back_to_glyph(), the map-memory cmap arms with their colour macros and tables, display.h's cmap glyph macros and both definitions of glyph_is_cmap; the worker traced the same range while implementing and found the list short in three places. The trace covered state and random-number order: no arm in scope consumes randomness, the development score is identical call for call, and the wall arms' branch dependence through u.uz is state read at record time. Stubs and stops identified: 'wizmgender' is the one refusal left in optfn_boolean(); unmap_object()'s engraving refusal stands and its comment now names the real remaining requirement rather than a helper that is ported; and map_glyphinfo()'s guard refuses the zap, swallow, explosion, warning and GLYPH_UNEXPLORED ranges, which no ported path produces.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Every reachable excluded branch stops before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output. One gap is recorded rather than hidden: the four MG_BW_* bits and reglyph_darkroom()'s GLYPH_NOTHING write are unit-tested and reach no fresh differential, because the terrain they need does not occur on the first level and doengrave() has no port, which is the open deferral remembered-cmap-cues-have-no-fresh-case.

checklist.reason: the checklist covers be8cce14, an ancestor of the range head; the 2 path(s) changed between them own no QUALITY.json area

evidence: Counts: 12 raw, 10 deduplicated, 8 confirmed, 8 applied, 0 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 8 mutants. The goal's closing pass, run because the goal closes rather than because a threshold forced it; the gate read WATCH. Eight of ten deduplicated findings confirmed. The one that mattered most was a citation: hero_glyph_info() acquired its first C reference in this range, to display.h hero_glyph, and ported that macro's gender half while dropping its species disjunct, so a reviewer diffing the function against the named lines would have signed off on a branch that is not there. Porting the disjunct then exposed a second defect the pass did not report: an older fixture built its hero with umonnum and no umonster, which you.h:554's Upolyd reads as polymorphed. Four test findings were coverage gaps no mutation run could see, and one of them is the sharper result of this pass: the live configuration-file bug the slice had found and fixed was pinned by nothing, so reverting the fix left the whole suite green. The menu path cannot catch it, because it never runs applyBooleanOption(). The readiness delta run then caught a survivor of its own, the colour half of the disjunct I had just ported, unpinned because the fixture's polymorph form and HI_DOMESTIC were both CLR_WHITE; a colour assertion killed it. Two findings were rejected with counter-evidence. The development score did not move: 10 of 33 sessions, 1,768 screens, 125,937 random-number values and 1,786 cursors before and after, and both fresh differentials match C, the options menu now over 20 recipes at 57,424 calls and 321 screens. Optional finders: performance was not enabled, because the range adds one flag to a presentation and merges three attribute tests into one chain, with no amplified work and no measured budget; concurrency was not enabled, because the range changes no asynchronous or reentrant flow. A clarity pass was not run: the two comment findings this pass confirmed were applied here.

productionDefects.summary: js/display.js hero_glyph_info() cited display.h hero_glyph (654-656) for the first time in this range and ported that macro's Ugender half while dropping its Upolyd species disjunct, so the citation asserted a fidelity the function did not have, and a new test driving Upolyd true made the polymorph case look handled. The disjunct is ported now, with the colour it selects; it is inert while polyself is unported.

scripts/display-symbols.test.mjs's 'hero and pet symbol overrides' fixture built its hero as { umonnum: 0 } with no umonster, and you.h:554's Upolyd compares the two, so the hero read as polymorphed the moment the disjunct existed. Exposed by the fix above rather than reported on its own, and corrected in the same commit.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:757 The new `Ugender()` gives `hero_glyph_info()` C's polymorph branch, but the species and colour it sits beside still omit C's `Upolyd ||`, so `hero_glyph` is now polymorph-aware in one half only — and the new test drives the polymorph branch without distinguishing the two readings.
rejections.counterEvidence: The transcription gap is real but the correctness problem it claims is impossible in any state the port can build. Counter-evidence: `grep -rn "umonnum\s*=" js/ | grep -v "==="` returns exactly two hits: js/eat.js:2109 (a comment) and js/u_init.js:370, `u.umonnum = u.umonster = state.urole.mnum;`. There is no writer that makes them differ, so `Upolyd()` is constantly false and `(Upolyd || !flags.showrace)` reduces to `!flags.showrace` for every reachable state — the port and C select the same mnum and the same colour in all of them. The finding concedes this itself: "Dormant today because Upolyd() is constantly false, so no screen changes now." No wrong screen, no wrong random-number call, no wrong state exists to find.

rejections.summary: js/objnam.js:775 The recorded reason for waiving end-to-end evidence on the male, female and neuter arms of the gender suffix is false: it argues only about statues from `mkcorpstat()`, while the same branch covers corpses and figurines that the port's own code gives a real gender.
rejections.counterEvidence: The code trace is right but the record it accuses says the opposite of what the finding reports, and the finding identifies no incorrect behaviour in its stated category. Counter-evidence: The committed entry in .agents/implementation-checklist.json states reachability as "Any STATUE, CORPSE or FIGURINE named while wizard && iflags.wizmgender hold. Reachable from a configuration file today, and from the menu once the refusal goes." — the record already says corpses and figurines reach the branch. Its CORPSTAT_RANDOM sentence is explicitly scoped and true as written: "The CORPSTAT_RANDOM arm is the common case for a level-generated statue", which js/corpstat.js:151 (`obj.spe = corpstatflags & CORPSTAT_SPE_VAL`) over mklev's bare CORPSTAT_INIT confirms. Nothing in the record claims the male, female or neuter arms are unreachable. The finding also concedes "the ported code is correct for all four spe values", so no correctness defect is asserted.

mutation.finderConclusion: Two runs compose this record. The window run over the slice ran six mutants and killed all six; the tests finder was asked to judge whether six over 208 changed lines meant few mutable sites or thin coverage, and answered with four confirmed coverage findings no mutation run could see -- a table driving a masked field only within the mask, an unpinned suffix position, an unobserved pet flag, and a live bug with no committed test at all. The delta run over the audit fixes ran two and left one survivor, js/display.js:755's showRace-and-not-Upolyd mutated to a disjunction, which was real: the species half of the disjunct was pinned and the colour half was not, because the fixture gave the polymorph form CLR_WHITE and js/const.js:2424 defines HI_DOMESTIC as CLR_WHITE, so both branches answered the same value. A colour assertion killed it and the rerun is clean at 2 of 2.

readiness.boundary: The starting event is a pick of the 'wizmgender' row from doset()'s full 'mO' menu in a debug game, or the same option set from a configuration file, where optfn_boolean() returns at options.c:5325's go.opt_initial guard before any menu code runs. The ending event is the screen drawn after reset_needed_visuals() returns, with every visible female monster and a female hero carrying the inverse video tty_print_glyph() gives MG_FEMALE. The real game executes both: two new recipes in scripts/run-options-menu.mjs drive them, and the configuration-file one failed against C before the applyBooleanOption() fix.
readiness.sourceReview: Traced in two independent passes and recorded entry by entry in .agents/implementation-checklist.json, which reaches ready-for-audit with fourteen entries, twelve done and two cannot-occur. The orchestrator traced the candidate list at the slice base, reading display.h hero_glyph, you.h Ugender, display.c's mgendercode assignment and its use in the M_AP_MONSTER arm, objnam.c:1549-1559, and every writer of levl[x][y].glyph across nethack-c/upstream/src/ -- which is what establishes that this slice is a print-time change rather than a range conversion, against a deferral that prescribed the conversion. The worker reached the same reading independently and found two things the list did not hold: applyBooleanOption() had no wizmgender arm at all, and hallucinated_statue_glyph_info() made a gender draw it discarded. The correctness pass then found the hero_glyph species disjunct missing. The trace covered state and random-number order: no ported arm consumes randomness except the statue draw, which already existed and whose position did not move. Stubs and stops identified: optfn_boolean() has one refusal left, on rest_on_space, outside this goal; the framecolor arm, the rogue-level terms and the worm-tail arms are unreachable for the conditions recorded on their entries.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary, and every reachable excluded branch stops before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output. Three arms rest on unit tests alone and their entries say which: the mimic and ridden arms, the male, female and neuter arms of the objnam.c suffix, and statue_to_glyph()'s hallucinating gender draw. The deferral wizmgender-never-inverts-a-female-monster is resolved with a note recording that the remedy it prescribed was refuted.

evidence:
Counts: 22 raw, 20 deduplicated, 18 confirmed, 17 applied, 1 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 25 mutants. Counts: 22 raw, 20 deduplicated, 18 confirmed, 18 applied, 1 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 25 mutants over two runs. The goal's closing pass, run because the goal closes rather than because a threshold forced it; the gate read WATCH at 3 of 10 commits and 512 of 1,000 lines. Eighteen of twenty confirmed, which is the highest proportion any pass here has returned, and the reason is that the range put a writer behind a marker every reader in the port already consulted.

The result that mattered most is the one the concurrency finder was enabled for. The slice's own comment asserted that no planning caller reaches mhitm.c pre_mm_attack(), naming js/allmain.js finishElapsedTurn() as the only function a clone runs with planning:true. That is false: preflightSimpleMonsterActions() runs moveSimplePet() with planning:true and a pet's blow arrives through dogmove.c dog_move(). The clone's level cells are the live game's and show_glyph_cell() takes no state at all, so a dry run marked a square in the running game and painted it, on a turn the scan may still refuse. Two findings, one from the correctness finder and one from the concurrency finder, described the write and the clear halves of the same leak. Both are closed: the mark goes through a seam the scan binds to a no-op, as it already binds newsym(), and map_invisible() now refuses a foreign state the way see_nearby_objects() does. mondead()'s clear refuses on a plan rather than skipping, because unmap_object() refuses an engraved square and a skipped call would hide that refusal from the pass that exists to find it.

Two more changed screens. monsterPossessive() open-coded the trailing-s half of hacklib.c s_suffix() and answered "It's tentacles suck" where C answers "Its", an arm this range made reachable. teleport.c rloc_to_core() calls Monnam() three times, before the move and twice after it, and the port read it once into a buffer; the snapshot was safe until this range made the name depend on canspotmon(), and a monster teleporting from a dark square into view was announced as "It appears!". A third, hack.c domove_fight_empty()'s digging refusal, omitted C's svc.context.forcefight conjunct, which became load-bearing when the entry test gained its non-forcefight disjunct.

Seven of the eighteen were test gaps, and they are the pass's real yield: the readiness mutation run killed 24 of 24 and found none of them, because each was a guard whose deletion breaks nothing the committed fixtures set up. The sharpest is newsym()'s !shouldDisplayMonster term, which keeps a monster the hero can spot from being replaced by a remembered 'I' -- and marker-and-monster is the ordinary follow-up state, not a corner, since the marker is written onto the square a monster is standing on. Every new assertion was watched failing against a mutant applied to the staged tree and reversed with git restore.

One finding is deferred rather than fixed. The marker seam's no-op makes the plan and the live pass diverge on the marker, so unmap_object()'s engraved-square refusal can now be raised by the live scan alone, where js/allmain.js has no class conversion and the segment loses its whole matching prefix. Closing it needs a recording of a monster dying on a marked engraved square; it is tracked as live-scan-map-memory-refusal-escapes-the-segment.

Two findings were rejected with counter-evidence, one on causality and one as pre-existing. The development score is unchanged across every fix: 10 of 33 sessions, 1,785 screens, 126,600 random-number values and 1,804 cursors before and after, and the fresh differential scripts/run-invisible-monster-marker.mjs still matches C over its five segments. Optional finders: concurrency was enabled and returned the leak; performance was not, because the range replaces a boolean read with an integer comparison and adds one arm to a glyph resolver, with no amplified work and no measured budget. A clarity pass was not run: the four comment findings this pass confirmed were applied here.

evidence:
Counts: 14 raw, 12 deduplicated, 6 confirmed, 5 applied, 1 deferred, 6 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 9 mutants. Counts: 14 raw, 12 deduplicated, 6 confirmed, 5 applied, 1 deferred, 6 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 9 of 9 relational, logical and boolean mutants killed over the range and no mutants at all over the audit-fix delta, with the slice's four declared integer survivors left standing. The goal's closing pass, run because the goal closes rather than because a threshold forced it; the gate read WATCH at 1 of 10 commits and 293 of 1,000 lines. Half the deduplicated findings were rejected with counter-evidence, the highest proportion any pass here has returned, and the adjudicators earned it: four of the six were refuted on reachability rather than on mechanism.

The result that mattered is a live escape the implementer had reasoned away. The comment above the elapsed-turn nh_timeout call said the live monster scan cannot take a due corpse off the floor without refusing first, since monster pickup is unported. Monster pickup is ported. mon.c mpickstuff()'s corpse filter lets an M1_COLLECT monster take an acidic or petrifying corpse, and the corpse's ROT_CORPSE element stays in the queue at the same expiry, because obj_timer_checks() runs only for a nonzero timed and acts only on ice. So a turn the pre-turn preflight admitted can reach run_timers() with the corpse at OBJ_MINVENT, which it refuses, and UnsupportedHeroTimeoutBoundaryError is not in js/jsmain.js's boundary list: the segment would have lost every screen it had already matched rather than ending on the last one. advanceElapsedTurn() converts it now, as its two preflights already did. The same finding's sibling, that the comment's ':1009' pointer had drifted to :1023 and now lands inside preflightGetHungry()'s env, is fixed with a name-based reference.

The second production fix is a message. run_timers() is reached from goto_level()'s arrival and from nh_timeout()'s tail, and both raised a refusal hard-coded to "elapsed-turn nh_timeout requires", so a descent stopping on a carried corpse's timer pointed boundary triage at js/allmain.js. The class carries a site now, each call site names itself, and the two assertions that pin them cannot be satisfied by one string.

Three of the six were test gaps, and the mutation runs found none of them. Only two of the nine timeout_funcs[] rows were pinned to their enum index, and the module-load guard checks only the table's length, which any permutation satisfies; a misaligned row would have made the port report the wrong C function in the boundary log that decides what is ported next. The integration fixture built its corpse from PM_LICHEN, which mkobj.c start_corpse_timeout() never schedules, so the one case tying the drain, the planning clone and the live newsym together stood on a queue state no recording can produce. And the dig recorder kept only the coordinates handed to newsym, so moving the redraw to the top of rot_corpse() passed the whole suite -- the redraw's position is this arm's only observable, since it writes no message and draws no random number.

One finding is deferred rather than tested: the new conversion is pinned by nothing, and two fixtures failed to reach mpickstuff()'s carry arm inside one turn. A gnome standing on the corpse never reaches it, because the arm runs from postmov() after a move; a gnome one square further out did not move at all, since a gnome's speed of 6 against NORMAL_SPEED 12 lets it act every other turn. Both attempts are recorded on live-timer-refusal-conversion-unpinned, which prefers a recording.

The development score is unchanged across every fix: 10 of 33 sessions, 1,802 screens, 126,961 random-number values and 1,821 cursors before and after, and scripts/run-corpse-rot.mjs still matches C over its three segments. Optional finders: concurrency was enabled, because the once-per-turn upkeep can run on a cloned state whose level cells are the live game's, and it returned no confirmed finding -- the previous goal's leak class was closed here by OBJ_AT()'s new state parameter and the newsym seam the plan binds to a no-op. Performance was not enabled, because the range adds one queue walk bounded by the due prefix. A clarity pass was not run: the pass's own comment findings were applied here, and the four wording findings it rejected were rejected as prose preference.

rejections.summary: js/dig.js:93 No test asserts the property the atomic-refusal design rests on -- that `unportedRotCorpseReason(obj) === null` implies `rot_corpse(obj)` runs to completion. rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The mechanical probe is accurate (unportedRotCorpseReason() checks where, Has_contents, unpaid, the hidden hero and the newsym seam, and js/invent.js:1636 demands setNotWorn after js/dig.js rot_organic() has already run obj_extract_self()), but the input it needs cannot exist, so the invariant the finding says is violated in fact holds for every reachable state. The other two demands preflightObfree() adds cannot fire on a corpse at all: a corpse is never `lamplit` and its otyp is CORPSE, not LEASH. The probe reaches the throw only by constructing the object directly with `newObject({ ..., owornmask: 1 })` and calling place_object() on it. causality refute: The range does introduce the atomic-refusal design, but the stated impact rests on a state neither C nor this port can produce, so it is a hypothetical future regression rather than a defect introduced or exposed here. rejections.summary: js/timeout.js:273 timerFireEnv() overwrites a caller-supplied hooks.newsym with the flat env.newsym, so the seam shape js/dig.js documents is silently discarded and run_timers() dies with a TypeError claiming the seam is missing.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: Anchored to changed code but the stated impact is not material: no caller can reach it and nothing fails closed differently. Counter-evidence: `grep -rn 'run_timers(\|nh_timeout_elapsed_turn(\|preflight_nh_timeout_elapsed_turn(' js/` returns exactly three live call sites -- js/allmain.js:734 `{ message, statusRefresh, newsym }`, js/allmain.js:1023 `{ newsym }`, js/do.js:1261 `{ newsym }` -- all flat, and none passes a `hooks` key at all, so the spread `{ ...env.hooks, ... }` never has anything to clobber. rejections.summary: js/timeout.js:290 The comment that justifies walking the due prefix ahead of the drain attributes element-object distinctness to start_timer()'s duplicate check, which does not provide it; the real guarantee is the `timed === 1` gate 18 lines below.

Counter-evidence: The comment scopes its claim to *admitted* elements. js/timeout.js:302-303 returns a refusal for any row without `f`, and js/timeout.js:255-263's table gives `f` to exactly one row, `rot_corpse`. Every admitted element is therefore a (TIMER_OBJECT, ROT_CORPSE) timer. nethack-c/upstream/src/timeout.c:2258-2263 rejects a new timer when an existing one matches kind, func_index and arg pointer together, and js/timeout.js:459-466 ports that check unchanged (`timer.kind === kind && timer.func_index === funcIndex && timer.arg === arg`). Two admitted elements therefore cannot name the same object, exactly as the comment says. The finding's own counterexample -- ROT_CORPSE plus REVIVE_MON on one corpse -- produces two elements of which only one is ever admitted, so it does not exhibit two admitted elements naming one object. The `timed === 1` gate at js/timeout.js:309 guards a different hazard (a second, unadmitted timer leaving `timed` nonzero after the drain's decrement, so remove_object() reaches obj_timer_checks()), which the comment above it states separately. causality refute: No defect is introduced or exposed: the changed comment states a true invariant with a true justification. Counte

Three of the eight confirmed findings are one defect. preflight_moverock() carries every arm of moverock_core() the slice left unported, and it lived only in cmd.c executeMovement()'s admission seam, which runs once per keystroke. On those steps the port pushed a boulder onto solid stone, into water, onto a trap or through a closed door, printed the push line, spent an rn2(19) C never draws, advanced the hero and called block_point() on the wrong square, where hack.c cannot_push() prints "You try to move the boulder, but in vain." and returns -1 with no time and no randomness spent. Before this range the unconditional throw at requireSimpleHeroDestination() fail-closed that path, so the range converted a named stop into a silent divergence, which is the failure AGENTS.md ranks worst. The adjudicator reproduced it rather than arguing it: replaying the range's own seed-110 geometry with a wall behind the boulder pushed it onto STONE and added the draw. test_move()'s DO_MOVE arm now asks the questions immediately before moverock(), which covers every entry and still lands ahead of nomul(0) and the next_boulder bookkeeping, and the seam keeps asking so a keystroke refuses before set_move_cmd() commits movement intent.

Two comments claimed more than the code does. preflight_moverock()'s header said three refusals are wider than their C branch; the Blind arm is a fourth, because C refuses only a boulder the hero has not already felt and pushes one he has, and nothing recorded that, so a later port of glyph_at() would have lifted the refusal without restoring C's glyph_to_obj() guard. And js/obj.js called C's second-boulder guard redundant: the rebuild does reach C's blocked answer, but it also raises vision_full_recalc, which js/allmain.js spends on an extra vision_recalc(0), so a stacked boulder makes a call C skips.

Three test oracles were weak and one of them was load-bearing. The throttle test asserted only that nothing printed, leaving unpinned the invariant the throttle exists to protect: that a silent push still draws exercise()'s rn2(19). Gating that draw on the message is the most natural misreading of dopush(), whose C body nests both under one `if (!u.usteed)`, and it was invisible to the whole unit suite. The rush test's "spends no time" half was asserted with Math.trunc(game.moves), an expression domove() cannot change, so its headline claim had no oracle; it reads the hero's movement ration now. And the second boulders added to cmd.test.mjs and hero-bear-trap.test.mjs were inert -- what refuses those fixtures is the wall they already stand in front of, moverock_core():432, not :435's second-boulder term -- and removing them leaves both suites green with the same refusal, which is the evidence they proved nothing.

Four findings were rejected with counter-evidence. The development score is unchanged across every fix: 10 of 33 sessions, 1,833 screens, 127,829 random-number values and 1,852 cursors before and after, and scripts/run-hero-boulder-push.mjs still matches C. Its seed-110 row pushes the boulder mid-run, so the new guard is exercised by a recording rather than by unit tests alone. Optional finders: concurrency was enabled, because the once-per-turn planning clone shares the live game's level cells and the last two closing passes each found a leak of that class; it returned no confirmed finding here. Performance was not enabled, because the range adds one bounded loop over the boulders of a single square. A clarity pass was not run: the pass's own comment findings were applied here.
