checklist.reason: One game system, 382 changed production lines against the 500-line threshold, and one agent session; AGENTS.md requires no checklist at that size.

evidence:
Counts: 15 raw, 13 deduplicated, 11 confirmed, 11 applied, 0 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 9 survivors of 43 mutants. Counts: 15 raw, 13 deduplicated, 11 confirmed, 11 applied, 0 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 34 of 43 killed over the window with 9 declared survivors, all confirmed, and no mutants at all over the audit-fix delta. The goal's closing pass, run because the goal closes rather than because a threshold forced it; the gate read WATCH at 1 of 10 commits and 382 of 1,000 lines. Every confirmed finding is a comment or a test: no production logic changed, the development score is identical at 1,846 of 7,765 screens and 128,125 of 610,816 random-number values, and the suite is 4,255 tests passing. This is the first closing pass in four that found no production defect, and the first whose main result is about what mutation cannot see.

Four of the eleven are one defect from four angles, and it is the one worth reading. js/read.js seeds mondata.c name_to_monplus() with `gender: NEUTRAL`, as read.c:3141 does, and both the comment at js/read.js:176-178 and the test at scripts/wizard-genesis.test.mjs:236-241 justified the seed with a mechanism that does not exist: they said an unseeded call would answer -1 for a name whose only match is the neuter pmname. It would not. mondata.c:1078-1082 writes the matched gender through the pointer whenever any pmname matched, and js/mondata.js:836-839 mirrors it, so "gas spore" answers NEUTRAL under either seed. The adjudicator ran both forms over all 434 mons[] pmnames and the alternate-spelling table and found no difference, then deleted the seed and ran the suite: 4,254 tests, zero failures. The seed is observable only where no pmname matched and there is no gender to write, which is the title_to_mon() fallback at mondata.c:1074, whose own FIXME at 1073 says titles carry no gender, and the no-match case. Both comments now say that, and a new test asserts it on "Digger", the Archeologist rank title, which answers NEUTRAL seeded and -1 unseeded. The value is not cosmetic: read.c:3287-3288 turns MALE or FEMALE into a gender bit and makemon.c:1265-1268 then assigns the gender directly instead of spending rn2(2) on it, so a wrong gender shifts every draw after it.

That defect is also the clearest limit of the project's mutation evidence. The seed is an argument, not an operator, so mutate-sites generates no mutant for it at any kind; the slice's 43-mutant run and this pass's rerun both reported the line as covered, because both were measuring the operators around it. The gap was closed by a finder reading the code against mondata.c, not by a counter.

Two more findings were assertions that could not fail. The disposition-prefix test used "newt tame", which strstri() answers -1 for because the required trailing space is absent, so it held under `=== 0` and `>= 0` alike; the adjudicator confirmed by flipping js/read.js:158 and running the whole suite unchanged, and noted that mutate-sites does not generate `=== 0` to `>= 0` either, so the slice's run could not have caught it. "a tame newt" is the case that separates C's strncmpi() prefix test from a substring search, and it is now in the refusal table. The Escape test asserted only absences -- no message, no monster, no turn -- which a fail-closed boundary satisfies exactly as C's early return does, because js/jsmain.js swallows the boundary and returns the segment; the adjudicator changed js/read.js's ESC test to read bufp[1] and watched the whole suite stay green. That test now collects boundaries and asserts the list is empty.

iflags.debug_mongen's save-clear-restore had no oracle at all. Every existing run entered wiz_genesis() with the flag already false, so `assert.equal(game.iflags.debug_mongen, false)` was satisfied whether or not the restore ran, and the adjudicator confirmed by making js/wizcmds.js:80 assign false rather than mongen_saved and running the whole suite unchanged. The set state is reachable: js/optlist_data.js gives debug_mongen setwhere set_wiznofuz, which options.c:5211 rejects only while go.opt_initial is true, so a configuration file cannot set it but a wizard-mode options menu can. A new test sets the flag true and drives wiz_genesis() directly on the state the opening wait leaves behind, because a segment replay offers no point between its keys at which to set it.

Two comment corrections stand on their own. cant_revive()'s header said "both of C's callers read both halves"; C has four, at bones.c:156, trap.c:746, read.c:3262 and zap.c:982, and the two that pass a real from_obj are precisely what the port's refusal defers, so the undercount hid the refusal's future cost. And runtimeAppearanceMessage()'s new M_AP_MONSTER arm read as live behavior: set_mimic_sym() writes only M_AP_FURNITURE and M_AP_OBJECT, as makemon.c's does, and preflightCreation() refuses any runtime mimic that would print, so the line is written out because makemon.c:1483-1484 has it, not because a game can run it. The comment now says so and names both guards; flipping the line to `exclaim = false` leaves 4,255 tests passing and the development score unchanged, which is what it predicts.

The remaining findings are citation drift, reported independently by the readability and variable-trace finders. Fifteen C line references added by the range were wrong by one to nine lines, and three pointed at code meaning the opposite of the sentence around them: js/read.js said the covered arm "returns at 3231", which is the name_to_monclass() call the next sentence calls refused; the retry arms were cited as 3396-3405, which includes the ported return at 3405; and js/makemon_create.js cited 3307, a paragraph of commented-out alternatives, for the makemon() call at 3315. The variable-trace finder checked every citation the range added and reported which were right, so the drift is per-citation error rather than a uniform offset from another revision. All are corrected in the production files, in the tests and in QUALITY.json's deferral, and the function-range citations now run from each C function's return-type line to its closing brace.

Both rejections hold and both were rejected on materiality rather than on fact. The `fem: -1` initialiser is indeed never read, but js/read.js:185-188 already explains why at the site a maintainer would edit, and the proposed validation returns the same result in the fixed and the faulty state. wiz_genesis()'s restore is indeed skipped when create_particular() refuses, but js/jsmain.js ends the segment on that boundary and resets the game for the next one, so nothing reads the flag again; a try/finally would serve a control-flow path C has no analogue for.

Every new assertion was watched failing against the line it covers, by editing that line and putting it back: the title test against js/read.js's `gender: NEUTRAL`; the "a tame newt" row against `=== 0`; the debug_mongen test against both the restore and the clear, the second of which failed three tests; and the Escape boundary assertion against `bufp[0]`.

rejections.summary: js/read.js:120 `fem: -1` is the one request-struct default the port never reads, because js/read.js:190 overwrites it unconditionally, so both of its mutants are equivalent and no test can pin it, contradicting b11f36c's claim that the wave killed every default in the request struct.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: Refuted on materiality. The operative explanation the finding asks for is already in the file, four lines below the initialiser: js/read.js:185-188 states that C tests `d->fem == MALE || d->fem == FEMALE` here, that both gender words are refused above, that d->fem is still -1 at this point, and that only C's else arm has an owner, which is exactly why line 190 assigns unconditionally and therefore exactly why the -1 has no reader. A maintainer restoring read.c:3220-3228's guard reads that comment at the site they must edit. The remaining half of the complaint targets a sentence in b11f36c's already-published commit body, which is not code and cannot be corrected in place. resolution refute: The proposed comment restates what js/read.js:185-188 already says, so it resolves nothing that is not already resolved. The validation cannot distinguish fixed from faulty for the fix actually proposed: re-running mutate-sites still reports the same survivor after a comment is added, and `fem: 0` plus npm test passes both before and after, so both checks return the identical result in the fixed and the faulty state. The adjudicator's evidence lens accepted the mechanical core: every path that returns `d` passes through the unconditional `d.fem = named.gender;`, so the initialiser is written and never read.

rejections.summary: js/wizcmds.js:80 wiz_genesis()'s save-clear-restore of iflags.debug_mongen is not exception-safe, while its comment presents the restore as the point of the pattern; every refusal raised by create_particular(), the designed outcome for most typed answers, skips line 80 and leaves the flag clear.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: The skipped restore has no reader, in this segment or any later one, so the impact is not material, and the comment the finding calls a broken invariant makes no exception-safety claim. Counter-evidence: js/jsmain.js:598-620 catches UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError including the branch subclass, calls onBoundary and breaks the moveloop, so the segment ends on its last matching screen and nothing in the port reads iflags.debug_mongen again; js/makemon_create.js:2821 is its only reader and only runs under that loop. The next segment starts from js/jsmain.js:263 `const g = resetGame();`, and js/options.js seeds the field from optlist_data.js's initval false, so no leak crosses a segment. resolution refute: Both proposed fixes either add a branch nothing enters or pin behavior no consumer observes. A try/finally exists solely to serve a control-flow path C has no analogue for, since create_particular() always returns in C, and whose only successor in the port is the end of the segment; AGENTS.md, Complete common gameplay first item 3, forbids code with no owner in the running game. The suggested validation, catching the boundary error and asserting game.iflags.debug_mongen === true, asserts a post-boundary state that js/jsmain.js:598-620 immediately discards and js/jsmain.js:263 overwrites. The adjudicator's evidence lens accepted the mechanical trace: js/wizcmds.js:74-85 has no try/finally and js/cmd.js failClosedCommand() throws from inside the awaited call, so the restore is genuinely skipped.

mutation.finderConclusion: The window range ran 43 mutants of the three gating kinds and left 9 survivors, reproducing the slice's own figures exactly: js/cmd.js:2449's reset_cmd_vars() argument, js/makemon_create.js:657's M_AP_MONSTER override, js/read.js:117's multi test, :205, :246 and :269's three writes to a return value wiz_genesis() discards, both conjuncts of :228's gender guard, and js/wizcmds.js:78's clear. Those refusals are deliberately raised after getlin() has echoed the whole typed line, which is why js/cmd.js failClosedCommandRefusals() lists UnsupportedMonsterRequestError: leaving it out would discard every screen the prompt already matched rather than stopping on the last of them. Counts: 18 raw, 14 deduplicated, 11 confirmed, 10 applied, 1 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 93 of 106 killed over the window with 13 declared survivors, all confirmed, and 7 of 7 killed over the audit-fix delta. The first slice of hero-zaps-a-ray-wand, reviewed because the gate forced it rather than because the goal closes: npm run quality read DUE at 1,207 changed production lines against the 1,000 limit, on one commit. The development score is identical before and after the fixes at 1,861 of 7,765 screens and 128,006 of 610,816 random-number values, which is what two defects unreachable from any recorded session should look like.

Two production defects, both on the ray's own damage path and both shaped like a table rather than a branch.

Grease blocked fire. trap.c erode_obj() assigns check_grease per erosion type and clears it inside `case ERODE_BURN` at 208, as it does inside `case ERODE_ROT` at 217; the grease arm at 246 reads `check_grease && otmp->greased`, so C never greases a burn away. The port tested the caller's EF_GREASE flag alone, and this range made burnarmor()'s `burn_dmg(obj, descr) = erode_obj(obj, descr, ERODE_BURN, EF_GREASE)` the first live ERODE_BURN caller. A hero wearing a greased cloak would have drawn an rn2(2) C never draws and printed "Your cloak is protected by the layer of grease!" where C prints "Your cloak smoulders!". The adjudicator reproduced both answers from the ray matrix's own segment rather than arguing them. The EROSION table now carries check_grease as a third per-type output beside the vulnerability test and the resistance damage type.

The pre-existing oracle actively pinned the wrong answer: scripts/trap-erode-obj.test.mjs's 'grease blocks fire before material and erosion checks' asserted ER_GREASED and the grease message for exactly the ERODE_BURN combination C excludes. It now asserts what C does. A new test walks all five erosion types through the grease arm, and that is what pins the rest of the table: three of the five rows survived their own flip until it existed.

The second defect is four invented rows. zap.c adtyp_to_prop() (5656-5670) is five cases and a default, and the port added AD_DRST, AD_DRLI, AD_SLEE and AD_STON on top, so the ported pure function answered a resistance property where C answers 0. Nothing reachable passes those damage types, so no screen moved, but u_adtyp_resistance_obj() reads the answer to decide whether to roll at all, and the test asserted only rows C also has. The rows are gone and the test now names all five of C's and all four of the port's inventions.

Two comments claimed more than the code does, and both were settled by running the experiment rather than by reading. js/timeout.js justified a second copy of invent.c carrying() by a cycle "this file is written to avoid"; the file already sits inside that cycle through './dig.js' and './do.js', both of which import js/invent.js. Importing carrying() and deleting the copy leaves the suite green, so the copy is gone and the comment says what the display boundary is actually for. And the negate() helper's comment described a hazard that does not exist: -0 and 0 are indistinguishable to every branch on this path, including zapdir_to_glyph()'s own `dx ? 1 : 0`, so the helper keeps a delta identical to the int C holds and fixes no branch, which is now what it says.

Five oracles could not fail, and each was confirmed by an adjudicator running the mutation rather than reasoning about it. zapcolors[] had three of eight entries asserted while a hero's wand of sleep or lightning paints entries 3 and 5 onto a screen the scorer compares; all eight are now read from display.h's enum zap_colors, with entry 4 asserted through js/display.js recorderMapColor()'s documented folding of CLR_BLACK onto the terminal default. The invisible-monster-memory test asserted that squares with no memory showed none, which held whether or not unmap_invisible() ran; it now seeds a memory on the bolt's line and one off it. dobuzz()'s `zap_hit(Math.trunc(state.u.uac), 0, random)` argument had no oracle and survived `+ 5` against the whole suite; two runs differing only in u.uac now pin it, stopped at Reflecting so the hit does not run on into zhitu(). The miss arm -- "whizzes by you!" and the stop_occupation() tail below it -- had no cover in the unit tests or the five-segment differential. And inventory_resistance_check()'s rn2(100) bound was scripted past rather than recorded.

One confirmed finding is applied as a deferral rather than as a test, because its proposed fix does not work. dobuzz()'s `if (dx === 0 && dy === 0) range = 1;` is genuinely unpinned, and the mutation to 2 surviving the suite reproduces. The pass proposed counting nh_delay_output() frames for a forced-miss vertical bolt and asserting exactly one; under the mutant that bolt still draws one frame and still prints its miss message once, both measured. Writing an assertion that cannot fail is the mistake this pass exists to catch, so vertical-ray-range-one-is-unpinned records the measurement and the structural question behind it: in C the assignment stops a stationary bolt re-entering the hero-square block, and something else in the port's loop is already doing that, which is worth understanding before the line is called equivalent.

Three rejections hold, each refuted on a specific reading rather than on judgment. zap_over_floor()'s burn_floor_objects() call does carry the named refusal and the comment the finding said it lacked. save_bhitpos's reference-versus-copy shape rests on a C statement the finding quoted as present above line 1260, and only C's comment is there. And no reachable input produces a dobuzz type in 6 through 9, because weffects() reaches ubuzz() only over the six consecutive ray wands.

The mutation evidence is worth stating plainly, because it is the second consecutive pass whose main result is a value no mutant can reach. The window ran 106 mutants over a baseline of 3,807 tests, the largest run this project has made, and neither production defect is of a kind it could find: a missing table field and four extra switch cases are not operators. Five of the six test findings are the same shape.

Every new assertion was watched failing against the line it covers, by editing that line and putting it back: the ERODE_BURN grease test against the unconditional guard; the five-type test against each of ERODE_ROT, ERODE_CORRODE and ERODE_CRACK in turn; the adtyp_to_prop assertions against a restored AD_SLEE row; the zapcolors block against a wrong entry 3; the unmap_invisible test against a deleted call; the armor-class test against `u.uac + 5`; the miss test against a changed message; and the resistance bound against rn2(1000).

One measurement kept out of the finding list. Driving the hit path with a random source that answers 0 to every rn2 hangs, and C hangs the same way: trap.c burnarmor() is `while (1) { switch (rn2(5)) { case 0: ... continue; }`, so a source that always answers 0 never leaves the helmet arm. That is a degenerate script rather than a defect, and the tests avoid it.

rejections.summary: js/zap.js:1159 zap_over_floor()'s burn_floor_objects() call drops C's result test and the two statements it guards -- couldsee(), newsym() and the "You see a puff of smoke." message -- with no comment or named refusal.

Counter-evidence: js/zap.js:1159-1169 does not call burn_floor_objects() bare. It passes `unsupported: (reason) => { throw new UnsupportedZapError(\`burn_floor_objects() reached ${reason}\`); }` and carries the comment 'js/zap_destroy_items.js keeps the hero-caused half fail-closed, because useupf() charges a shopkeeper for what it burns.' js/zap_destroy_items.js:197-202 refuses on uCaused before touching any object, so the hero-caused path this range makes reachable stops by name rather than diverging silently, and the two statements C guards with the result cannot be reached without first passing that refusal.

rejections.summary: js/zap.js:1231 `save_bhitpos` binds a reference to the live `state.gb.bhitpos` object, so the save and restore pair at 1231 and 1378 is correct only because line 1260 replaces the object rather than mutating it, which is the opposite of the in-place convention three other ported writers of the same value use.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: The deviation is harmless as written and the stated impact is entirely counterfactual, resting on a future edit the finding calls obvious but which the file's own conventions do not support. Counter-evidence: three of the finding's supporting claims fail on inspection. The claimed C text is not quoted above line 1260, which carries only C's comment `/* hit() and miss() need gb.bhitpos to match the target */` rather than the assignment, so the premise that the port must match a quoted C statement is false; the competing in-place convention it cites does not hold across the writers it names; and no reachable caller observes the difference, because the restore at 1378 runs on every path out of dobuzz() that the port admits.

rejections.summary: scripts/zap-ray.test.mjs:737 The type-9 assertion in 'dobuzz admits a hero wand zap and nothing else' accepts any error whose message merely lacks the band-refusal phrase, so an outright crash on flash_types[]' empty row passes as success.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: The stated impact, the running game aborting a segment on an unnamed error instead of a named refusal, cannot occur, because no reachable input produces a dobuzz type in 6 through 9. Counter-evidence: js/zap.js weffects() reaches ubuzz() only through `Math.abs(otyp - WAN_MAGIC_MISSILE) % 10` over the six consecutive ray wands WAN_MAGIC_MISSILE through WAN_LIGHTNING, which yields types 0 through 5; every negative monster type and every type at or above 10 is stopped by dobuzz()'s own band guard at js/zap.js:1206-1210; and spell casting is refused earlier at weffects(). evidence:
Counts: 22 raw, 18 deduplicated, 14 confirmed, 13 applied, 1 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 8 survivors of 84 mutants. Counts: 22 raw, 18 deduplicated, 14 confirmed, 13 applied, 1 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 76 of 84 killed over the window with 8 declared survivors, all confirmed, and 5 of 5 killed over the audit-fix delta. The goal's closing pass, which the gate also forced at 1,079 changed production lines against the 1,000 limit. The development score is identical before and after the fixes at 1,879 of 7,765 screens and 133,468 of 610,816 random-number values.

Two production defects, and the first is one this pass's own orchestrator created. The previous slice wired zhitu():4436 to ignite_items(gi.invent), and the orchestrator folded into it a named class for js/apply_catch_lit.js's OBJ_INVENT refusal, which until then threw a bare RangeError that no fail-closed list carried. The naming was right and the placement was wrong: the refusal stood ahead of every guard apply.c catch_lit() evaluates first, so a hero carrying a brass lantern -- which obj.h:397's own comment says can be lit but not by fire -- ended the segment where C returns FALSE at 1583-1588 and does nothing at all. The same covered an empty magic lamp or candelabrum, a burnt-out candle, a cursed candelabrum, and a cursed lamp whose rn2(2) came up zero, whose draw the port never made. The adjudicator traced C's order rather than arguing it. OBJ_INVENT now falls through those guards and the refusal stands at 1598, where C's inventory-specific work begins.

The second is a dropped conjunct with a test that agreed with it. zap.c:4572 is `type < 0 || (type == 0 && gb.buzzer != 0)`, and the port wrote `type < 0 || gb.buzzer`. A hero's own magic missile is type 0, so the conjunct is the whole of what separates it from every other hero band; without it a set gb.buzzer would send a fire bolt to the monster killer arm. scripts/zap-ray.test.mjs pinned the port's reading as if it were C's, asserting a refusal at type 1 that C sends to "zapped by herself". Both are corrected, and the test now drives the pair that separates the terms: type 0 with a buzzer must refuse, type 1 with the same buzzer must answer the ordinary killer string.

That second defect is the pass's sharpest general lesson, and it is about the instruments rather than the code. A mutation run measures whether the tests notice a change; it cannot notice that the tests agree with the code against C. Every mutant of that disjunction died -- against an oracle that was itself wrong.

Four comments claimed more than the code does. The refusal-class header said all three new classes follow a killing blow, where the ignition one fires a guard earlier on a hit that need not be fatal. _statusHitPoints() named one omission from botl.c and silently dropped a second, the `Upolyd ? u.mh : u.uhp` selection, which a polyself port must add here and nowhere else. maybe_destroy_item() said gc.current_wand is not modelled, which the last slice made false, and the deferral that comment justified covers the one damage type where C's clear actually fires. And js/zap.js's ray header still said the killer-and-losehp() tail refuses, 280 lines above the doc comment that now says the opposite.

Seven oracles could not fail. Four of the five refusal classes this range registers could be deleted from failClosedCommandRefusals() with the whole suite green, which is the failure mode that costs a segment every screen it earned; each now has a membership assertion beside the site that raises it, and each was watched failing against its own deletion. losehp()'s death branch could have used ttyPline() instead of ttyUrgentPline() unnoticed, which would have removed the only path to UnsupportedUrgentMessageError. The Half_spell_damage test used only dam = 25, where (25 + 1) / 2 is 13 in JavaScript too, so Math.trunc() was never exercised; 24 is the smallest input that separates them. The k_format KILLED_BY_AN was asserted nowhere. And the Book of the Dead arm had no test at all, which turned up something no finding predicted: the arm prints only while the Book is unidentified, because objnam.c The() over a discovered one takes the proper-noun branch js/objnam.js refuses. Both halves are now pinned, the second by the named refusal.

One confirmed finding became a deferral, measured rather than argued. _statusVitals()'s clamp has no oracle: reverting that one call site to `u.uhp || 0` leaves all 4,329 tests green and the development score identical, because its two readers use only the string's length and a negative total is two characters longer, which cancels against thresholds that move in two-character steps. status-vitals-clamp-has-no-oracle records the measurement and what closing it needs. The clamp stays, because botl.c applies it before every use and the other two renderers are pinned by both witnesses.

One confirmed finding was applied and then withdrawn, which is worth recording because the withdrawal is the correct outcome rather than a retreat. It asked for WIN_NOSTOP's second reader, topl.c more():233, to be modelled with a flag threaded through ttyUrgentPline(). That was written, and then the assertion added for it passed with the change removed: ttyPlineCore()'s existing deathComparisonReached clear already does the same work, and "You die..." is urgent_pline()'s only caller, so the two rules answer identically for every reachable input. Keeping the flag would have been production code with no owner, which AGENTS.md forbids. The comment now names both readers and says which mechanism models the second, and the test pins that mechanism: breaking the clear fails it.

Four rejections hold, each refuted on a specific reading. The bare Error for C's own impossible() is a programming-error report rather than an unported path. state.current_wand's placement departs from no convention the files that carry gc values actually share. Its plumbing is untested only to a reader no reachable input distinguishes, and the branch it feeds is pinned directly. And the clear it omits on a refusal is unobservable, because the refusal ends the segment and js/jsmain.js resets the game before the next one.

Every new assertion was watched failing against the line it covers: the ignition guards against the old refusal placement; the killer guard against the dropped conjunct; each of the three refusal classes against its own deletion from the list; the urgent-pline test against ttyPline(); the halving against a removed Math.trunc(); the killer format against a changed constant; the Book's blind selector against a forced true; and the WIN_NOSTOP test against a disabled deathComparisonReached clear.

productionDefects.summary: js/apply_catch_lit.js catch_item_light() raised its OBJ_INVENT refusal ahead of every guard apply.c catch_lit() evaluates first, so a hero carrying a brass lantern -- which obj.h:397's own comment says can be lit but not by fire -- ended the segment where C returns FALSE at 1583-1588 and does nothing at all. The same covered an empty magic lamp or candelabrum, a burnt-out candle, a cursed candelabrum, and a cursed lamp whose rn2(2) came up zero, whose draw the port never made. OBJ_INVENT now falls through those guards in C's order and the refusal stands where C's inventory-specific work begins at 1598. The exposure was created by the previous slice, which wired zhitu():4436 to ignite_items(gi.invent), and by the orchestrator's own decision to fold the naming of that class into it.

js/zap.js zhituLosehpArguments() dropped C's `type == 0 &&` conjunct from zap.c:4572's `type < 0 || (type == 0 && gb.buzzer != 0)`, so a set gb.buzzer would have sent every hero band to the monster killer arm rather than magic missile alone. scripts/zap-ray.test.mjs pinned the port's reading as if it were C's, asserting a refusal at type 1 that C sends to the ordinary "zapped by herself" arm. The conjunct is restored and the test now uses the pair that separates the two terms.

deferrals.summary: Of the three status renderers the checklist says now read _statusHitPoints(), only two are covered: reverting _statusVitals() to the unclamped `u.uhp || 0` leaves the whole suite green.

rejections.summary: js/zap_destroy_items.js:442 destroy_items() raises a bare Error for C's impossible("destroy_item: items in multiple chains"), in a file where every other unported or should-not-happen path raises the named UnsupportedItemDestructionError.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: C's own impossible() is a programming-error report rather than an unported path, and the port's bare Error is the shape this repository uses for that class throughout. Counter-evidence: the condition requires an object whose where field disagrees with the chain it was reached through, which no caller can build; the named class exists so a refusal ends the segment on its last matching screen, and a state that cannot arise needs no such conversion. Naming it would put an unreachable arm into failClosedCommandRefusals() and invite a reader to treat it as a stop the game can take.

rejections.summary: js/zap.js:336 C's gc.current_wand is stored at the bare path state.current_wand, while the port's established home for the gc struct is state.gc.* and the same function three hundred lines below uses state.gb.bhitpos for gb.bhitpos.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The premise that state.gc.* is the port's established home does not hold across the files that carry gc values, several of which use the bare path, so there is no single convention the placement departs from. Counter-evidence: the value has exactly one writer and one reader, both added by this range and both in js/zap.js, so no other module has to agree on where it lives; and the gb.bhitpos comparison is not parallel, because that value is read by js/trap_erode_obj.js across a module boundary, which is what put it on the struct.

rejections.summary: js/zap.js:337 The gc.current_wand modelling this range adds to dozap() -- both the set before weffects() and the clear after it -- is pinned by no test; deleting all three lines leaves the suite green.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: The value's only reader is zhitu()'s verb selection, whose TOOL_CLASS arm needs a fire horn that music.c would have to reach, and no ported path reaches it. Counter-evidence: the range's own tests pin the verb selection directly over zhituLosehpArguments(), including the played/zapped pair, so the branch the value feeds is covered at the point it is read; what is untested is the plumbing to a reader no reachable input distinguishes, and a test asserting it would assert the port's own bookkeeping rather than any C behavior.

rejections.summary: js/zap.js:338 dozap() clears state.current_wand only on the normal return from weffects(); every refusal raised inside the ray leaves the wand recorded, where zap.c:2672-2675 always clears it.
rejections.counterEvidence: resolution refute: A refusal ends the segment, and js/jsmain.js resets the game before the next one, so no reachable state observes the stale value. Counter-evidence: the only reader is zhitu()'s verb selection inside the same weffects() call that would have to have already refused; the segment cannot continue past the refusal to reach a second zap, and the next segment starts from resetGame(). Wrapping the call in a try/finally would serve a control-flow path whose successor is the end of the segment, which AGENTS.md's 'Complete common gameplay first' rules out.

mutation.finderConclusion:
The window ran 84 mutants of the three gating kinds over a baseline of 1,439 tests in 53 files and left 8 survivors, three in js/display.js and five in js/zap_destroy_items.js, each carrying a stated reason in the commit body of 0aac3a7 or c7241af. The pass tested those claims and reported none of them wrong. The delta over the audit fixes ran 5 mutants and killed all 5.

What the runs could not see is both production defects and five of the seven test findings, which is the fourth consecutive pass where that holds. A refusal placed ahead of the guards C answers first is an ordering error, not an operator; a dropped `type == 0 &&` conjunct changes a disjunction the run does mutate, but the surviving oracle asserted the port's own reading, so every mutant of that line died against a test that was itself wrong. That second case is the sharper lesson: a mutation run measures whether the tests notice a change, and cannot notice that the tests agree with the code against C.

The deferral status-vitals-clamp-has-no-oracle records the same shape from the other side: js/display.js:3714 survived as an equivalent mutant, and the orchestrator then measured that removing the clamp entirely leaves all 4,329 tests green and the development score identical, because the value's readers use only its string length and the difference cancels against thresholds that move in two-character steps.

evidence:
Counts: 14 raw, 14 deduplicated, 11 confirmed, 10 applied, 1 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 2 survivors of 12 mutants. The goal's closing pass, over a deferred-area sweep whose forecast was zero and whose four slices each met it. The development score is identical before and after the fixes at 10 of 33 sessions, 1,879 of 7,765 screens and 133,468 of 610,816 random-number values, and the suite is 4,341 tests passing. Nothing here was expected to move a screen, and nothing did.

The sharpest finding is a coverage hole the sweep itself opened, and an adjudicator proved it by running the mutation rather than arguing it. The first slice moved the monster refusal out of bhit() and into throwit() and throw_gold(), deleted the assertion in scripts/bhit.test.mjs that had covered it, and put none at either new site. Changing `if (mon)` to `if (false)` at both js/dothrow.js:788 and :990 left all 4,340 tests green: with those guards gone, throwit() falls through to breaktest(), flooreffects(), place_object() and stackobj() and deposits the missile on the monster's square with no thitmonst() and no draws. The slice's whole deliverable was equally unpinned. Its deliverable is a name, not a screen -- throwit() must stop under thitmonst() and throw_gold() under ghitm() -- and both could be reverted to their pre-slice values with the suite still green, which is what the boundary census .agents/selection.md ranks goals with reads. Both are now pinned by segment replays of the two recipes QUALITY.json already records as expected failures, asserting each name and the absence of the other. The test was watched failing twice: once against the restored pre-slice names, once against both guards disabled.

The single production defect is the one the sweep's own consolidation slice was supposed to prevent. js/objnam.js obj_is_pname() kept half of objnam.c:337; the restored half is `!program_state.gameover`, and both halves skip the identification test because once the game is over the tombstone names an artifact whatever the hero learned about it. It is asserted on the function rather than through doname(), because js/objnam.js refuses end-of-game object text one frame above, so no ported naming path reaches it; that came out of writing the test the other way first and watching it stop on the refusal.

Three comments claimed more than the code does, all three about work this range did. throw_gold()'s header still said its ghitm() refusal is unreachable because bhit() stops for a monster -- the claim this range falsified. UnsupportedBhitError's census still said "nine branches" and that each stops before it changes anything; the range added a tenth, the shade, and that one fires only after uhitm.c:1575's dmgval() has rolled the damage dice. And hold_another_object()'s C reference and fail-closed scope sat as the header of a private helper while the function itself had none.

Four oracles could not fail, and each now has an assertion watched failing against its own line: the shade's obj argument, whose replacement by null removes the draws entirely; the y disjunct of the newly ported gn.notonhead write, whose test varied only x; the tmp_at(DISP_END) the THROWN_WEAPON arm adds; and the gameover half above.

One finding became a deferral, and it is the second time in this goal that an assertion which cannot fail was caught before it was committed. The pass reported the set_wear() await chain unpinned; the test written for it passed with the caller's await removed, so the claim was measured from the other side instead. That measurement is what startup-set-wear-await-has-no-observable records, and it is the third entry of that shape in two goals.

The score attribution is that there is none to make. Every slice in this goal was chosen from the deferred ledger rather than from a session that stops, the scan over the 33 development sessions found no objects refusal among the thirteen boundaries where sessions do stop, and the fixes touched no path a recorded session reaches. What the goal delivers instead is the census repair the first slice exists for, and the pass's own result is that the repair had no oracle until now.

rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: two of the three claims fail on a source read and the third is inert. Every noun in the comment refers to this port's flooreffects(): js/do.js:383-384 refuses `obj.otyp === BOULDER` unconditionally, and dropx() calls freeinv() before dropzAdmitted() reaches flooreffects(), so 'reads the object rather than the square' and 'sits past freeinv() in dropx()' are both true as written. The one accurate sub-claim, the glob arm, points at a branch the same function already refuses forty-five lines earlier, so trusting the two-item enumeration cannot admit an unpreflighted object. rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: the mechanical trace is right and the stated problem does not exist. The finding rests on 'no test can pin the number, order or bounds of the draws' and 'the one randomness-consuming path in bhit() that a unit test cannot steer'; both are false. js/rng.js:26-27 exports enableRngLog() and getRngLog(), and an adjudicator used them on the unmodified head worktree to pin the shade arm exactly, recording draws ["rnd(6)=4"] against [] for the same non-shade fixture, and the existing fixture already calls initRng(1) to make those draws deterministic. js/weapon.js:430 resolves `env.random ?? { d, rn2, rnd }` and bhit()'s own default at js/zap.js:620 is `{ rn2, rnd }`, the same module-level functions, so the two bind identically in production and the range introduces no divergence in draw count, order or value. The window ran 12 mutants of the three gating kinds over a baseline of 1,142 tests in 36 files and left 2 survivors, both at js/zap.js:728, the two boolean literals in the shade_miss() call. checklist.reason: One slice, one game system, 203 changed production lines: AGENTS.md triggers a checklist for work that continues across agent sessions, touches more than one game system, or approaches 500 changed lines of game code, and this crosses none of the three.

evidence:
Counts: 20 raw, 18 deduplicated, 16 confirmed, 15 applied, 1 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 36 mutants. The closing pass for hero-death-reaches-done, a fail-closed boundary port whose one slice delivered its capped forecast to the screen. The gate did not force this pass; the goal's close did, at 1 of 10 commits and 203 of 1,000 lines. The development score is identical before and after the fixes at 10 of 33 sessions, 1,949 of 7,765 screens and 133,468 of 610,816 random-number values, and the suite is 4,366 tests passing, both measured by the orchestrator at the fix head.

The sharpest finding is the one production defect, and it is the class AGENTS.md forbids outright rather than a divergence from C. done() refused the paranoid_confirmation path only where C asks the question, at end.c:1112, by which point the port had already run bot(), incremented u.umortality and forced u.uhp and u.mh to zero. A configuration the port cannot answer therefore lost its hero's state and then stopped. The refusal is now a preflight above the status paint, guarded by the same five terms that decide C's own 1105-1112 condition. This is a deliberate divergence from C's order of evaluation, taken because the port cannot complete the path and must stop before changing anything; for the supported path the preflight evaluates false and nothing moves.

I verified that independently rather than accept it. Moving the preflight back below the `if (how < PANICKED)` mutation block makes "ParanoidDie reads its bit before status or death-state changes" fail, along with the exclusion test beside it, and restoring it makes both pass.

The fix leaves one consequence and one precondition. The consequence is the deferral: the preflight rejects every raw flags.paranoid_confirmation value, including the reset forms that leave PARANOID_DIE clear and would reach the single-key prompt the port already draws, because js/options.js has not ported optfn_paranoid_confirmation() into flags.paranoia_bits and so cannot tell them apart. The precondition is that the call at 1112 now passes a literal false where C passes ParanoidDie, on the proof that every path reaching it evaluated the bit as false in the preflight and every path that skipped the evaluation refused above. A life-saving port would have to revise that proof, and the comment beside the call says so.

The remaining fourteen confirmed findings are eight test findings and six clarity findings, all applied. Two of the test findings are ordering claims with no mutable operator, pinned by new assertions and demonstrated by targeted break-and-restore.

Two rejections hold, each with its reopening condition recorded. done() was said to be able to repaint the live game from a planning clone, and losehp() is its only production caller on the live hero's turn while planned damage refuses in mdamageu() before reaching it. And the revised paranoid-query comment was said to omit cancellation by quit or Escape, which the adjacent comment already states.

Two limits on this pass, both stated rather than resolved. The reviewer could not rerun the fresh differentials, because the C recorder is absent from the frozen worktree, so the live-path evidence is the slice's own strict-parity run rather than a rerun under the fixes; the orchestrator's checkpoint at the fix head is what shows the fixes moved no screen. And the reviewer recorded a pass entry in its own worktree against a commit that exists only there. That record was not imported. This entry is written against the repository's own history, with the range extended through the audit-fix commit so that commit carries no debt of its own.

The score attribution is that the fixes moved nothing, and should not have. Every one lands on a configuration no development session sets: no recorded rc carries paranoid_confirmation, and the goal's own 70 screens came from the slice rather than from this pass.

The refusal is now a preflight above the status paint, guarded by the same five terms that decide C's 1105-1112 condition, so a configuration the port cannot answer stops before it changes anything. The orchestrator verified it independently: moving the preflight back below the `if (how < PANICKED)` mutation block makes the ordering test and the exclusion test beside it fail, and restoring it makes both pass.

The same preflight rejects every raw flags.paranoid_confirmation value, including the reset forms !paranoid_confirmation, paranoid_confirmation:none and paranoid_confirmation:pray, which leave PARANOID_DIE clear and would reach the single-key prompt the port already draws. js/options.js applyOption() has not ported options.c optfn_paranoid_confirmation() into flags.paranoia_bits, so the port cannot tell those values apart from one that sets the bit. mutation.finderConclusion:
Every mutant died: 29 over the reviewed range and 7 over the audit-fix commit, with no survivor and none needing a stated reason. That is the cleanest run this project has recorded, and it is also the run that says least about the pass's own result.

The production defect has no operator to mutate. A refusal raised in the wrong place is an ordering error: the same statements run, in a different sequence, and no boolean, logical or relational operator changes between the two versions. The pass reported it from a source read, and the orchestrator confirmed it by moving the preflight back below the mutation block and watching two tests fail. Nothing in either mutation run distinguishes the two orderings.

That is the sixth consecutive closing pass whose sharpest finding sits outside what scripts/mutate-sites.mjs can reach, and the third distinct shape after a transcribed table and a missing switch case: an ordering, a pass-through argument, a table constant. The slice's own commit added a seventh instance from the other side, an await whose absence changes no operator. .agents/proposals.md carries the entry this pattern produced; the evidence for it now spans three goals.

Stubs and stops identified: the TRICKED head, fuzzer_savelife(), the life-saving amulet body, savelife() for a declined death, and really_done() (1130-1590). The pass then found what the trace had not, which is that one of those stops was raised after the state it was protecting had already changed.

readiness.boundary: The reviewed boundaries span bones creation (savebones, getbones, resetobjs, drop_upon_death), game termination (really_done tail with tombstone and farewell text), and polyself transformation (#polyself controlled-input through polymon for PM_GNOME, dropp hooks, weight_cap Upolyd adjustment, and status-line Upolyd selection).

readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the completed boundaries. Excluded branches stop before changing state, consuming randomness, or producing output.
